title: Walk every authored book step in CI
body:
## Summary

Adds a full-book walk that runs every authored step of every book against the built learner binary, and fixes the CLI problems it turned up.

**New harness**
- `scripts/walk-books.ts` (`bun run test:books`) walks each book's steps with the compiled binary and smoke-tests graphical launches under Xvfb. It writes `test-results/book-walk/report.json`.
- New reusable workflow `.github/workflows/book-walk.yml`. It installs JDK 21, Maven, Python with pygame-ce/Pillow, the JUnit console jar, and Xvfb/xdotool. CI runs it, and `release` now needs it to pass.
- The Docker `test` image gets the same GUI runtimes (`libgtk-3-0`, `xauth`, `xdotool`, `xvfb`).

**CLI fixes**
- `run`: when a project checkpoint moves on, generated files from the earlier checkpoint that are no longer wanted are removed if unchanged. If the learner edited one, the run stops with `checkpoint_conflict` and leaves the file alone. Files removed by `clean` targets now also drop their ownership record.
- `GeneratedFileStore` gains `recordsUnder(root)` and `forget(path)`.
- `replay execute` now returns `command`, `timedOut`, `stdout` and `stderr` for commands that don't match the expected result. It also adds a `--relax-output` flag that skips the exact stdout/stderr comparison. The flag only works when `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK=1` is set, so only the harness can use it.
- Native learn now shows the program's failure output instead of only "did not run cleanly".
- Book content: the Chapter 6 thermostat step now cleans up `ThermostatApp.java`.

**Housekeeping**
- `@aifirst/content` is pinned to commit `57ef4bc` (pack 2.0.1) and the embedded content is regenerated. Version bumped to 0.13.2.

## Testing
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json`: passes.
- `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`: content in sync (pack 2.0.1).
- `bun test`: 558 pass, 37 skip, 4 fail in the full run.
  - These 3 also fail on `main` in this environment, so this branch doesn't cause them:
    - `dependencies` › builds native Maven installation plans
    - `run` › book scoping › never hands a Python reader a Java exercise (5s timeout)
    - `tui-learn` › opens progress and command reference as dismissible Home screens
  - The remaining full-run failures were 5s timeouts that changed between runs. Each of those files passed when run on its own.
- The full book walk (`xvfb-run bun scripts/walk-books.ts`) was **not** run locally. It needs the CI runtime set, and the new `book-walk` job will run it.

title: Walk every authored book step in order and reconcile generated project files
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A reader reported that exercise java-6-05 stopped at "The program did not run cleanly". The plan keeps the isolated verifier, which proves each sample works alone, and adds an ordered pass to catch state left by earlier exercises. This PR adds a harness that runs every sample in both books in order, as the request put it, and fixes what that walk turned up.

`scripts/walk-books.ts` drives the compiled CLI through the authored steps of both books in order, using one persistent workspace per book, and writes a JSON report; it accepts `--binary`, `--report`, `--book`, `--from`, `--skip-smoke` and `--keep-workspace`, sets the exit code to 1 when any step fails, and runs graphical window smoke tests unless `--skip-smoke` is given. Graphical projects are checked through headless replay, plus Xvfb window launches for two representative apps, `py-9-01` (closed with Escape) and `java-11-01` (stopped once its window title appears, since Xvfb has no window manager), as chosen during planning. A reusable `book-walk.yml` workflow installs the book runtimes, runs the full walk and uploads the report; CI calls it on pull requests and main pushes, and the release job now needs it.

Shared projects are cleaned by automatic checkpointing. `prepareExerciseFiles` now treats a recorded generated file that the next scaffold does not want, and that `GeneratedFileStore` still matches, as obsolete. A recorded file the next scaffold drops that the learner has changed aborts with `checkpoint_conflict` and is left alone. The new `recordsUnder` skips malformed records and records whose path falls outside the given project root, and returns an empty list when the record directory cannot be read.

Other fixes from the walk:
- `replay` gains `--relax-output`, which is refused as `bad_option` unless `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK=1` is set; the harness uses it for externally launched steps so their captured output is compared loosely, and replay results now carry `timedOut`.
- The portable shell's `rm` handling now matches a single double-quoted, single-quoted or bare argument and normalizes backslashes in it.
- Previously `renderToolResult` built the error card inline; error tool results and unclean program launches now share `renderExecutionFailure`, which shows the command detail and falls back to a placeholder when the detail is empty; the native-learn test covers command details on a reader-controlled launch failure.
- The Java Thermostat checkpoint now lists `src/main/java/ThermostatApp.java` to clean. `.gitignore` ignores `/test-results/book-walk/` and the Dockerfile installs packages with `--no-install-recommends`. Housekeeping: the CLI goes to 0.13.2, `@aifirst/content` is pinned to a commit instead of the v2.0.0 tag, the embedded pack version moves from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1 and `bun.lock` is regenerated.

The process-stopping code in the harness and the path check in `generatedFiles.ts` have Windows-specific branches; the recorded runs were on linux/x64, so none shows the Windows path running. The new workflows have not run in CI in the session logs, and CI results for the pushed head are not there either.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content and, on separate lines, the checks recorded in the session logs while the change was made.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`.
- `bun test`: failed (554 pass, 8 fail, Ran 599 tests across 63 files. [535.07s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.
- `bun scripts/walk-books.ts --binary bin/aifirst-linux-x64 --report test-results/book-walk/report.json`: passed (PASS book walk: 163/163 steps, 2/2 graphical smokes. Report: <local path>) in the session logs. An earlier run of `npx -y bun@1.4.0 test test/generated-files.test.ts test/run.test.ts test/native-learn.test.ts test/replay-flow.test.ts …` failed (69 pass, 1 fail).

Where to start: `prepareExerciseFiles` in `src/commands/run.ts`, which decides which recorded generated files are obsolete.

Feedback wanted: should `prepareExerciseFiles` remove an obsolete generated file that a reader deliberately kept from an earlier exercise, or ask first?

A learner on Bazzite (a Fedora immutable Linux) could not get the Duckling to install its dependencies, because pip had only the pygame 2.6.1 source tarball and the system lacked `sdl2-config` and the `freetype2` package. title: fix: use Homebrew for Maven on immutable Linux
body:
## Summary
On rpm-ostree systems (Bazzite, Fedora Silverblue/Kinoite, etc.) `dnf` is present but can't install packages into the immutable base image. Because of that, the Maven auto-install for the Java book picked `dnf` and failed.

- Adds `isImmutableLinux()`. It detects `/run/ostree-booted` or an `rpm-ostree` binary on Linux.
- `systemDependencyInstallPlan` now checks for immutable Linux **before** the apt/dnf branches:
  - If `brew` is on PATH, it runs `brew install maven` (labelled "Homebrew (immutable Linux)").
  - If not, it returns no plan, so `dnf` is never tried.
- When there's no plan and only `mvn` is missing on an immutable host, the user now sees a specific message telling them to install Homebrew and retry.
- Docs: adds the rpm-ostree case to step 18 of `docs/learn-verification.md`.
- Bumps the version to 0.10.3.

A follow-up commit makes the existing "native Maven installation plans" test hermetic. Before, it used the real `existsSync` probe and failed when run *on* an ostree host. The same commit restores the doc list's continuation indent.

## Testing
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json` passes.
- `bun test test/dependencies.test.ts`: 11/11 pass on an rpm-ostree host. New tests cover marker/binary detection, the Homebrew plan ahead of dnf, and no fallback to dnf when brew is missing.
- `bun run check` (full suite): 514 pass, 36 skip, 4 fail, 3 errors.
  - All 4 failures are 5 s timeouts in CLI subprocess tests (`test/run.test.ts`, `test/bare-mode-learning-ux.test.ts`). The 3 errors appear in the same log, e.g. a JSON parse error in `test/run.test.ts`; I only looked into the timeouts.
  - Rerunning those two files on `main` also gives 2 timeouts, and which tests time out changes between runs. They look like timing flakes in this environment, not something this change caused.
- Not done here: manual install on a real Bazzite/Silverblue machine and the Docker replay from step 18.

title: fix: use Homebrew for Maven on immutable Linux
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
On Bazzite, the Maven install before `java-11-01` was rejected because Fedora Atomic images use rpm-ostree rather than `dnf`, so this PR's purpose is to detect an immutable distribution and install Maven through Homebrew instead.

Previously, on Linux `systemDependencyInstallPlan` checked APT, then DNF, then Alpine apk (each needing an elevation prefix), so an rpm-ostree system with `dnf` on PATH got a `dnf install -y maven` plan.

## Design

A new `isImmutableLinux` helper returns true on Linux when `/run/ostree-booted` exists or `rpm-ostree` is on PATH. `systemDependencyInstallPlan` now takes an injectable `exists` check and, after the Windows branch and before the APT/DNF/apk branches, asks `isImmutableLinux`. When it is true and `brew` resolves, the plan is `brew install maven` using the resolved path, labelled "Homebrew (immutable Linux)" and run without a sudo or other elevation prefix; when `brew` is missing, it returns no plan rather than falling through to `dnf`.

With no plan, `installDependencies` reports failure as before; when all missing dependencies are the `mvn` system command and the host is immutable Linux, the message tells the learner to install Homebrew, put `brew` on PATH and retry, instead of the generic `Install <packages> and retry.` text; this branch calls `isImmutableLinux()` with real host probes, and the added tests do not exercise it.

## Consequences

macOS and mutable Linux distributions keep their existing plans, since the new branch is guarded by the Linux platform check and the ostree markers. Tests cover both detection markers, the non-Linux case, the Homebrew plan on an rpm-ostree host that also has `dnf`, and the no-Homebrew case returning no plan; they inject fake `which` and `exists` functions rather than probing a real ostree system. Step 18 of the manual verification checklist now also covers rpm-ostree systems such as Bazzite or Fedora Silverblue. The package version moves from 0.10.2 to 0.10.3.

One known gap: the pre-existing APT assertion in `test/dependencies.test.ts` calls `systemDependencyInstallPlan` without an `exists` argument, so it reads the host's real `/run/ostree-booted`; it should pass `() => false`.

CI results for the pushed head were not available when this was written.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`.
- `bun test`: failed (512 pass, 6 fail, Ran 554 tests across 59 files. [487.02s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.

Where to start: `installDependencies` in `src/dependencies.ts`, which owns the immutable-Linux Maven failure message and calls `systemDependencyInstallPlan`.

Feedback wanted: should detection also treat other immutable families (for example NixOS or openSUSE MicroOS) as Homebrew-first, or is the ostree check the right scope for now?

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
## Summary

The Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` replay hook and the skill's commands called bare `aifirst`, so they relied on Claude Code's inherited `PATH`. On Windows, a Windows Terminal, VS Code, or Claude Code process that was already running keeps the `PATH` it had before the PowerShell installer ran. In that case the hook and the allowlisted commands fail.

This PR routes every Claude integration through a launcher that is written next to the skill.

- **Launcher**: `aifirst skill install --claude` now writes `~/.claude/skills/aifirst/aifirst-cli.sh`, which `exec`s the absolute path of the running binary. During source development it keeps the Bun entrypoint too. On Windows, paths are converted to Git Bash form (`C:\…` → `/c/…`) and every argument is shell-quoted.
- **Hook**: the replay hook command becomes `bash '<launcher>' replay hook # aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1`. Hooks are found either by the old bare command or by the marker, so a skill refresh replaces the old hook in place.
- **Skill and slash-command content**: `skillMarkdown()` / `commandFiles()` take the CLI command and render it everywhere the text used to say `aifirst`.
- **Permissions**: `claudeEntries(command)` builds entries for the launcher command. `grantPermissions` replaces legacy `Bash(aifirst …:*)` entries instead of adding new ones next to them. `revokePermissions` removes both forms. Book mode's pre-approval check uses the new entries.
- **Docs**: `docs/integrations/replay.md` explains the launcher, how existing installs migrate, and the direct-path fallback for PowerShell.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc -p tsconfig.json`: passes
- [x] `bun test test/agents.test.ts test/permissions.test.ts test/upgrade.test.ts`: 69 pass. New tests cover `bashPath`, quoting, launcher generation, hook migration, and replacing legacy permissions.
- [ ] Full `bun test`: 444 pass, 37 skip, **1 fail**. The failure is `test/run.test.ts › book scoping › never hands a Python reader a Java exercise`, which hits the 5 s default timeout. It **also fails on `main`** in this environment, and on this branch it passes with `--timeout 30000` (about 6 s). It's a timing problem that already existed and isn't caused by this change.
- [ ] Not tested by hand on native Windows (no Windows machine was available here).

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
On Windows, Claude Code's `UserPromptSubmit` hook and its `aifirst` Bash calls could report "aifirst: command not found", after which Claude suggested the macOS/Linux `install.sh`. This PR stops the Claude Code integration from looking up `aifirst` on the inherited `PATH` (the generated commands still start with `bash`), by installing a stable Claude-owned Bash launcher that delegates to the current `aifirst` executable and using it in hooks, generated instructions and permission rules.

Previously the hook was the bare `aifirst replay hook` and permission entries were `Bash(aifirst <cmd>:*)`, so a terminal, VS Code or Claude Code process that started before the installer ran could not find it.

**Design.** `install` now writes `aifirst-cli.sh` into the Claude skill folder alongside `SKILL.md`; the script `exec`s the absolute path of the executable that ran `install`, so a moved binary needs the skill reinstalled. The hook becomes `bash '<launcher>' replay hook # aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1`. On `win32`, `bashPath` converts drive paths such as `C:\...` to the Git Bash form `/c/...`; on other platforms it just normalizes slashes. `currentCliArgv` keeps the Bun entrypoint when the runtime is `bun` running `src/index.*` and otherwise uses just the executable. Arguments are single-quoted so spaces and apostrophes don't allow shell expansion. The skill markdown and command files render their executable instructions through this launcher command, and the missing-CLI guidance now sends native Windows to the PowerShell installer instead of `install.sh`. `claudeEntries`, `skillMarkdown` and `commandFiles` still default to bare `aifirst` when called without a command.

**Migration.** As decided for existing Windows installs, refreshing the skill migrates them. The hook now carries a marker comment; a hook is recognized as ours if it equals the legacy `aifirst replay hook` command or ends with that marker, so the old entry is replaced. Granting permissions removes legacy bare-command entries, adds the launcher-based ones and leaves unrelated entries alone; settings are left untouched when the list is already up to date, and the result note reports how many legacy entries were replaced. Permission state checks and book mode pre-approval now look for the launcher-based entries, and revoking removes both legacy and new ones. The docs explain the launcher, the `aifirst skill install --claude` refresh (with a fallback that runs `aifirst.exe` from `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\aifirst` when PowerShell can't resolve `aifirst`), and that native Windows uses the PowerShell installer.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`: passed, run on the submitted content.
- `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`: failed, run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.
- `bun test`: failed (444 pass, 1 fail, Ran 482 tests across 47 files. [369.82s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.

**Where to start:** `install` in `src/agents/claude.ts`, which writes the launcher and renders the skill with the launcher command.

**Feedback wanted:** Is recognizing our hook by its trailing marker comment robust enough against users editing `settings.json` by hand?

title: fix: launch JavaFX projects with Maven

## Summary

Maven-based JavaFX exercises (e.g. `java-11-01`, Pocket CFO) were launched with the plain `java` single-file/classpath launcher, which can't resolve JavaFX modules. This PR runs them through the project's configured plugin instead.

- New `src/projects.ts` → `mavenJavaFxCommand(step)`: returns `["mvn", "javafx:run"]` when a Java step's scaffold `pom.xml` declares `javafx-maven-plugin`.
- `aifirst run` (`commandsFor`) and `aifirst next` use that command ahead of the `java` launcher fallbacks.
- `opensExternalWindow` treats these steps as external-window programs, so the learn UI stays active while the JavaFX window is open (same path as pygame).
- `docs/learn-verification.md`: adds a manual check for the `java-11-01` final run, renumbers the following items, and fixes list indentation.
- Bumps version to 0.10.4.

## Tests

- `test/graphical-run.test.ts`: `java-11-01` resolves to `mvn javafx:run` in `commandsFor` and counts as an external window.
- `test/run.test.ts`: end-to-end `aifirst run java-11-01` against a stub `mvn` on `PATH`; checks the reported command and the arguments the stub received. Skipped on Windows, where the shell stub can't run.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck` passes.
- `bun test test/graphical-run.test.ts test/run.test.ts`: the new tests pass. One test fails: `book scoping > never hands a Python reader a Java exercise`, which hits the 5s timeout. It fails the same way on `main` in this environment, so this branch didn't cause it.

title: Launch Maven JavaFX projects with mvn javafx:run
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A learner reported that the final launch of the Chapter 11 JavaFX budgeting app was not working, even though that project is meant to be started with `mvn javafx:run`. This PR makes the CLI launch those projects the way they are authored, through Maven.

Previously, a Java step was launched with the single-file `java` launcher, or `java -cp out <Main>` when the scaffold contained extra `.java` sources, regardless of whether the project was a Maven build.

The new `mavenJavaFxCommand` in `src/projects.ts` returns `["mvn", "javafx:run"]` when the step is a Java step and its scaffold `pom.xml` content contains the literal text `<artifactId>javafx-maven-plugin</artifactId>` (a substring match, not a POM parse); for any other step it returns `undefined`, so existing launchers are untouched. When it matches, `mvn` is run from `PATH` with no fallback to the `java` launcher, so Maven must be installed.

It is consulted in three places:

- `next` uses the Maven command as the run command when it applies, and otherwise keeps the previous Java launcher logic.
- `commandsFor` in `src/commands/run.ts` returns the Maven command when it applies, after the existing JUnit branch for test examples. `commandsFor` is now exported so tests can call it directly.
- `opensExternalWindow` in `src/learn/native.ts` treats Maven JavaFX steps as external-window programs, alongside the existing pygame case.

A new test loads the authored `java-11-01` step and checks that it is launched with Maven and flagged as an external-window program; the follow-up commit is titled "make JavaFX launch coverage portable". In `test/run.test.ts`, a shell test (skipped on Windows) puts a fake `mvn` on `PATH`, runs `java-11-01`, and asserts the only command run is `mvn javafx:run`. The learn verification checklist gains a step to confirm the final `java-11-01` launch, renumbering later steps, and the package version is bumped to 0.10.4.

CI results in the session logs belong to an earlier commit of this PR, not the final head.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content and, on separate lines, the checks recorded in the session logs while the change was made.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `npx --yes bun x tsc -p tsconfig.json`, `npx --yes bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`.
- `npx --yes bun test`: failed (517 pass, 3 fail, Ran 556 tests across 59 files. [431.16s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.
- `npx --yes bun test test/graphical-run.test.ts test/run.test.ts`: passed (28 pass, 0 fail) in the session logs.

Where to start: `mavenJavaFxCommand` in `src/projects.ts`, which owns detecting the JavaFX Maven plugin in `pom.xml` and choosing the `mvn javafx:run` launcher.

Feedback wanted: is a substring match on `<artifactId>javafx-maven-plugin</artifactId>` in `pom.xml` robust enough, or should detection parse the POM (for example, plugins declared in a parent POM)?

title: feat: improve learner replay experience
body:
## Summary
Improves the built-in learner and replay experience (version bump 0.10.4 → 0.10.5).

- **Home menu:** removes the "Browse books and exercises" and "Connect an AI assistant" entries. "View progress" and "Command reference" now open as full screens you close with Enter or Esc (`src/commands/home.ts`, `src/prompt.ts`).
- **TUI session / native learner:** adds a new terminal renderer and expands TUI session handling for streaming output and code previews (`src/tui/session.ts`, `src/learn/native.ts`, `src/learn/terminalRenderer.ts`).

title: Improve learner replay pacing, code previews and portable Windows replays
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes replayed lessons easier to follow at the keyboard and lets captured replays that use portable shell scripts run without an external bash, which is what Windows learners need.

**Pacing and readability in the learner views.** After a read-only exercise prompt finishes typing, the learner now has to press Enter before the replay continues, so the text isn't scrolled away mid-read; Esc at that gate backs out and Ctrl+C exits. The new `pauseForEnter` returns without waiting when the session isn't interactive, and treats an abort as dismissal while rethrowing other errors. The Home menu's progress and command-reference screens now clear the transcript and wait before returning Home; in the OpenTUI session that screen scrolls with up/k, down/j, PageUp and PageDown and returns on Enter or Esc. The menu also drops its Browse and Connect entries. In the native renderer, code blocks longer than 40 lines are collapsed with a more-lines hint, and the learner can expand them unless stdin isn't a TTY with raw mode. Replayed tool calls and status events are now rendered as their own blocks rather than folded into trailing text.

**Portable replay commands.** Captured operations can carry a `portableCommand`; when present, the executor uses it in place of the recorded command and substitutes the selected Python launcher for a `<python>` placeholder. In the async executor, `<shell>` scripts run through Bun's in-process shell; the synchronous path falls back to the recorded command. Operations gain a `timeoutMs` for spawned commands; previously a command with no exit status reported 127, and it now reports 124 when it timed out and 127 otherwise. An operation marked `expectedTimeout` counts as successful only if it actually timed out. For pygame steps, a graphical entrypoint launch is replaced with a `py_compile` check of the entrypoint. The `replay` command now awaits `executeReplayAsync` at each place it previously ran the synchronous executor.

**Consequences.** A new `windows-duckling-replay` CI job on `windows-latest` installs Python 3.12 with pygame-ce and Pillow and runs the Save the Duckling replay test in portable mode. The Windows path itself is not shown running on Windows yet, since the new job is CI-only. Keyboard handling in the native and terminal renderers is not shown with a person at the keyboard. New scripted TUI and native-learn drivers plus tests cover the Enter gate, code collapse, portable commands and the Windows replay timeline. The package version moves to 0.10.5.

## Validation

title: fix: defer macOS setup outside piped installer

## Summary
On macOS, `curl … | bash` followed by `aifirst init </dev/tty` hangs: Bun can't poll stdin reopened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495). Running the binary directly works, because it inherits the real `/dev/ttysNNN` device.

- `install/install.sh`: on Darwin, skip the inline `aifirst init` and tell the user to run `aifirst init` in a new terminal. Linux behavior stays the same.
- `install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh` + `install/fixtures/macos_installer_tty_driver.py`: macOS-only regression test. It runs the real installer through a pipe inside a PTY (a stub `curl` serves the built binary and checksum), then runs `aifirst init` directly. It checks two things: no prompt appears inside the piped installer, and the direct init accepts keyboard input.
- CI: the test runs on the macOS smoke job and in the release darwin verification, and shellcheck now also lints the new script.
- README: documents the temporary extra step on macOS.

## Testing
- `shellcheck --shell=sh install/install.sh install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh`: passes.
- `sh -n` on both scripts and `py_compile` on the driver: pass.

title: fix: defer macOS setup outside the piped installer
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A macOS user reported that the piped installer reaches "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" and then accepts no keyboard input, while running the installed command afterwards works fine. This PR applies the safe workaround until a durable Bun fix ships in a release, and adds the recommended macOS smoke test.

On macOS (`$OS = darwin`), unless `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` is set, the installer skips guided setup inside the pipe; it prints "On macOS, finish setup in a new terminal:" followed by `aifirst init` on its own line, while other systems keep the existing `/dev/tty` branch and its non-interactive fallback. The commit message says the hang comes from Bun being unable to poll stdin reopened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495), and the `install.sh` comment adds that a direct invocation inherits the real `/dev/ttysNNN` device and stays interactive. The README now says guided setup opens immediately on Linux and Windows, tells macOS users to open a new terminal and run `aifirst init`, and replaces "No second command and no AI tool are required" with "No AI tool is required".

To guard the workaround, `install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh` exits with status 2 on anything other than Darwin or without an executable binary argument; otherwise it runs the real `install.sh` download and checksum flow against a fake `curl` that serves the just-built binary. A Python driver, `macos_installer_tty_driver.py`, forks the child under a pseudo-terminal, waits for the "Set up 1 tool? [Y/n]" prompt from a direct `aifirst init`, answers `n`, and treats a missing prompt, a 45-second deadline, or a child that does not exit normally with status 0 as an error. The test also checks that the installer printed the macOS deferral line. In CI the build-and-smoke step runs the script when the runner reports `Darwin`, the release workflow runs it against each built darwin binary, and the shellcheck job now also lints the new script.

Consequences: macOS users get one extra manual step until the Bun fix lands, and on macOS the piped installer does not open the interactive prompt itself.

The recorded runs were on linux/x64, so none shows the macOS path of the installer or smoke test running. The workflow changes run in CI, and no run of them is in the session logs. Recorded checks ran without a terminal, so none shows the pseudo-terminal path with a person typing at the keyboard.

title: test: add real-Claude Showtail scenario E2E harness
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR adds end-to-end coverage for three kinds of Claude Code sessions (a multi-prompt build, a plan-mode run that overrides the defaults, and an auto-mode turn followed by plan mode and execution); the request was to drive Claude Code programmatically, save its terminal output, Showtail JSON, plans and code as inputs, generate book content from them, replay that through `aifirst learn`, and require the two sides to match exactly.

Following the established rocket example, `scripts/capture-claude-showtail-e2e.ts` (exposed as `bun run capture:claude-e2e`) captures each scenario (all three by default, or one via `--scenario`) through a PTY driver with Showtail hooks enabled, generates replayable content, replays it through a second driver, and writes the oracle files. The scenarios are `train-multiprompt`, `sandwich-custom-plan` and `habit-auto-plan`, defined in `scripts/lib/claude-e2e-scenarios.ts`. "Exact" here means canonical conversation events plus source checkpoints, not raw terminal bytes: the raw logs are kept for review, but PTY redraws, spinners and timestamps change from run to run, so the oracle in `scripts/lib/claude-e2e-oracle.ts` normalizes events before comparing (CRLF to LF, temp workspace paths to `.`, test timings masked).

When the target directory is non-empty, the capture script refuses to write it unless `--replace` is given; a subprocess with a non-zero exit aborts the capture unless the call allows failure; and when omitted, `--content-repo` defaults to `../aifirstcontent` and `--showtail-repo` to `../../Showtail` relative to the repo root. The capture copies Claude credentials from `AIFIRST_CLAUDE_AUTH_HOME` (or the home directory) into a scratch HOME, and when Showtail's output matches its known journal-entries gap, the capture accepts it and records `showtailVerifyKnownRawEventGap` in `capture.json`.

`test/claude-showtail-scenarios-e2e.test.ts` compares committed author and learn oracles when the sibling fixtures exist, and live replay requires `AIFIRST_CLAUDE_E2E=1` and a `claude` binary; otherwise it is skipped with a warning.

Previously, `respond` handled an exact workflow step itself, calling `beginPlanning` and `planningOutcomeReply` directly when there were no pre-plan segments. It now delegates to `selectedReplayReply`, which in that case prefixes any trailing pre-plan text to the planning reply, so a text-only preamble appears before the first plan question.

title: build: prepare releases for SignPath signing
body:
## Summary

Gets releases ready for Windows code signing through the SignPath Foundation. The SignPath application is **still pending**, so this PR does not submit any signing requests yet. It sets up the licensing, the policy, the build metadata and the artifact layout that SignPath needs.

### Licensing and policy
- Relicenses the project from MIT to **Apache-2.0**: adds `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`, and updates `package.json`.
- Adds `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md` and `TRADEMARKS.md`, adds `.github/CODEOWNERS`, and updates `README.md` to match.

### Builds
- New `scripts/build-config.ts` holds the target selection and the `bun build` arguments, so they can be unit-tested.
- Each OS family is built on its own native runner. `--all` has been removed. Windows targets now fail fast if you try to build them anywhere except Windows, because Bun only writes PE version resources on a Windows host.
- Windows executables get product name, company, description, copyright and a four-part version (`X.Y.Z.0`) taken from `package.json`.
- Bun is pinned with `.bun-version`, and every workflow uses it instead of `latest`.
- **`--bytecode` is dropped from compiled builds.** CLI startup may be somewhat slower. The comment in `src/index.ts` is updated to match.

### Release workflow
- `build-linux-windows` is split into `build-linux` (ubuntu) and `build-windows` (windows-latest).
- `build-windows` checks the PE metadata of every `aifirst-windows-*.exe`, smoke-tests the x64 and baseline binaries, and uploads them as `binaries-windows-unsigned`. That artifact is what will go to SignPath later.
- `workflow_dispatch` is now a build-only dry run: the `tag` input is removed, the tag/version check runs only on push, and the `release` job runs only for `v*` tag pushes.
- `build-darwin` now just calls `bun scripts/build.ts`.

### SignPath
- `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml` and `.signpath/README.md` describe the expected project, policy, artifact slugs and secrets. Both will be used after approval.

### Also included
- `chore(test)`: pins Claude Code to 2.1.252. The full compatibility suite passed upstream: https://github.com/aifirstprogramming/aifirstcli/actions/runs/33439784819

## Testing
- `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`: in sync (pack 1.5.0)
- `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`: clean
- `bun test`: 422 pass, 37 skip (live/e2e gated), 0 fail.
  - The first full run had 1 failure plus 1 error (`SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unexpected EOF` at `test/run.test.ts:221`).
  - `test/run.test.ts` passed when run alone, and the full suite passed on rerun, so the failure looks intermittent. I didn't find the cause.
- New tests: `test/build-config.test.ts`, `test/signpath.test.ts`, plus additions to `test/platform.test.ts`.
- Local Bun is 1.3.14, while `.bun-version` pins 1.4.0.
- **Not tested here:** the Windows build, PE metadata checks and Windows smoke test only run on a `windows-latest` runner. They need a CI run (a manual `workflow_dispatch` dry run works) to confirm.

title: build: prepare Windows releases for SignPath signing
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Windows users installing v0.8.0 got a compiled `aifirst.exe` that segfaulted inside Bun on `--version`, while the stock Bun runtime worked; the request was to "make the fix and publish replacement Windows executables" for the latest release. This PR changes how Windows binaries are built (natively, without `--bytecode`) and prepares the repository and release pipeline for a SignPath Foundation code-signing application, standardizing this CLI repository on Apache-2.0; the other repositories in that plan are not part of this PR. In the commit's words, it will "publish Apache-2.0 licensing and code-signing policy, build Windows artifacts natively with enforced PE metadata, and add the pending SignPath artifact configuration".

Previously, `build.ts` by default cross-compiled the non-darwin targets from one host with `--bytecode`, and `--all` built all targets. Target selection now lives in `selectBuildTargets` in `scripts/build-config.ts`: without flags it builds the host OS family's targets, `--local` and `--target` still pick one target, `--all` is rejected, and a Windows target requested from a non-Windows host throws. `buildArgs` omits `--bytecode` for every target and, when the target is Windows and the host is `win32`, adds PE metadata (title, publisher, a four-field version from the package version, description, copyright); non-Windows builds get none of those arguments. The release workflow splits the old combined job into `build-linux` on Ubuntu and `build-windows` on `windows-latest`, which, per its comment, exists because Bun can write Windows version resources only on a Windows host; it fails unless each `aifirst-windows-*.exe` carries the expected product, company, version, description and copyright metadata, smoke-tests the x64 and x64-baseline binaries, and uploads them as `binaries-windows-unsigned`; the `release` job now needs all three build jobs and runs only for pushed `v*` tags.

For SignPath, the PR adds `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml` describing the Windows files and metadata to sign, `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md` stating the application is pending, an Apache-2.0 `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `TRADEMARKS.md`, a `license` field in `package.json`, and CODEOWNERS entries for the release and build scripts. Unsigned Windows publishing continues until approval. The `src/index.ts` comment no longer cites `--bytecode`. Workflows now read Bun 1.4.0 from `.bun-version`, and the Claude Code pin moves to 2.1.252. New tests cover target selection and metadata arguments (`test/build-config.test.ts`), the absence of host bytecode in cross-compiled executables (`test/platform.test.ts`), and the SignPath prerequisites (`test/signpath.test.ts`). Replacement executables are published by the `release` job once a `v*` tag is pushed; this PR does not publish them itself.

title: feat: improve learner TUI responsiveness
body:
## Summary

Keeps the learner TUI responsive while exercises and replays run, and makes long or streamed content easier to work with. Also bumps the CLI to **0.13.4**.

**Running processes without blocking**
- New `src/process.ts` with `runAsyncProcess`. It spawns a child, streams its stdout/stderr through callbacks and still captures the full output. It supports timeouts and `AbortSignal`, kills the child's whole process group on POSIX (`taskkill /T` on Windows), and has an `"interactive"` stdin mode that hands the caller a `ProcessInput` writer.
- `aifirst run` (`src/commands/run.ts`) now uses it through `executePreparedExercise`. In a TTY, interactive exercises take the reader's own input and stream their output live. Without a TTY they fall back to the authored sample input.
- Replay commands that aren't shell commands (`src/replay/executor.ts`) also run through it, with streaming, abort, and relaxed-output options.
- On Linux, a graphical replay step with no `DISPLAY`/`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is now skipped (it reports a skip message) instead of hanging. Replay file reads now show a short summary for binary files (PNG dimensions, or type and size) instead of decoding them as text.

**TUI (`src/tui/session.ts`, `src/learn/native.ts`)**
- Running programs can take input from an inline input field, and the learner can stop them ("Program stopped by the learner.").
- Streamed prompts and `## Proposed plan` documents can be revealed in full with any key or a click. The footer shows a hint while this is available.
- After a run, the transcript scrolls to the latest output.
- The choice panel is sized by a new testable `tuiChoiceLayout()`. It takes at most about 45% of the screen (14 rows max), and long descriptions or previews go in a scrollable detail box instead of using the whole screen.

**Plain-terminal renderer (`src/learn/terminalRenderer.ts`)**
- A proposed-plan document can be skipped in one step with any key, instead of one block at a time. Skipping a prompt also skips the rest of its animation.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`: passes.
- New and updated tests: `graphical-run`, `replay-flow`, `run`, `terminal-renderer`, `tui-choice`, `tui-learn`, `tui-streaming`. New driver fixtures cover plan streaming, scroll-follow, interactive programs, and the native TUI.
- Full `bun test` locally: **571 pass, 37 skip, 3 fail, 1 error between tests**. None of these come from this branch:
  - `dependencies.test.ts › builds native Maven installation plans` and `tui-learn.test.ts › opens progress and command reference as dismissible Home screens` fail the same way on `main` in this environment.
  - `run.test.ts › book scoping › never hands a Python reader a Java exercise` hit its 5 s timeout under full-suite load, and the "unhandled error between tests" came from that timed-out test. `test/run.test.ts` passes on its own (28/28).
- Not run here: the live/E2E suites that need Claude or external fixtures (skipped by default), `explore:learn:pr`, and the Windows replay job. CI will cover these.

title: Keep learner TUI responsive while programs run and prompts render
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR carries out the "TUI Quality-of-Life Improvements" plan: keep terminal programs inside the TUI with live output and an embedded input field, let long prompts and plans reveal on any keypress, and stop long-running replay commands from freezing rendering.

**Design.** A new asynchronous runner, `runAsyncProcess` in `src/process.ts`, streams stdout/stderr, enforces a timeout (exit code 124 when it fires) and can be aborted. When stdin is piped and the caller supplies input, that input is written; when the run is interactive, a `ProcessInput` handle lets the TUI forward the reader's typing. Windows gets a separate stop path. `executePreparedExercise` hands the `onInputReady` callback to the process layer when a reader input exists, and that reader-input step gets no timeout even without `--no-timeout`. A multi-step run breaks out of its loop when a step exits non-zero, times out or is aborted. Previously, `--no-timeout` was read from the flags inside `runTimeoutMs`; that logic now lives in `executionTimeoutMs`. `runExercise` in `src/learn/native.ts` now prepares files and calls `executePreparedExercise` in-process instead of spawning a child `run --format json` command; with no TUI display, an interactive step uses its authored sample, so a step with no sample gets ignored stdin where the old child inherited the terminal. An aborted run now reports "Program stopped…" from the executor result rather than from the abort signal. The replay executor moves ordinary (non-shell) commands from the synchronous runner to `runAsyncProcess`, skips graphical operations on Linux when neither `DISPLAY` nor `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, and describes binary reads such as PNGs as metadata instead of raw bytes.

**Reader-facing consequences.** While a prompt or plan is animating, an ordinary key reveals the rest of it, and that key is consumed rather than also running the prompt; a mouse click on the prompt or plan panel also reveals it. In the embedded input, Ctrl+D sends end-of-input to the program. After a menu choice that runs something, the output view follows the latest output again. Detail panels scroll with PageUp/PageDown when they overflow, keeping long pickers compact: at most 14 rows and 45% of terminal height, with the list and detail panel each capped at 6 rows. `ProgramDisplayContext` carries the stdout, stderr and input-ready callbacks into that call, and `BlockSkipController` in `src/learn/terminalRenderer.ts` handles the any-key skip. New driver fixtures and tests cover streamed program output with reader input, plan streaming and scroll-follow. The package version moves to 0.13.4 for the release; CI results for that head are not yet known.

**Limits.** The Windows-specific branch in `src/process.ts` is not shown working on Windows. The renderer tests replace collaborators with fakes, so they check the key-handling logic rather than a real terminal, and the interactive TTY path in `run.ts` has not been shown with a person at the keyboard.

## Validation

title: Verify every book step both in isolation and in sequence
body:
## Summary

Every published book step is now checked two ways: on its own (as before) and in order through a shared, persistent workspace for each book, the way a learner works through it. That catches steps that only break once earlier steps' files are on disk.

### Exercise runner (`scripts/run-exercises.ts`, `scripts/lib/verify.ts`)
- New flags: `--isolated`, `--sequential` (both run when neither is given), `--report <path>`, `--json`, `--keep-workspace`.
- The sequential pass puts each book in its own temp workspace. Project steps share their `projectRoot`, and files a previous step managed but the current one doesn't declare get removed (along with `scaffold.clean`). The pass stops at a book's first failure, and the workspace is kept when something fails so you can inspect it.
- External launches are marked `delegated` to the compiled CLI book walk, not counted as passes.
- `verify()` takes an optional `directory` to reuse a workspace the caller owns. It only deletes directories it created.

### Content fixes found by the sequential walk (pack 2.0.0 → 2.0.1)
- `py-2-12` (`math.py`) now runs in its own `py-2-12/` project root, so later Python steps can't import it in place of the standard-library `math`.
- The Java Chapter 6 `pom.xml` scaffolds also declare `maven.compiler.source`/`target` 17, so they work on Maven setups that don't use `release`.

### CI
- New reusable workflow `.github/workflows/exercise-walk.yml`: Java 21 (`actions/setup-java@v5`), Python 3.12, Maven, and the JUnit console launcher. It runs both passes and uploads `report.json` as an artifact even when the run fails.
- `ci.yml` calls it in place of the old inline `run-exercises` job. `release.yml` now requires it to pass before releasing.
- New `test/exercise-walk-workflow.test.ts` pins this wiring. There are also new assertions for the `py-2-12` path and the Chapter 6 POM.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run check` (audit, asset sync, validate, `bun test`, both `tsc` configs): 482 pass, 0 fail
- [x] `bun scripts/run-exercises.ts --isolated --sequential --report test-results/book-walk/report.json` run locally: 148 isolated and 116 sequential checks passed, 20 delegated, 2 failures, both `java-6-15`, and both because of the local environment. The local JDK is 27, and the Byte Buddy version Mockito uses supports up to Java 22, so it can't mock `java.time.Clock`. CI pins Java 21. Since the sequential pass stops at a book's first failure, the Java steps after `java-6-15` were not checked locally. The JUnit console jar also wasn't in the local tool cache.
- [ ] The full exercise walk in CI on Java 21 (the authoritative run)

title: fix: make Python replays portable across platforms
body:
## Summary

Python replays recorded their shell commands as `bash -lc "..."` with a hard-coded `python3`, so they could not be replayed on Windows or any host without a POSIX shell. This PR adds a portable execution path while keeping the original command as captured.

- **Schema / types** (`schema/content.schema.json`, `src/types.ts`)
  - `portableCommand` (command ops): a cross-platform argv. `<shell>` and `<python>` are placeholders the player resolves to the host's shell and Python interpreter.
  - `display` (all ops plus `status` events): sanitized metadata about the original tool (`toolName`, `description`, `command`), so playback can show what the author actually ran, e.g. a PowerShell call, separately from how it is executed.
  - `timeoutMs` / `expectedTimeout` (command ops): lets a replay declare a command that is expected to time out. These are only in the schema for now; no content uses them yet.
- **Importer** (`scripts/lib/import-showtail.ts`): for replays with `.py` sources, emits `portableCommand` (rewriting `python3` to `<python>` when it is followed by `--version`, `-c`, `-m` or a `.py` file) and `display`.
- **Validator** (`scripts/validate.ts`): for Python steps, fails any `bash` command that uses `python`, `rm`, `timeout`, `ls` or env-var assignments but has no `<shell>` portable command. Also rejects an empty `portableCommand`, and `expectedTimeout` without `timeoutMs`.
- **Content**: regenerated `books/ai-first-python-programming.json` (56 portable commands) and the matching generated replay fixtures.
- **Tests**: covers the importer output, checks that every captured command in Python chapters 9–10 has a portable command, checks that the Windows tool label is kept, and excludes the new playback-only fields from the replay privacy-equivalence comparison.
- Bumps the package version from `1.7.1` to `1.7.2`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check` (repo privacy audit, asset sync check, `validate`, `bun test`, both `tsc` configs): 459 tests pass, schema valid.

title: fix: make Python replays portable across platforms
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Previously the Python book's replays stored each shell step only as a `bash -lc` argv (running `python3`, `rm`, `ls` and the like), which ties playback to a POSIX shell. Continuing that portability work, this PR keeps the captured argv and adds a portable alternative beside it, plus the tool label the author actually saw.

The content model gains two optional fields. `portableCommand` on command operations is a cross-platform argv of the form `["<shell>", "<command with <python> placeholders>"]` that a player can run instead of the captured `bash` argv; the schema requires at least one item. `display` (`ReplayToolDisplay`) is accepted on write, edit, read and command operations and on status events, and carries the original tool name, description and command for playback, so a step authored in PowerShell can still be labelled "PowerShell" while its portable form runs. Command operations also accept `timeoutMs` (integer, at least 1) and `expectedTimeout`.

In the Showtail importer, `operationFromTool` adds `portableCommand` and `display` to shell commands when the replay's source paths include a `.py` file; other replays are emitted unchanged. `portableShellCommand` rewrites `python3` to `<python>` where it is directly followed by `--version`, `-c`, `-m` or an unquoted `.py` path, so a `python3` before a quoted or variable path is left as is. `toolDisplay` falls back to the tool name "Tool" and includes `description` and `command` when the input has them. The `display.command` string is copied from the capture, so in the regenerated fixtures it can still contain absolute capture paths such as `/tmp/...`.

`scripts/validate.ts` gets stricter for steps whose language is Python: a `bash` command mentioning `python`, `rm`, `timeout`, `ls` or an `ENV=` assignment fails unless it has a `<shell>` portable command, checked across replay events, pre-plan events, workflow interludes and variants. This keys on the step language, while the importer keys on `.py` source paths, so the two conditions can disagree. For any language, an empty `portableCommand` or `expectedTimeout` without `timeoutMs` is rejected. The Python book, the rocket fixture and the Claude Showtail e2e fixtures are regenerated with the new fields, and the privacy-equivalence test ignores `display` and `portableCommand` when comparing semantics. The package version moves to 1.7.2.

Nothing under `src/` here executes `portableCommand`; this repository emits and validates it, and resolving `<shell>` and `<python>` is up to the consuming player.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/validate.ts`, `bun scripts/add-ids.ts --check`, `bun test` (459 pass, 0 fail, Ran 459 tests across 18 files. [1495.00ms]), `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`.

title: Record the exercise a replay starts from
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Exercise replays should be runnable independently of each other, but the py-10-01 replay ("Design a level editor" for the savetheduckling game) was reported to break because it could not find the file produced by the chapter 9 exercise. This PR makes a replay declare which earlier exercise's files it starts from, so a runner can set up that state first.

**Design.** `Replay` gets an optional `initialState: { fromExercise: string }`, mirrored in `content.schema.json`. Previously `processBundle` handed the previous exercise's scaffold to `deriveReplay` as `initialFiles` with no exercise id. When that scaffold and a previous exercise exist, `processBundle` adds `initialExerciseId`, the previous step's or parent's id. `deriveReplay` asks a new helper, `replayNeedsInitialState`, whether the replay's pre-plan, interlude and completion events read or edit a file from those initial files before the replay itself has written it. The replay records `initialState` when that holds and an exercise id was given. A replay that creates everything it touches, or that has no earlier scaffold, is left unchanged.

**Consequences.** Six replays in the Python book now carry `initialState`, each pointing at the exercise before it: py-9-02 and py-9-03 start from py-9-01 and py-9-02, py-10-01 starts from the chapter 9 exercise py-9-03, and py-10-02 through py-10-04 start from py-10-01 through py-10-03. The chapter 9 and chapter 10 retrofit tests assert this mapping, and that py-9-01 has no `initialState`. The starting exercise is the immediately previous one; a replay that touches a file from an earlier exercise but not from that one records nothing. `scripts/validate.ts` now fails when `fromExercise` names an unknown step or a step with no scaffold files. Runners still need to act on the field; this PR records and validates it. The separate picker loop reported for the py-9-01 duckling replay is not addressed here.

## Validation

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/validate.ts`, `bun scripts/add-ids.ts --check`, `bun test` (429 pass, 0 fail, Ran 429 tests across 15 files. [1073.00ms]), `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`.

It only adds the line if it isn't already there. Before, it printed instructions for the user to copy. For other shells it still asks the user to add the PATH line themselves. This PR carries the "Seamless Install and Native Learning" plan onto the website: it makes the hosted installers hand off directly to `aifirst init` and updates the site to describe the guided, AI-tool-optional experience the CLI now offers.

Previously, the installers printed "Next: aifirst init / aifirst next" (the shell script only when the directory was already on PATH; otherwise it printed the rc-file line to add and told the reader to open a new terminal and run `aifirst init`).

**Shell installer.** When the install directory is not on PATH and the shell is zsh, bash or fish, the script creates the rc file's directory if needed and appends a `# Added by aifirst` comment plus the matching `export PATH=…` or `fish_add_path` line, unless a `grep -F` finds the line already there, then reports the addition; for other shells it prints a note to add the directory later; in both cases it exports the directory onto PATH for the rest of the script. Unless `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` is set, the script hands off to `aifirst init` on `/dev/tty` if a terminal can be opened, and otherwise prints a skip notice; if setup exits non-zero it prints a hint to run `aifirst` later.

**PowerShell installer.** With `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP` not set to `1`, an interactive host runs `init` and reports when it exits non-zero; a non-interactive host gets a skip notice.

**Docs.** The home page now describes a guided offline learner that needs no AI account, alongside book skills for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity and VS Code; the CLI page says the installer's setup asks which book you are reading, creates a learning workspace and offers the built-in learner, drops the separate `aifirst init` step (and with it the note about never touching tool settings and `aifirst skill remove`), documents `aifirst learn` with Space/Enter to skip ahead and `--no-animation`, says AI tools are optional, and points to bare `aifirst` for reopening the readiness checklist.

**Consequences.** The shell installer now appends to the user's rc file without asking when the directory is off PATH, the shell is zsh, bash or fish, and the line is not already present. The PowerShell changes are Windows-specific and none of the recorded runs show that path. No recorded session command ran either changed installer script; only the diff shows their behavior.

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- `sh -n static/install.sh`: passed, run on the submitted content.

title: fix: publish macOS installer setup workaround
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the hosted installer (`curl … | sh`) no longer starts guided setup itself. Instead it tells the user to open a new terminal and run `aifirst init`.

**Why:** Bun can't currently poll stdin when it has been reopened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias ([oven-sh/bun#41495](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/41495)). Because of that, `aifirst init </dev/tty` inside the piped installer can't take keyboard input. Running `aifirst init` directly gets the real `/dev/ttysNNN` device, and that works.

## Changes

- `static/install.sh`: in the first-setup block, added a `darwin` branch that prints the `aifirst init` instruction. Linux keeps the existing `/dev/tty` behaviour, and `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` still skips setup entirely.
- `content/cli/_index.md`: the install docs now say guided setup starts automatically on Linux and Windows, and that on macOS it's a temporary manual `aifirst init` step.

## ⚠️ Installer is a synced copy

`scripts/sync-installers.sh` says `static/install.sh` is a copy, and that edits belong in `aifirstcli/install/install.sh`. This PR patches the hosted copy directly so the workaround goes live now. The same change needs to land in `aifirstcli`. If it doesn't, the next run of `sync-installers.sh` will silently undo it.

## Testing

- `sh -n static/install.sh`: passes
- `shellcheck static/install.sh`: no warnings
- Confirmed `$OS` is set to `darwin` on `uname -s` = `Darwin` (line 164)
- Not tested on a real macOS machine (none available here). Hugo build not run (`hugo` isn't installed here). The docs change is prose only.

title: Defer installer setup on macOS to avoid Bun /dev/tty input bug
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A macOS user reported that the hosted installer stops at the "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" prompt and accepts no keyboard input, while running the installed command afterwards works fine; the same user saw the identical symptom with another Bun-based installer, which points to a macOS-specific terminal input problem. This PR applies the safe workaround until a durable upstream fix ships in a release.

When `$OS` is `darwin`, the installer now skips the in-pipe `aifirst init` step and prints a short instruction to open a new terminal and run `aifirst init`. On other platforms the existing branches are kept: setup runs through `/dev/tty` when it can be opened, and otherwise falls back to the earlier message. Setting `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` still bypasses this block.

The commit message says this publishes a macOS installer setup workaround; the code comment points at a Bun stdin issue with macOS's `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495) as the reason, and says a direct invocation inherits the real terminal device and stays interactive, so setup is deferred until the pipe has exited.

The CLI page is updated to match: it now says Linux and Windows continue directly into guided setup (for `install.sh` on Linux, that holds when `/dev/tty` can be opened), while macOS users run `aifirst init` in a new terminal as a temporary extra step.

Consequences: the darwin check does not look at whether the script is piped, so every macOS run of `install.sh` with setup enabled leaves `aifirst init` to the user, so the darwin branch should be removed once a Bun release with the fix is adopted.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- `sh -n static/install.sh`: passed, run on the submitted content.

Where to start: the first-setup block in `static/install.sh`, which owns the new `darwin` branch and the `/dev/tty` fallback.

title: Fix stale xdg-desktop-portal after exiting Gaming Mode
body:
## Summary

After you leave Gaming Mode, Gamescope and Plasma can end up sharing the same user systemd manager. When that happens, `xdg-desktop-portal.service` stays running from the Gamescope session without a KDE backend. The next Plasma session then reuses that stale broker and the KDE portal interfaces (InputCapture, FileChooser, Settings, …) are missing, so Deskflow and other Flatpaks break.

This PR adds a best-effort `ExecStopPost` to the Gamescope template drop-in. It stops the generic portal broker during teardown, so Plasma starts a fresh one with the right environment.

## Changes

- **`scripts/gamescope-clear-autologin.conf`**: adds `ExecStopPost=-/usr/bin/systemctl --user stop xdg-desktop-portal.service`, placed before the existing autologin backstop. The `-` prefix keeps a shutdown or a closing user bus from marking the Gamescope unit failed. The autologin `ExecStopPost` still reports failures as before. Also updates the comment, which mentioned `Relogin=true`; the armed config no longer sets it.
- **`tests/test-units.sh`** (new): static checks on the order and failure semantics of the hooks. Also runs `systemd-analyze --user verify` against the real `gamescope-session-plus@.service` when it's installed; skips otherwise.
- **`tests/test-ensure.sh`**: shellcheck cleanups (`source=/dev/null`, an exported var in a subshell, targeted disables) and the file is now executable.
- **README**: documents the portal cleanup, tells users to re-run the installer after updating, adds a troubleshooting entry for diagnosing and recovering a stale portal, and lists the new test.

Existing installs need to re-run `./install-desktop-login.sh` to pick up the new drop-in. The installer already runs `systemctl --user daemon-reload` after writing it.

## Testing

- `./tests/test-ensure.sh`: all pass
- `./tests/test-units.sh`: all pass, including `systemd-analyze` accepting the drop-in
- `shellcheck tests/*.sh`: clean
- Not run in this environment: a full Gaming Mode → Plasma round trip on real Bazzite hardware.

title: Stop stale xdg-desktop-portal when Gaming Mode exits
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
After returning from Gaming Mode to Plasma, Flatpaks such as Deskflow can fail because the desktop portal comes back without its KDE interfaces. The aim of this PR was to inspect that problem and address it with targeted hardening rather than a broader rework. The commit describes it as fixing a stale portal after gaming mode exit.

## Design

Gamescope and Plasma can reuse the same user systemd manager, so `xdg-desktop-portal` can stay alive with no KDE backend after Gaming Mode exits. The Gamescope template drop-in now carries a first `ExecStopPost=-/usr/bin/systemctl --user stop xdg-desktop-portal.service` line, ahead of the existing autologin-clearing `ExecStopPost`. Stopping only the generic broker during teardown (synchronously, per the drop-in comment) lets the next Plasma session activate it again with the correct KDE environment. The leading `-` tells systemd to ignore a non-zero exit from the portal stop, which the drop-in comment ties to shutdown or a closing user bus. Because the hook sits on the `@.service` template, it applies to every Gamescope client instance.

## Consequences

- Existing installs only pick this up after re-running the installer, which the README now says replaces the managed scripts and drop-in in place and reloads the user manager.
- The README gains a troubleshooting entry with a `gdbus introspect` check for missing `InputCapture`/`FileChooser`/`Settings` interfaces and a manual recovery that restarts `plasma-xdg-desktop-portal-kde.service` and then `xdg-desktop-portal.service`.
- A new `tests/test-units.sh` statically checks the hook count, ordering and the best-effort prefix, and runs `systemd-analyze --user verify` on the drop-in when the Gamescope base unit is present, otherwise it skips that step; the README Tests section now lists it. `tests/test-ensure.sh` gets shellcheck annotations, an exported `WAYLAND_SESSION_DIR` in one negative case, and an executable bit.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `./tests/test-ensure.sh` (=== negative tests: must fail rather than emit a dangling Session= ===), `./tests/test-units.sh`.

**Where to start:** `scripts/gamescope-clear-autologin.conf`, the `[Service]` block, which owns the portal-stop teardown hook.

**Feedback wanted:** is stopping `xdg-desktop-portal.service` from Gamescope's `ExecStopPost` safe when the user manager is also tearing down for a real logout or shutdown, or should it be conditioned on something?

title: fix(digest): don't count commands quoted inside scripts or heredocs
body:
## What

Shell command lines from session logs were split on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newlines with a plain regex, including inside quotes and heredoc bodies. So an agent running an inline script (`python -c "..."`, `cat <<'EOF' ... EOF`) whose text mentioned `bun test` was counted as a test run, and its grouping key came out as junk like `bun test',`.

## Changes

- **`src/util/shell.ts`** (new): `splitCommands()` splits on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newlines, but leaves alone:
  - single-, double- and backtick-quoted strings (and backslash escapes)
  - heredoc bodies (`<<EOF`, `<<-EOF`, `<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`). The body is skipped up to the closing delimiter line, and anything after it is still parsed.
- **`src/digest/build.ts`**: `testSegment()` and `commandKey()` now use the splitter. Grouping keys also drop heredoc (`<<…`) and redirection (`>`, `<`, `2>`) tokens, so `cd repo && python - <<'PY' …` groups as `python`.
- **`src/correlate/correlate.ts`**: `makesCommit()` uses the same splitter, so a `git commit` that only appears inside quoted or heredoc text no longer counts as making a commit.
- Version bumped to `1.0.0-rc.12` everywhere it's set (`package.json`, `src/version.ts`, `plugin.json`, `VERSION`), and the bundle is rebuilt.

This closes the known gap noted in #8.

## Tests

New `tests/shell.test.ts` covers chains and pipes, quoted scripts with separators inside them, escaped quotes, heredoc bodies (including a pipe after the heredoc opener), test detection, and grouping keys.

- `bun test`: 96 pass, 0 fail
- `bun x tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `bun run bundle`: the rebuilt `dist/tracetoon.mjs` is byte-identical to the committed one

title: fix(digest): don't count commands quoted inside scripts or heredocs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Agents often run scripts inline, so Tracetoon has to tell a line of script text apart from a command the session actually ran. This PR makes the command splitter respect shell quoting and heredocs, so text inside a `python -c "..."` string stays inside its command and a `cat <<'EOF'` body is skipped, instead of either being split out as separate commands. The commit says it fixes a known gap noted in PR #8. The fix was found while dogfooding Tracetoon to open its own PR.

Previously, command lines were split on `;`, `|` and newlines even inside quotes and heredoc bodies, so an inline script line mentioning a test runner was detected as a test command, and (per the commit message) its grouping key came out as `bun test',`.

## Design

`splitCommands` in `src/util/shell.ts` scans the line character by character and splits on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newlines when it is outside quotes. Inside single quotes a backslash is literal; inside double quotes or backticks, and outside quotes, a backslash escapes the next character. When it sees a heredoc opener (`<<WORD`, `<<-WORD`, `<<'WORD'` or `<<"WORD"`), it skips from the end of that line through the closing delimiter line, so commands after the heredoc are still split normally. If no closing delimiter is found, the rest of the input is treated as the body.

Three existing call sites now use it instead of their own regex split: `testSegment` (test detection) and `commandKey` (grouping) in `src/digest/build.ts`, and `makesCommit` (commit detection) in `src/correlate/correlate.ts`. `commandKey` also drops tokens that start with `<`, `>` or a digit followed by `>`, so most heredoc and redirection operators stay out of a grouping key. The word after a dropped `>` is kept, though, so `cat > a.md` now groups as `cat a.md`, and a bash `&>` token is not filtered.

## Consequences

For sessions that run inline scripts, test detection, command grouping and commit detection now see the commands outside quotes and heredoc bodies rather than the script text inside them. The scanner is a heuristic rather than a full shell parser; `$(...)` substitutions are not modeled, a second heredoc opener on the same line is not skipped, and an unclosed quote (such as a stray apostrophe) makes the rest of the line one command. The new `tests/shell.test.ts` covers chains and pipes, quoted scripts, heredoc bodies and what follows them, a runner named inside a quoted script, and grouping keys; none of them exercises `makesCommit` directly. Version moves from 1.0.0-rc.11 to 1.0.0-rc.12, and the generated bundle is regenerated.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (96 pass, 0 fail, Ran 96 tests across 9 files. [42.90s]).

**Where to start:** `splitCommands` in `src/util/shell.ts` (quote and heredoc handling); the redirection filter lives separately in `commandKey` in `src/digest/build.ts`.

**Feedback wanted:** With no closing delimiter, a heredoc body runs to the end of the input; is that the right fallback, or should the scanner stop at the end of the line?

title: 1.0.0-rc.8: clickable preview link; keep unrelated work out of a PR's digest
body:
Release candidate 1.0.0-rc.8: clickable preview links, plus two fixes to which session work gets counted as part of a PR. Both digest problems turned up while using tracetoon on this PR.

## Preview link (b95f159)
- `render` and `preview` now print an absolute `file:///…/preview.html` URL that can be Ctrl+clicked. Before, they printed a bare path, which agents passed on as a relative path the user couldn't open. The URL is also returned as `previewUrl` in `--json`, and the comic image path is printed the same way.
- SKILL.md tells agents to pass the link on exactly as printed.
- Version bumped to `1.0.0-rc.8` in all four places.

## Digest: earlier work and viewed commits (f167fc6)
- **When a turn ends:** only edits inside the repo now count. Editing a file outside it (a report, notes) after the last base commit used to keep a whole earlier turn, prompts included, in the PR.
- **Which commits the session made:** a commit's SHA in a command's output only counts when the command makes commits (`commit`, `merge`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`, `am`, `rebase`, `pull`), chained or not. Before, any output counted, so a `git log` in another repo looked like the session had made the commit.
- `scripts/eval-summaries.ts` now pins two cases to fixed commits, because their branches have since been merged or committed.

## Digest: commands that start with `cd` (c973ef3)
- Agents log a command with the directory the shell was in *before* it ran. That meant `cd ../other-repo && bun test` was filed under this repo, and its test failures showed up in this PR. The new `leadingCd()` handles `cd`, `pushd`, `Set-Location`/`sl`, `~`, and Git Bash `/c/...` paths, so these commands are judged by the directory they move to.

## Testing
- `bun run typecheck`: no errors

title: compare --systems; cross-model composite delta in score
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Comparison runs needed a way to drop the native writer when the question is only whether the candidate beats the baseline, and the accuracy view needed a composite delta across models: the round's goal is a graph pipeline that matches or beats the main skill on the composite score at much lower cost, on a recommended default model per provider.

`compare --systems native,baseline,candidate` picks the writer systems for a run; a new run defaults to all three, baseline and candidate are required because the baseline pairing is the primary comparison, and full names as well as the provider's native name are accepted. Any other name is rejected with an `Unknown system` error. The selection helpers `selectSystems`, `manifestSystems` and `judgedAgainst` live in src/run/provider.ts. Previously the judging loop always compared against both `tracetoon-baseline` and the provider's native system. When native is not selected, no native writers run and only candidate vs baseline is judged, in both orders. Planned counts, rebuild coverage, the quality gate and `--plan` output follow the selected systems; the `--plan` object gains `systems` and `judgedAgainst` keys without a schema version change, and `qualityGate` takes a null native system and then skips that consensus row.

title: Add crossjudge: judge one run's candidate drafts against another run's baseline drafts
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR lets one writer model's drafts be judged directly against another model's drafts. The approved plan behind it notes that `compare` pairs drafts only within one model group, so cross-model claims rest on composite scores from separate runs, which carry about ±3 points of noise.

## Design

A new `prbench crossjudge --candidate <dir> --baseline <dir> --out <dir>` command pairs the `tracetoon-candidate` drafts of one finished compare run with the `tracetoon-baseline` drafts of another, reusing their saved artifacts; no writer runs. Each run must be a `prbench.comparison/v2` experiment with exactly one writer model. The two runs must agree on judge contract, judges, rubric version, replicates, split and case hashes, and the current checkout's rubric and judge contract must match theirs; run-to-run mismatches are refused with the list of differences, and a checkout whose rubric or judge contract differs is refused with its own message. A missing or receipt-mismatched draft is rejected before any judge call.

Each pair is judged in both orders by every configured judge and summarised with the same consensus rule `compare` uses (a win only when every judge's two orders agree on the same draft), plus per-draft composite scores, error rates and judge cost. Judge pairs run through the existing pool, four at a time unless `--parallel` says otherwise; `--parallel` must be a positive integer. With `--plan`, it verifies inputs and prints the planned call count without calling models or requiring a Claude login. Under `--out` it writes `crossjudge.json` (inputs), `pairs.json`, `summary.json` and `summary.md`; reusing an `--out` that holds a different cross-judge is refused. Judgments go through a content-addressed stage cache (`--cache`, default `<parent of --out>/.prbench-cache/v2`), and the reported judge cost sums the stored cost of every judgment, reused ones included. If a judge job fails, `pairs.json` still records the finished pairs but no summary is written. Any refusal or error is printed to stderr with exit status 2. To support this, `modelRoot` in `src/comparison.ts` is now exported.

## Consequences

The tests in `tests/crossjudge.test.ts` use fake judges, so they check pairing, refusals and summarising, not real judge behavior.

## Summary

**Judge retries and isolation-proof resume** (08b8254)
- If a judge call times out or hits a transient error, it is now retried up to 3 times with backoff instead of invalidating the run. This also applies on resume when a timeout was already saved. Codex judges now report timeouts as timeouts.
- Each failed judge attempt records which judge it was. The score report adds a judge-reliability table (`collectJudgeFailures`) next to the writer-reliability table.
- Fix: resuming any arm that had an effort was always refused with "Saved isolation proof does not match this experiment." Probes saved the bare model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), but resume compared it against the arm spec (`claude-sonnet-5-5@medium`). Probes now save the arm. Proofs saved before this change are matched on the bare model, and the experiment id still binds the exact arms.

**Score: Codex subagent usage, robustness tables, writer env hash** (18d2df1)
- Codex writer tokens and estimated cost now cover every thread a run spawned: the main rollout plus forked subagent rollouts. Each model response is counted once, by response id, so the parent history that subagents replay isn't counted twice. Live runs record `meta.usageScope` (`all-threads` / `main-thread`) and `meta.subagentThreads`.

- Paired composite deltas now show a leave-one-case-out range. A new table gives the per-case composite delta (candidate minus same-model baseline) for each model.
