title: Retry timed-out judges and count Codex subagent usage in scores
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes judge timeouts retryable instead of invalidating the comparison, counts Codex usage across the main thread and forked subagent threads, and fixes two resume problems that refused or re-froze otherwise valid experiments.

**Judges.** Previously a judge failure that was not transient ended the attempt loop, timeouts included.

Timed-out judge calls are now retried like transient ones, up to 3 attempts with backoff unless cancellation has been signalled, and a persisted timeout or format failure is retried on resume rather than refused (a format failure still is once its repair was used); Codex judges report a timeout as a timeout. 

Each unusable judge attempt now stores its judge id (older results take it from a sibling judgment, else the judge's folder name), and the score report adds a judge-reliability table beside writer reliability.

**Codex usage.** `codex exec --json` reports usage for the main thread alone. Live Codex runs now read the new rollouts from the sandbox `CODEX_HOME`, sum the main thread and forked subagent threads, and count each model response once by response id (records without one are keyed by thread, turn, timestamp and ordinal), so replayed parent history is not double counted; when the rollouts are missing or hold less input than the stdout count, the run keeps the stdout counts as main-thread usage; the artifact records `usageScope` (`all-threads` or `main-thread`) and the subagent thread count. For older Codex drafts without a recorded cost, `score` recomputes all-thread usage from the accepted attempt's saved traces when the receipt key resolves, otherwise it keeps the recorded totals, and the score table gains Cost covers and Subagents/draft columns. The judgment walk also skips `<order>.json.attempts` folders so judgments are counted once, and paired composite deltas gain a leave-one-case-out range plus a per-case table of candidate minus same-model baseline, one column per model.

**Resume.** Isolation probes saved the bare model while resume compared against the arm spec (`model@effort`), so resuming an arm with an effort was refused. Probes now record the arm, and proofs saved earlier match on the bare model; the experiment id still binds the exact arms. Writer environment identity for Codex and Claude ignores shell, terminal and session bookkeeping such as `PWD`, `SHLVL` and `CLAUDE_*`, and an experiment frozen with the legacy hash keeps it while it still matches.

tests/codex-usage.test.ts covers all-thread Codex usage. tests/comparison.test.ts covers a judge timeout being retried and counted. tests/recovery.test.ts covers a persisted judge timeout retried on resume. tests/score.test.ts covers per-judge failure counts and the leave-one-case-out range. tests/claude-comparison.test.ts covers accepting a saved proof for effort arms. tests/environment-hash.test.ts covers the environment identity and legacy hash. The comparison tests use a fake comparison setup, so they check the code around it rather than the real one.

title: Run comparisons in parallel on Codex or Claude
body:
## Summary

Comparisons can now run on either model family, and they run in parallel.

- **`--provider codex|claude|both`** chooses who writes and who judges. A comparison never mixes the two families. `claude` uses `claude-native` plus baseline and candidate Tracetoon on Opus and Sonnet (effort medium), with Opus and Sonnet as judges. `both` runs each provider independently into `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`, and the two are reported separately. `prbench auth claude` reads a `claude setup-token` token. Test-split runs must use the same provider as their development run. `compare` can still choose the writer models while keeping the provider's judges.
- **`--parallel <n>`** (default 4) runs up to n writers, judges and isolation probes at once per provider, using a new job pool (`src/run/pool.ts`). Each judge starts as soon as both drafts it compares exist. `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. Frozen inputs, cache keys and reports don't depend on the setting. After a failure no new jobs start, running jobs finish and are saved, and `--resume` continues.
- **Codex login sharing**: concurrent Codex runs reach the dedicated login file through a link instead of a copy, so a refreshed token is never overwritten. Windows keeps the exclusive copy mode.
- **Judging**: `judgmentSchema()` turns each reference field into an enum of the IDs that side may cite, so a structured-output judge can't make up a fact ID or cite the other draft's evidence. The judging prompt's meaning is unchanged, so `RUBRIC_VERSION` is not bumped.
- **Fixes**:
  - Cases recorded on Windows replay correctly on POSIX hosts.
  - The launch directory is no longer part of the Claude environment identity.
  - An escaped dot in a shell glob is no longer read as an absolute host path.
  - The sandbox's fake `gh` treats `--help` as help.

README documents providers and parallel runs.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`: passes
- `bun run prbench validate`: passes

The host shell exports `TRACETOON=0`, which leaks into the Tracetoon-arm assertions in `tests/agents.test.ts`, `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` and `tests/codex.test.ts`. title: Run compare in parallel, end to end on Codex or Claude
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The `real-cases@1.0.0` comparison was blocked because it was too slow (writers and judges ran one at a time) and Codex-only. This PR lets a user who has Claude *or* ChatGPT run a comparison end to end on that provider, judges included, with an option to run both, never mixing the two, and runs as much of the pipeline in parallel as possible.

`compare --provider codex|claude|both` picks who writes and who judges. Codex keeps Sol and Terra and its frozen identity; `claude` runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort with the same models judging, which the README calls an accepted limitation; `both` runs two independent comparisons under `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`, reported separately and never pooled. A frozen experiment refuses to resume under another provider. Previously the native system was hard-coded as `"codex-native"`. Claude Tracetoon arms install only the pinned skill and runtime, and Claude writers get a stripped Anthropic and Claude Code environment, no MCP or plugins, stop early on the result event, and have no USD cap, only the configured timeout and effort. A Claude isolation probe reads the startup catalogue, Claude judges run with no tools and no hooks, and `prbench auth claude` stores a setup token with mode 0600.

`--parallel <n>` (default 4) runs isolation probes in their own bounded pass, then schedules writers and judges as one job graph: a judge runs once the two drafts it compares exist, pairs are rebuilt in a fixed order, and `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. After a failure the pool starts no new job, and running jobs finish and are saved. Concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login through a symlink, per the commit message, while Windows keeps the copy mode. `compare --models <ids>` replaces the writer models to test cheaper writers such as Haiku or Luna, keeping the provider's judges so cheap and strong writers are scored by the same judges; ids must be distinct and `--provider both` refuses the option.

Claude judges invented fact IDs and cited the other draft's evidence, so each judge call now gets a schema whose reference fields are enums of the IDs that side may cite whenever it has any; checkJudgment still validates the rest. The Claude environment identity ignores PWD, OLDPWD, INIT_CWD and npm_* variables, which per the commit message never reach writers in their sandbox cwd, so `--reuse-from` works from another directory; the Codex hash is unchanged.

Windows-recorded cases now name the checkout by the recorded path's last segment and, under a mapped prefix on a POSIX sandbox, get POSIX separators, while unrelated host paths keep their spelling; the commit message reports pr8 now links 92 replayed edits and pr5 45, up from 0. In the scope audit, a backslash escaping a leading dot (as in `rg --files -g '!\.agents/**'`) is dropped when the token continues without backslashes; Windows paths are still flagged. The fake `gh` treats `--help`, `-h` and `gh help` as help: they print help, record a help call and do not count as a PR.

The Claude writer, judge and isolation tests replace the CLI with fakes, so they check the logic around those steps, not real Claude Code runs. The interactive terminal handling in `src/cli.ts` has no recorded check with a user at the keyboard.

title: Performance gate: pass on paired priced cost per draft, not time and tokens
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes prbench's performance gate judge a candidate on what its drafts cost, rather than on writer wall time and input tokens, following the recorded choice of a cost-based gate. Previously the gate required the candidate to improve writer wall time and not increase input tokens, so a slower candidate with more (mostly cached) input was rejected regardless of price; the writer-time interval requirement and the per-model token-recorded check are dropped as criteria.

## Design

Given complete pairs, comparable validation and any required work evidence, the gate is met when the candidate/baseline geometric mean of paired per-draft priced cost is at most 1.000; drafts are paired on model, case and replicate, and log ratios are averaged within each case before being averaged across cases, so repeats do not count as independent cases. The case-clustered 95% interval is reported but not required.

Cost per draft comes from a shared `draftCost` helper in `src/report/score.ts`, which `collectDraftScores` now calls too, so the gate uses the same pricing logic as `prbench score`: the reported total when the agent gives one, otherwise an estimate that prices each model at its own rate and cached input at its own rate, using list prices from `src/report/prices.json` (not an invoice). `rebuildComparison` attaches that priced cost to each writer metric.

If any draft in a candidate/baseline pair has no usable priced cost (the draft is missing, a model has no price, token counts are missing, Codex usage is limited to the main thread, or the cost is not positive), the gate is inconclusive and lists that draft in `unpricedDrafts`.

## Consequences

Writer wall time and token counts stay in the report as information, not criteria. Validation-comparability handling is unchanged. The report schema moves from `prbench.performance/v2` to `v3`, adding fields such as `rule`, `unpricedDrafts`, `geometricMeanCostRatio` and `costRatio95CI`; the comparison summary states the rule and labels the cost ratio as the criterion and the writer-time ratio as information; and because `src/performance.ts` changed, the gate policy hash changes. The CHANGELOG and README describe the new rule.

The updated tests describe a cheaper but slower candidate with more input tokens, a pricier but faster one, and an unpriced draft; an existing slower-candidate assertion now expects a pass, and `tests/comparison.test.ts` checks the v3 schema and `pricedCost` on writer metrics.

title: Absolute draft scoring, effort-aware arms, and writer retries
body:
## Summary

Adds absolute per-draft scoring and makes comparison runs survive single writer failures. Before this, one failed writer invalidated the whole run.

**Scoring**
- New `prbench score <roots…>` command, plus a Scores section in every compare summary. It scores each draft on coverage (claims, context, uncertainties), rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, averaged over all of the draft's judgments. It also reports a documented 0–100 composite, case-clustered bootstrap intervals and paired candidate deltas. It works retroactively on old runs.
- New Accuracy section:
  - error rate per arm: the share of judgments with ≥1 factual error, with a case-clustered CI
  - error classes: validation, code structure, attribution, motivation, pipeline
  - every candidate arm compared against every baseline arm, with a 0.05 claim-coverage guard and the cost ratio
- `src/report/prices.json` estimates USD from token counts when a run reports no cost (Codex), so cost and score can be compared per draft.

**Effort as part of the arm**
- `compare --models model@effort`: writers get the bare model plus that effort (default `medium`, as before). Saved artifacts must match both model and effort.
- Isolation probes run at the configured effort, not the arm's. Haiku@low misreported the skill path and stopped whole runs.

**Writer reliability**
- Writers that leave no draft (`no-draft`), fail the scope audit, or time out are retried, up to 3 attempts. A rejected draft is never scored. `failure.json` names the arm. A new writer reliability table counts each kind of failed attempt per arm.
- Writer output is cached only after the scope audit passes, so a retry no longer collides with an immutable cache entry.
- fake gh supports `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose`, taking the title and body from the branch's commits. Explicit `--title`/`--body` take precedence.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`: passes.
- `bun run prbench validate`: passes.
- `bun run test`: 237 pass, 1 skip, 3 fail. The 3 failures come from this environment, not the code: the shell exports `TRACETOON=0`, which leaks into the sandbox env, so the tests asserting that variable is unset fail:
  - `agent systems > tracetoon: installs into the sandbox…`
  - `claude comparison writers > tracetoon arm installs only the pinned skill and runtime`
  - `Codex systems > same prompt/model/effort and isolation…`

  With `env -u TRACETOON`, all 3 pass. The full suite was not rerun with the variable unset.

## Notes

- `CHANGELOG.md` is not updated in this branch.
- No rubric meaning changes, so `RUBRIC_VERSION` is unchanged.

title: Score drafts on an absolute scale, run writers at a chosen effort, and retry failed writers
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR moves prbench from "A or B is better" toward a score, because an A/B verdict alone makes it hard to tell how much better a writer is getting. It also lets a writer run at a lower effort, so cheap models and low-effort arms can be compared on quality and cost.

## Design

`prbench score <roots…>` and a Scores section in compare summaries report per-draft coverage (claims, context, uncertainties), rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, averaged over all judgments of a draft, with a 0-100 composite and case-clustered bootstrap intervals. Components are fractions of the fact sheet and rubric over applicable items; coverage with no applicable items counts as 1, a draft with no scored rubric items is scored on coverage weights rescaled to 100, and mistakes (15 per factual error, 7 per unsupported claim, 10 per trap) subtract without taking the composite below zero. `src/report/prices.json` estimates USD from token counts when a run reports none (Codex), so cost and score can be compared per draft. The estimate prices cached input at its own rate, from third-party list prices dated 2026-11-06 that the file says to verify against the provider. An Accuracy section gives the error rate per arm, error classes, and each candidate arm against each baseline arm.

`compare --models model@effort` makes effort part of the arm. Previously `runComparisonWriter` handed writers the full model string with `effort: "medium"`; now writers get the bare model and the arm's effort, defaulting to medium when none is given. Scoring reads saved rubric-v6 judgments (other rubric versions are skipped), which the commit message says makes it work on old runs retroactively. Arms are checked against the provider's efforts and must be distinct, and a saved artifact must match the arm's model, and also its effort when the arm names one. Isolation probes use the bare model but run at the configured effort, since low-effort models misreported the skill path.

A low-effort writer can finish without a PR: Luna@low refused to publish when it skipped the skill's role phases, and Sonnet@low ran `gh pr create --fill`, which the fake gh recorded without a title. Both invalidated whole runs. `failureKind` adds `no-draft` (writer finished without a PR) and `scope` (the scope audit rejected the draft), retried like transient failures; a writer that hits the timeout is also retried, up to 3 attempts. Per the commit messages, the rejected draft stays rejected and is not scored, and a new sample in a fresh sandbox takes its place, so one mistyped absolute path (Luna@low dropping a TMPDIR segment) costs an attempt rather than the run; a writer rejected on all 3 attempts still stops it. A scope-rejected sample is no longer cached, so its retry doesn't hit the immutable cache entry. A writer reliability table counts these attempts per arm, with scope-rejected and timed-out attempts in their own columns. The fake `gh` now honours `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose`, with explicit `--title`/`--body` winning.

## Limits

In the comparison fixture, the fake Codex writer types one mangled out-of-sandbox path and the comparison is expected to complete with one scope failure recorded. Those fixtures replace the real writer and `gh` with fakes, so they cover the logic around those steps, not the real steps.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run prbench validate`, `bun run test` (240 pass, 0 fail, Ran 241 tests across 34 files. [229.30s]).

Where to start: `rebuildComparison` in src/comparison.ts, which adds the scores and writer reliability table to compare summaries; the cache-after-audit change lives in `compareV2` in the same file.

Feedback wanted: are the composite weights (coverage and rubric summing to 100, mistakes subtracting) a reasonable single number to track, or should reports lead with the error rate instead?

title: Keep shell bookkeeping out of writers and out of the environment identity
body:
## Problem

A Claude comparison couldn't be resumed from a new shell. The Claude environment hash included every inherited variable, so per-process values like `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID` changed it from one shell to the next. Those same variables also reached writers, which meant `CLAUDE_EFFORT` from the host session could change a writer's effort.

## Change

- `src/run/sandbox.ts`: adds an exported `VOLATILE_ENV` list for per-login and per-process bookkeeping (`INVOCATION_ID`, `JOURNAL_STREAM`, `SHLVL`, `OLDPWD`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `_`, …) and `VOLATILE_PREFIXES` (`KONSOLE_`, `CLAUDE_`). Sandboxes now drop both. `CLAUDE_` replaces the narrower `CLAUDE_CODE_` prefix, so it also covers `CLAUDE_PID` and `CLAUDE_EFFORT`.
- `src/run/provider.ts`: `claudeComparableEnv()` skips exactly that list. The hash still changes when anything a writer can see changes.
- `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts`: a new test checks that `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `INVOCATION_ID` and `SHLVL` leave the hash unchanged and never reach the sandbox env, and that an unrelated variable (`SOME_TOOL_SETTING`) still changes the hash.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`: passes.
- `bun run test`: 230 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail across 32 files.
  - The test shell had `TRACETOON=0` exported. With it set, `tracetoon arm installs only the pinned skill and runtime` fails because the fake Claude reads it. That comes from the environment, not this branch, so the suite was run with `TRACETOON` unset.

title: Keep shell bookkeeping out of writers and the Claude environment identity
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This fix came up while comparing drafts for work on how Tracetoon builds and retrieves its evidence graph, where the request was to make the graph cheaper and more precise for the drafting task; a comparison run had to be cancelled, fixed and restarted. Per the commit message, a Claude comparison could not resume from a new shell because the environment hash covered per-process variables like `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`. The same variables also reached writers, and `CLAUDE_EFFORT` from the host session could change a writer's effort. Previously the sandbox's dropped prefixes were `CODEX_`, `ANTHROPIC_` and `CLAUDE_CODE_`.

`src/run/sandbox.ts` now exports two lists: `VOLATILE_ENV` (systemd, session and shell bookkeeping such as `INVOCATION_ID`, `JOURNAL_STREAM`, `XDG_SESSION_ID`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `GPG_TTY`, `OLDPWD`, `SHLVL` and `_`) and `VOLATILE_PREFIXES` (`KONSOLE_` and `CLAUDE_`). `sandboxEnv` deletes a variable when its upper-cased name matches one of these, alongside the existing dropped names and prefixes, so sandboxes now drop every `CLAUDE_*` variable and per-login session bookkeeping. `claudeComparableEnv` in `src/run/provider.ts` imports the same two lists and skips a variable when its name, as given, is in `VOLATILE_ENV` or starts with a volatile prefix.

Consequences: writers lose access to `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `GPG_TTY`, the D-Bus session address and `KONSOLE_*` variables, so a writer that relied on the host's SSH agent or GPG TTY will no longer find them. Because the hash now skips names it used to include, a shell that sets any of them gets a different identity from before this change, so existing experiments recorded under the old hash will not match. The sandbox matches upper-cased names while the hash matches names as given, so a mixed-case spelling is dropped from writers but still counted in the hash. A new test in `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` sets `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `INVOCATION_ID` and `SHLVL`, checks that the hash is unchanged and that a sandbox's env lacks them, and checks that an unrelated `SOME_TOOL_SETTING` changes the hash.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run prbench validate`, `bun run test` (230 pass, 0 fail, Ran 231 tests across 32 files. [617.88s]).

Where to start: `sandboxEnv` in `src/run/sandbox.ts`, which owns dropping the volatile names from writers.

Feedback wanted (the change drops every `CLAUDE_*` variable from writers): is that too broad, or does a writer's Claude Code legitimately need one of them from the host?

title: fix: recover shell exit codes from Claude tool result text
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A code comment in the change notes that Claude sometimes puts a shell command's nonzero status in the tool-result text rather than in a structured exit-code field. This PR makes the Claude importer recover that status from the text so tool-result events can carry an `exitCode`, in support of the goal of using the chapter 9 exercises as acceptance criteria for this importer work.

Previously `rawToolResult` read the exit code from the structured fields `exitCode`, `exit_code` and `code`, first on the structured result and then on the content block. Now, when neither of those yields an integer, it falls back to a new helper, `resultTextExitCode`, applied to the block's `content`. That helper returns nothing when `asString` yields no text for the content, and nothing unless the text begins with `Exit code` followed by a signed integer and then a line break or end of text (so `Exit code 1 (timed out)` does not match); otherwise it returns the parsed integer. Structured fields keep precedence, so a transcript that already carries a numeric exit code is read as before.

As a consequence, a Bash result flagged `is_error` whose content begins with `Exit code 1` now yields a tool-result event with `exitCode: 1` next to `isError: true`, and the Bash fixture in `tests/claudeToolCall.test.ts` now carries that prefix and expects that event shape. The pattern is anchored at the start of the content, so an "Exit code" phrase later in ordinary output is not treated as a status. The fallback is not gated on tool name or `is_error`, so any tool result whose content begins `Exit code 0` also gets `exitCode: 0`.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`.
- `bun test`: failed (656 pass, 17 fail, Ran 677 tests across 91 files. [242.11s]), run on the submitted content.

Where to start: `rawToolResult` in `src/core/claudeCode.ts`, which owns the structured-then-text fallback order for `exitCode`.

Feedback wanted: should the text fallback be limited to results flagged `is_error`, or is matching a leading `Exit code <n>` line on any result safe enough?

title: Add a local Docker test environment for Showtail
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR adds an isolated Docker environment for exercising Showtail against real Claude Code and Codex installs, keeping host source, agent configuration and credentials isolated. The request was to set up a local Docker test environment modeled after the scripts in the aifirstcli project, and the agreed plan called for two workflows: a persistent manual sandbox for the compiled CLI and a one-shot runner for the existing live capture tests.

**Design.** A multi-stage `Dockerfile` based on `oven/bun:1` installs `bash`, `curl`, `git`, `ripgrep` and the Claude Code and Codex CLIs, then compiles the checkout to `/usr/local/bin/showtail`; per a Dockerfile comment, the agent CLIs live under `/opt` so resetting the home volume doesn't reinstall them while keeping the source and dependencies for the live tests. `.dockerignore` keeps `.git`, `.showtail`, agent directories, env files and keys out of the build context. Shared helpers in `scripts/docker-common.sh` map the host architecture to a Bun target (x86_64/amd64 or aarch64/arm64; anything else fails with an error), build the image, and prepare two named volumes. Following the decision to copy minimal auth, the host's `.claude.json`, `.claude/.credentials.json` and `.codex/auth.json` are mounted read-only and copied into the home volume when the source file exists and the target is not already present. The sandbox and test containers run with all capabilities dropped and `no-new-privileges`, while the volume-preparation container runs as root without those flags. Image, volume and test-identity names default to values overridable through `SHOWTAIL_DOCKER_*` variables.

**Consequences.** The manual sandbox script forwards its arguments to `showtail` or provides `shell`, `login claude|codex` and `clean` subcommands; `clean` removes each named volume that exists and reports the others as already absent. Codex login pipes `OPENAI_API_KEY` over stdin to `codex login --with-api-key` when set and otherwise requires an interactive terminal for device login. `scripts/docker-live-test.sh --check` verifies the installs and exits 20 if Claude Code isn't authenticated or 21 if Codex isn't, without calling a model; without `--check` it then runs `tests/live/capture.live.test.ts` with `SHOWTAIL_LIVE=1` and `SHOWTAIL_DISABLE_FIRST_RUN=1`, which consumes model quota. `docs/contributing.md` documents both workflows. Both scripts rebuild the image from the current checkout at every invocation. The agent CLIs come from unpinned install scripts with no cache-busting, so a cached layer keeps the older CLI until that layer is invalidated.

title: feat: add self-upgrade command
body:
## Summary

Adds `showtail upgrade`, so standalone installs can update themselves without re-running the one-line installer.

- **`src/core/selfUpgrade.ts`**: looks up the latest GitHub Release, picks the asset for the current OS/CPU, and downloads it next to the installed binary. It checks that the download runs and that `--version` prints the expected version. Then it swaps the binary and `showtail.vsix` into place, keeping backups so it can roll back if the swap fails. Finally it refreshes capture integrations with `setup --first-run`.
  - Refuses to run when invoked through Bun or a source checkout, so it can never overwrite the Bun runtime or a developer checkout.
  - On Windows the running `.exe` is locked, so a detached PowerShell helper finishes the swap (with rollback) after the command exits. In that case the result is `pending`.
  - Reports `current` or `newer` and makes no changes when nothing needs upgrading.
- **CLI**: a new `upgrade` command (with `--json`) under a new "Maintain Showtail:" help group. It is excluded from the first-run bootstrap hook.
- **Docs**: README, installation guide, CLI reference, classroom workflow and CHANGELOG.

## Testing

- `bun test tests/selfUpgrade.test.ts`: 8 pass, 0 fail. The tests cover version comparison, asset mapping, refusing Bun/source copies, the Windows helper script, upgrade/rollback, and the current/newer cases.
- New `tests/cli.test.ts` case: running `upgrade` from a Bun/source invocation exits non-zero before any network request.
- Full `bun test` in this sandbox: 622 pass, 4 skip, 71 fail. I looked at the failures and none involve the upgrade code. Most are the 5 s per-test timeout firing in this slow environment: hook/CLI end-to-end tests, plus contract tests that fail because those tests did. Two more fail because this sandbox puts its temp dir under the workspace (project-discovery and Codex auto-capture checks see the enclosing checkout). I didn't run a baseline on `main` in this environment, so I haven't confirmed these failures also happen there. Please check CI.
- Not tested: a real network upgrade against a published release, and the Windows swap path running on actual Windows.

title: feat: add showtail upgrade for standalone installs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR adds a `showtail upgrade` command so that a copy installed with one of the one-line installers can update itself in place, without finding and re-running the installer.

## Design

`runUpgrade` in `src/commands/upgrade.ts` calls `selfUpgrade` in the new `src/core/selfUpgrade.ts` and reports the result, or emits it as JSON when `--json` is given. `selfUpgrade` first checks that the current executable file is named `showtail` (`showtail.exe` on Windows) and exists, and refuses a Bun/source invocation before making a network request, since that path points at the Bun runtime. It then maps the host platform and architecture to the release asset name, asks the GitHub releases API for the latest release of `Tingsters/Showtail`, or of the repository in `SHOWTAIL_REPO` when that is set (sending `GITHUB_TOKEN` when one is set), and compares the release version numerically against the installed one.

When the installed copy is current, the command prints that it is up to date; when it is newer than the latest release, it makes no changes. Otherwise it downloads the binary and the bundled `showtail.vsix` extension, runs the downloaded binary's `--version` and checks the reported version matches the release (no checksum or signature is checked), and then swaps files. On Linux and macOS the old binary and extension are moved to backups, the new files are renamed into place, and the backups are restored if a replacement step fails; integrations are then refreshed on a best-effort basis, and when that refresh returns false the command says they will refresh the next time Showtail runs. On Windows the running executable can't be replaced, so a detached PowerShell helper waits for the process to exit, swaps both files with rollback, and reruns setup; the command reports the upgrade as pending in that case, before the helper has finished; if Showtail has not exited within 30 seconds the helper gives up and deletes the downloads.

`upgrade` also skips the first-run setup bootstrap. The README, installation guide, classroom workflow, CLI reference and changelog describe the new command.

## Consequences and limits

When verification fails, the code throws before the swap, so the installed files stay in place. The recorded runs were on linux/x64, so none shows the macOS or arm64 paths running.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`.
- `bun test`: failed (626 pass, 67 fail, Ran 697 tests across 95 files. [307.66s]), run on the submitted content.

Where to start: `runUpgrade` in `src/commands/upgrade.ts`, which owns the current, newer and pending status messages.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR prepares the repository for a SignPath Foundation code-signing application: the goal is to "prepare Showtail for SignPath Foundation Windows code signing while keeping the application itself deferred until credible public reputation evidence is available", with only `showtail-windows-x64.exe` in the signed scope. The plan calls for complete Apache-2.0 licensing, a third-party licence inventory with a CI check, and origin-verified signing before release publication, so the work touches licensing, build scripts, CI, release, installers and docs together.

**Release pipeline.** Previously the release workflow copied whichever `showtail-*.vsix` was newest; it now copies the file named for the extension version. The release workflow gains a `validate` job that checks the tag format, matches it against the package and source versions, and requires the tag commit to be on `main`. Non-Windows binaries build in their own job, the Windows executable is uploaded unsigned and submitted to SignPath for signing, and `publish` needs `validate` and both build jobs. The Windows job throws unless the `SIGNPATH_ENABLED` variable is `'true'` and the SignPath organization ID and API token are configured, so tag releases cannot publish before onboarding; after signing it requires exactly one executable with a Valid Authenticode signature from SignPath Foundation and matching product name and versions. `publish` also attaches an SPDX SBOM, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and a `SHA256SUMS` file.

**Builds and licensing.** `.bun-version` and the workflows' setup-bun steps pin Bun 1.4.0. `scripts/build-all.sh` now builds only the non-Windows targets via `build-non-windows.sh` and prints that Windows builds must run `build-windows.ps1` on Windows. `scripts/build-windows.ps1` stops when the package version, embedded version or a Windows metadata field differs from what is expected, and CI runs it on the Windows matrix leg. `scripts/verify-licenses.ts` (run as `bun run license:check`) compares declared dependencies against an approved inventory and checks that the extension ships no runtime dependencies.

**Supply chain and policy.** External GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs, CodeQL runs on pushes and pull requests to `main` plus a weekly schedule, and Dependabot, CODEOWNERS and a SignPath artifact configuration are added. The dependency review workflow runs on pull requests, and its job is skipped unless the `DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED` repository variable is `'true'`; a workflow comment notes the action fails when Dependency Graph is disabled. Docs gain a code-signing policy and uninstallation page, an updated privacy page, `SECURITY.md`, third-party notices and an application checklist.

**Installers.** `install.ps1` and `install.sh` now print what they will change; when `SHOWTAIL_DISABLE_FIRST_RUN` is set both installers report that setup is skipped. `tests/signingReadiness.test.ts` asserts these policy, pinning and signing requirements.

## Summary

Adds `showtail migrate`, which goes back to existing (older) trails and recovers the transcript detail newer Showtail versions capture.

- **`showtail migrate [tool]`** matches existing sessions to local Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI/IDE, Copilot CLI and Copilot Chat transcripts. It adds missing replies, edits, plans, decisions, models, tool calls/results and recap stats without rewriting anything. Options: `--dry-run`, `--json`, `--session`, `--file`, `--yes`, `--resume`.
- **`showtail migrate undo [batch-id]`** removes a migration batch and records a declared `migration-undo` marker, so `verify` stays clean.
- **One-time upgrade offer.** Existing generation-1 installs get one prompt with consent: scan home for projects, show one bulk preview, ask for one confirmation. Fresh installs aren't prompted. Non-interactive runs and `--json` defer the offer. Bulk progress lives in `~/.showtail-cli/migrations/`.

title: fix: launch extension CLIs through cmd on Windows
body:
## Summary
On Windows, VS Code-style launchers (`code`, Antigravity's CLI) are `.cmd` batch files. `spawnSync` goes through `CreateProcess`, which can't run batch files directly. That includes a bare `code` that PATHEXT resolves to `code.cmd`. As a result, `connect` couldn't install the bundled VSIX.

- Adds `src/core/extensionCli.ts`:
  - `extensionCliInvocation()` sends every Windows launch through `%ComSpec%` (falling back to `cmd.exe`) as `/d /c <cli> ...args`. POSIX launchers still run directly.
  - Each token is passed as a separate spawn argument, so Node/Bun does the Windows quoting. That covers paths with spaces, like `Program Files` and temp directories.
  - `runExtensionCli()` wraps `spawnSync` with `utf8` output.
- `vscodeExtension.ts` and `antigravityIdeExtension.ts` now use `runExtensionCli` instead of calling `spawnSync` directly.
- Adds unit tests for the invocation shape on win32 (bare `code` and a full `.cmd` path containing spaces) and on POSIX.
- Includes the Showtail provenance trail (`.showtail/`) for this change.

- `bun x tsc --noEmit`: passes

title: fix: launch extension CLIs through cmd on Windows
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR routes VS Code and Antigravity extension-CLI launches on Windows through the command processor, a change requested as a blocker before tagging a new Showtail release.

Both `installVsCodeExtension` and `installAntigravityIdeExtension` are changed to launch the extension CLI through a shared helper. According to a code comment in the commit, Windows installs expose `code`-style CLIs as `.cmd` batch files, which a direct `spawnSync` cannot execute, even when a bare `code` resolves to `code.cmd` through PATHEXT.

## Design

A new module, `src/core/extensionCli.ts`, owns the process invocation. `extensionCliInvocation(cli, args, targetPlatform, commandProcessor)` returns a `{ command, args }` pair:

- When the target platform is `win32`, the command is the command processor and the arguments are `/d /c <cli> …args`.
- On any other platform, the launcher is executed directly with its arguments unchanged.

The command processor defaults to `ComSpec`, then `COMSPEC`, then `cmd.exe`. `runExtensionCli` builds that invocation using the runtime `process.platform` default and runs it with `spawnSync` and UTF-8 output; both installers now call it in place of their own `spawnSync` call. Each token is a separate spawn argument after `/c`, and the code comment leaves Windows quoting of paths with spaces (under `Program Files` or in temporary directories) to Node/Bun.

## Consequences

The installers' result handling is unchanged: a zero exit status still means installed. The platform and command processor are parameters, so tests can check the Windows shape on any host; the new tests in `tests/vscodeExtension.test.ts` assert that every Windows launcher is routed through `cmd.exe` and that POSIX launchers run directly. The test file supplies the command processor as an argument, so the `ComSpec`/`COMSPEC`/`cmd.exe` default is outside its scope. Those tests inspect the invocation that is built rather than spawning a real `.cmd` file, so the Windows CI leg is what exercises the real launch path; its results for this head are not in the session logs.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`.
- `bun test`: failed (615 pass, 69 fail, Ran 688 tests across 94 files. [324.85s]), run on the submitted content.

Where to start: `extensionCliInvocation` in `src/core/extensionCli.ts`, which owns the Windows `cmd.exe /d /c` routing and the `ComSpec` fallback.

Feedback wanted: `cmd /c` strips outer quotes when its command line both starts and ends with a quote, so does a quoted launcher path with spaces plus a spaced VSIX path survive this invocation, or should the `/c` string be built as one outer-quoted argument?

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR implements two fixes to Tracetoon's PR evidence output so description writers stop misplacing behaviors and misreading diff direction. When one change unit touches several functions, a writer had no way to tell which function does what, and could fall back on call relations; and bare `+`/`-` code fragments let a removed line be read as added.

**Design.** `patchHunks` in `src/graph/build.ts` now records per-function changed-line words (`fnWords`), with a changed doc comment going to the definition below it, so a hunk defining several functions still tells them apart. `ownerRows` in `src/graph/briefExtras.ts` splits commit sentences into clauses and maps each clause to the one or two changed functions whose changed lines say it; a word shared by more than two functions counts half, linked hunks get a bonus, and a clear lead is required. Only source hunks contribute, and a row's functions all sit in one file. Owners rows are emitted only for change units where two or more functions own different sentences, at most 5 per unit and 6 in all, and never as call relations. The new `owners` section appears in the TOON brief, in the neighborhood tail via `renderNeighborhood`, and, when there are owners rows, in the lean review packet.

Code cells change too: `added:` / `removed:` replace bare `+`/`-`, pairs read `was ... -> now ...`, and a changed boolean condition (including multi-line chains) lists the operands it dropped, kept and added. Value fallbacks such as `a || ref` stay value changes, and direction words are discounted from the code-cell budget, so they cost about what `+`/`-` did (one character less for `added:`, one more for `removed:`). Previously the cost was a flat `line.length + 3`. The conflict check now skips operand lines and splits `⇒` pairs on any whitespace. `drafting.md` now tells writers to read direction from code cells and name where a behavior lives from the owners rows.

title: Record every check in a chained command, and keep the full merge base
body:
## What changed

**Every check in a chained command is now recorded.** Agents often chain checks in one shell command, for example `bun run bundle; bun x tsc --noEmit && bun test > log; bun scripts/eval.ts`. Before this change the digest kept only the first verification segment, so the rest looked like they never ran. The new `commandRuns` in `src/digest/build.ts` returns one run per check, in order. `commandRun` now returns the first of these.

- Several test runners in one command still collapse into one run with an `unknown` outcome, as before.
- When a command holds several checks, they share one output. Each run keeps only the output lines that match its own kind (`KIND_LINE`), so a test run no longer carries an eval's `57/57 checks pass` line.
- A non-zero exit from a chain of checks can't be blamed on any one of them. Those runs are `unknown`, not `failed`. A single failing check is still `failed`.

**The digest records the full merge-base hash.** `pr.mergeBase` used to be cut to 12 characters. `src/commands/source.ts` compares requested revisions against `digest.pr.mergeBase`, so `source --revision base` returned the short hash. It now returns the full 40-character SHA.

**Bundle rebuilt.** `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` and `build.json` were regenerated with `bun run bundle`. On main's source, the bundle comes out byte-identical to main's committed bundle, so this diff comes only from the source change above.

## Tests

- New test in `tests/evidence.test.ts` covers: chained build/test/eval runs, per-kind output filtering, `&&` chains, and a failing chain giving `unknown` while a single failing check gives `failed`.
- `tests/preparation.test.ts` checks that `--revision base` resolves to a full 40-character hash.

## Verification (local, Linux, Bun 1.3.14)

- `bun run typecheck`: passed
- `bun run test`: 36 source test files passed, 0 failed
- `bun run bundle && bun run build:check`: passed
- `test:bundled` / `test:compiled`: not run locally. They are left to CI, which runs the packaged contracts on every PR.

title: test: guard CLI and test-runner processes that Bun on Windows does not exit
body:
## Summary

On the Windows CI runner, Bun 1.3.14 sometimes keeps running after it has finished its work. This happens both for `tracetoon` CLI processes that have already printed their whole result and for `bun test` itself after it prints `Ran N tests across 1 file`. Each run hit a different test file, so jobs stalled until a timeout fired. This branch makes the CLI and the test harness stop waiting on a process that is done.

**Product change**
- `src/cli.ts`: after the command runs, flush stdout/stderr and then call `process.exit(exitCode)`. Before this, the CLI relied on exiting naturally, and any handle left open kept the process alive. If `TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` is set, the CLI writes its exit code to that file just before exiting. It removes the variable from its own environment first, so child processes never inherit it.

**Test harness**
- `tests/spawn-guard.ts`: runs a command with inherited stdio. If the exit file appears and the process is still alive 3s later, the guard kills it and returns the recorded exit code. Commands that exit on their own, or never finish, behave as before.
- `tests/helpers.ts` (preloaded for every test file) mocks `node:child_process`. `spawnSync(bun, [cli.ts | tracetoon.mjs, …])` now goes through the guard, which covers every test file that spawns the CLI.
- review-run / review-lean: each CLI call is capped at 180s, and a timeout produces an error with the command and its partial output. Output is redirected to files instead of pipes, because on Windows a leftover child process can hold a pipe open. `TRACETOON_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS=60000` stops a hung fake reviewer after one minute instead of 15.
- `scripts/test-files.ts`: once a file prints its Bun summary line, the runner waits 20s for bun to exit (configurable via `TRACETOON_TEST_EXIT_GRACE_MS`). If bun is still running, the runner kills it and takes the result from the summary's fail/error counts. A killed child's pipes are destroyed and unref'd. `test-source` and `test-packaged` exit explicitly. The per-test timeout goes from 30s to 120s, since a single CLI call takes about 10s on the Windows runner.

title: Target one repo for gh calls and stop a Bun that won't exit from hanging tests
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR fixes issue 52: context, doctor and publish now share one target repo, and once it is resolved, the gh calls that read or write PRs or repo metadata pass it with `--repo`. It also stops a hung Windows test file from stalling CI for hours; per commit f17a0924eef1, Windows runs had hung three times in different files with no output.

**Target repo.** The target is gh's default repo when it is a remote of this clone (fork to upstream), else origin; when origin is a GitHub remote, a stale default that matches no remote is ignored. Context records the target in context.json, render stores it in the approval and hashes it into the approval code, and the preview prints 'PR target: ...'. After re-resolving the target, publish refuses before any PR call if it differs from the approved one. Doctor reports the target and checks push access on origin. Previously the private-repo check ran on the clone alone; it now uses the target; per commit 6658b0a4db80, comic hosting still pushes to origin. When origin is a fork of the target, `gh pr create` gets `--head owner:branch`, and the existing-PR lookup drops PRs whose head is not in that fork. Digest and render read check receipts whenever the run has any, not only after `task begin`; receipt summaries let a wrapper's total win over per-file lines, and the environment identity ignores temp and terminal variables. tests/target.test.ts covers target choice and tests/receipts-and-fork.test.ts the fork head and receipts; existing tests now expect the targeted gh calls.

**Hang guards.** Previously the runner waited for each file's close event with no limit. It now kills a file after `TRACETOON_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS` (15 minutes by default; the whole process tree on Windows, the child pid elsewhere) and fails it with its output so far, and CI caps the job at 45 minutes. Once a file's summary appears, bun gets `TRACETOON_TEST_EXIT_GRACE_MS` (20s by default) before it is killed and judged by the summary, and a killed child's pipes are destroyed and unref'd so an orphan cannot keep the runner alive; tests/test-files.test.ts covers both kills. The runner also hands bun `--timeout 120000` instead of its 5s default; a code comment notes Bun 1.3 skips the bunfig.toml value. The CLI flushes output and exits explicitly, writing its code to `TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` when that is set; according to commit 9af69e8f453c, CLI processes that printed their result without exiting kept appearing in new test files. tests/helpers.ts, which the test preload loads, routes spawnSync of the CLI through `tests/spawn-guard.ts`, which kills a CLI still alive 3s after recording its code; commands that exit themselves, or hang before recording one, behave as before. Per commit e8b441728a5d, a Windows `review run --all` call stalled after printing its result, because piped spawnSync on Windows waits for every pipe holder. Commit 2fe71a320c8c says the watchdog caught review-run.test.ts stalled for 15 minutes; review-run and review-lean CLI calls are capped, redirect output to files, and count a timed-out call with its whole JSON result as finished. The merged-list test no longer hard-codes pass order, which depended on which concurrent reviewer finished first.

Commit messages 9af69e8f453c and fd4c9f7b30d5 describe Windows reruns where bun did not exit after its summary. Recorded CI results are for an earlier commit; the fork tests use a fake gh. The bundle is rebuilt.

title: Add an evidence graph of how each PR was made, queryable by the agents
body:
## What this adds

Each digest now also builds `evidence-graph.json`, a graph of how the PR was made. It links:

- prompts to the edits made in their turn
- edits to the diff hunks their lines still appear in
- check runs to the PR files edited after them
- commits to the sessions that made them

The graph runs in-process on **cypherlite v0.16.1 compiled to WebAssembly**. The `.wasm` file and its glue code are vendored under `plugin/skills/tracetoon/assets/` and `src/graph/vendor/`, and pinned by tag, revision and SHA-256 in `build-dependencies.json`. No native modules are added. Builds refuse mismatched bytes (`bun scripts/cypherlite.ts check`), and `bun scripts/cypherlite.ts rebuild` reproduces the bytes.

### Changes

- **`tracetoon query`**: named questions (`outline`, `why`, `unverified`, `unexplained`, `stale`, `dead-ends`, `turn`, `pushback`, `schema`) plus read-only Cypher. Output is TOON.
- **Digest**: per-file facts, the checks that ran after a file's last edit, the edits made after each run, and budgeting that keeps the facts that explain the PR.
- **The graph is an index, not a summary.** `why` lists every hunk of the target, marks the hunks that no captured edit explains, and includes each commit's message body. `outline` lists commits and says which ones have a body to expand.
- **Claims, notes and review**: claims about stale tests name the files edited later. Notes gain per-change provenance. The reviewer gets unverified files and unexplained hunks as leads to check, not as findings.
- **Drafters get pointed at the graph where they actually read**:
  - `prepare` output has a `next` step and a `graphOutline` (capped at 40 rows per section).
  - `evidence-notes.md` opens with the pointer and the outline.
  - `render` adds `graphHint` when no query ran.
- **Fails open**: if the engine can't start, the digest is still written, with a note.

### Fixes along the way

- When one shell command chained several checks (`bundle; tsc && bun test; eval`), only the test run was recorded. Each check is now its own run, and a failing exit status is no longer pinned on every check in the chain.
- `digest.json` cut the merge base to 12 characters, so `tracetoon source --revision base` always failed. It now keeps the full hash.

### Evaluation context

A prbench dev comparison (Codex and Claude drafters, 5 cases × 3 replicates) found **no benefit** from the first version of the graph. The causes it traced drove the follow-up commits: `why` returned only commit subjects and only some hunks, and drafters (Sonnet in particular) never queried the graph. After the pointer change, Sonnet went from 0 of 15 drafts with any query to 2 of 5. That is the motivation for embedding the outline directly. Whether the current version improves drafts has **not** been re-measured. `bun scripts/eval-graph.ts [--synthetic]` reports digest size and fact retention per budget, the cost of provenance lookups, and timings.

## Verification

- `bun run typecheck`: passed
- `bun run test`: 37 of 37 source test files passed (Bun 1.3.14, Linux)
- `bun scripts/cypherlite.ts check`: 4 vendored files match the pin
- `bun run build:check`: passed after rebundling. The last commit regenerates the bundle, which was stale: 14be3ce and ca6ac22 changed `src/` without rerunning `bun run bundle`.
- `test:bundled` and `test:compiled`: not run locally; left to CI, which runs the packaged contracts on every PR and platform.

title: Add a queryable evidence graph of how each PR was made
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR is meant to make the evidence graph "a proper feature integration, not just a partial integration" of Tracetoon. Each digest also builds `evidence-graph.json`, linking prompts to the edits made in their turn, edits to the diff hunks their lines survive in, runs to PR files edited after them, and commits to the sessions that made them.

## Design

The graph runs in-process on cypherlite v0.16.1 compiled to WebAssembly, pinned by hash in build-dependencies.json and rebuilt with `scripts/cypherlite.ts`, so no native modules are added; `buildManifest` calls `verifyCypherlite()` so a build stops when the vendored engine differs from its pin. `tracetoon query` answers named questions (outline, why, unverified, unexplained, stale, dead-ends, turn, pushback, schema) and non-writing Cypher, as TOON, capped at 60 rows per section unless `--all` is given. If the engine cannot start, the digest is written with a note. `assetsDir` moves to src/util/assets.ts and raster.ts re-exports it; `.prettierignore` skips src/graph/vendor/. Doctor, packaged contracts, docs, an offline benchmark (scripts/eval-graph.ts) and tests/graph.test.ts come with it.

## Consequences

- With relevance from the graph, budget trimming ranks runs by relevance and lets facts with more surviving lines keep more text; stale test claims name the later-edited files.
- When `graphLeads` are present, reviewers get unverified files and unexplained hunks as leads, to treat as places to look, not findings.
- `why` lists the target's hunks (marking those no captured edit explains) and each commit's message body; `outline` lists commits and which have a body.
- `prepare` output gains `next`, and `prepare --json` carries `graphOutline` as its third key. When a graph exists, evidence-notes.md opens with the same pointer and includes the outline right after it, at digest and again at render. The outline is capped at 40 rows per section and left out if the graph can't be read.
- When the run has a graph and no `tracetoon query` ran, `render` adds `graphHint`.
- The skill's graph step now applies to whoever drafts, not just a delegated drafter.
- For a chained shell command, the digest keeps a separate entry per non-test check with the output lines of its kind, merges several test-runner segments into one entry, and reads a non-zero exit in such a chain as unknown rather than as a failure. Previously one such command was folded into a single entry with another check's result line, and, per commit db53f4f, writers then claimed checks "were not run".

The bundle and WebAssembly binary are regenerated.

Commit ca6ac22 reports that pointing at the graph moved Sonnet only to 2 of 5 drafts with a query. CI results for the final head are not in the session logs.

title: feat(review): lean reviewer: review-packet --lean, review-findings.json, review import

## Summary

The full reviewer costs about 38% of each draft. Most of that goes to reading the workflow doc, the whole brief and the whole patch, then writing `review.json` by hand, which often ends up with a placeholder `agentId` or invalid refs. With the lean reviewer, the reviewer reads one packet and reports only findings. Tracetoon then writes the contract.

- **`tracetoon review-packet --lean --run <id> [--json]`** writes `review-packet.md`, which contains:
  - a fingerprint header and the title
  - the rendered body with line numbers (the generated Validation section is left out)
  - open limits, changes, commit messages, tests and requests, taken from the stored brief
  - a map from each hunk to the symbol that owns it
  - the diff: the whole reduced patch if it is ≤16000 chars, otherwise only the cited hunks, branching hunks and test assertion lines
- **`review-findings.json` v1 schema**, with validation that lists every needed fix.
- **`tracetoon review import --run <id> [--findings <path>] [--agent-id <id>]`** writes `review.json` v2, bound to the current review-input fingerprint:
  - the drafter is inline and the reviewer is delegated; placeholder ids are refused
  - brief refs and `path:line` resolve to diff refs
  - unknown refs are listed as warnings and don't fail the import
- **`references/reviewer-lean.md`**: the reviewer's whole instruction.
- The bundle (`dist/tracetoon.mjs`, `build.json`) is regenerated with `bun run bundle`.

New code: `src/commands/review.ts`, `src/contribution/leanReview.ts`, wired up in `src/cli.ts`. Tests are in `tests/review-lean.test.ts`.

title: Add a lean reviewer: one review packet in, findings JSON out
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
According to the commit message, the full reviewer pass cost about 38% of each draft, mostly spent reading the workflow doc, the whole evidence brief and the whole patch, and then hand-writing review.json, often with a placeholder agentId or invalid refs. This PR adds a lean reviewer that works from one packet, makes at most 3 location lookups, and reports findings rather than a contract; Tracetoon then writes the review contract itself. The work came from a session whose stated goal was a plan for faster, heavily parallel measurement runs, where tokens rather than raw speed are measured; a cheaper reviewer serves that token budget.

## Design

`tracetoon review-packet --lean --run <id>` writes review-packet.md: a fingerprint header, the title, the line-numbered rendered body with the generated Validation section elided, open limits, changes, commit messages, tests and requests from the stored brief, a map from hunks to their owning symbols, and the diff. A code comment says the packet holds what drove useful findings in measured reviews. The diff is shown whole when the reduced patch is at most 16000 characters; otherwise the packet keeps cited hunks, branching hunks and test assertions. Even when shown whole, test files are cut down to hunk headers and added assertion or test-title lines, and generated, lock and version files are left out. The reviewer's whole instruction lives in references/reviewer-lean.md.

The reviewer answers in review-findings.json (schema v1); schema errors are listed together, and a quote missing from the title or body is listed in a second step once the schema is valid. Quotes are matched exactly first, then loosely, ignoring case, markdown marks and whitespace. `tracetoon review import --run <id> [--findings <path>] [--agent-id <id>]` turns the findings into review.json v2 bound to the current review-input fingerprint. Import refuses placeholder-looking agent ids; CH, T and `path:line` refs become diff refs, commit refs stay commit refs, and unknown refs become warnings rather than errors. When there are no claim findings, import adds a supported claim on the title so the contract has at least one audited claim. Import marks the review incomplete when contributor guidance is not current or has requirements the lean review does not assess, when change-map.json is missing or a behavior group has no behaviorChecks, or when a comic is present. `evidenceExists` in src/contribution/review.ts is now exported so the importer can check refs.

## Consequences

Writing the contract moves from the reviewer to Tracetoon, so placeholder agent ids are refused at import, though other id strings pass unchecked. This PR does not itself measure the new reviewer's cost. tests/review-lean.test.ts covers packet layout for small and large diffs, findings validation, placeholder id detection, quote location, and an end-to-end import that binds review.json v2 to the fingerprint.

title: feat(brief): neighborhood evidence layout; render reports each brief-check finding once
body:
## Summary

Adds a **neighborhood layout** for the evidence brief, and stops `render` from repeating brief-check findings that the writer can't clear.

### Neighborhood brief layout (`feat(brief)`)
The brief can now be laid out as the graph's neighborhoods instead of TOON tables. Set it with `TRACETOON_BRIEF_LAYOUT=neighborhood`, which is the default on this branch. `toon` still produces the previous brief byte for byte.

- Each change block shows its requests (full text, once), its commits with each sentence's hunks (`→ H#`), and each changed file with its hunks, the requests behind them, and key changed lines (`- old ⇒ + new`).
- Hunks keep up to 24 key changed lines in the graph (`Hunk.code`). They can be cited as `H#` through a new hunks section in `briefParts`, so render checks them.
- Links from a sentence to a hunk work at hunk level and are conservative. A sentence links when it names the file, when it's one part of a list sentence, when a single code hunk shares words with it, or when `describedHunks` scores it above its tie margin.
- Blocks are packed into 2,112 evidence tokens (`TRACETOON_BRIEF_BUDGET`). Headers, requests, sentences and file lines are always kept. Code lines are added greedily by value per character. On big PRs, text is clipped and file lines are compacted to fit.
- Main code: `src/graph/neighborhood.ts` (new), `src/graph/queries.ts`, `src/graph/build.ts`, `src/graph/layout.ts`. The skill references (`quick-path.md`, `contribution-workflow.md`) are updated to match.

### Render repeats (`fix(render)`)
Codex graph-arm drafts ran up to 44 renders because render kept reporting findings the writer could not clear. One sentence that attributed a result to the commit message was flagged as a run claim 18 times. The goal request and change rows were reported as uncovered dozens of times.
- If an earlier render already reported a finding, render now lists it under "repeated" and doesn't block on it.
- A sentence tagged with the commit message, or naming it, is no longer treated as a run claim.

title: Receipt commands keep shell quoting and <repo> paths; reviewed brief path by default
body:
## Summary

Two changes:

### 1. Receipt commands keep shell quoting and show repo paths as `<repo>` (`fix(check)`)

`src/workflow/checks.ts`
- **Repo paths.** When a check receipt is recorded, each argument now has the repository root (and its realpath, if that differs) replaced with `<repo>` before scrubbing (`atRepo`). Before this, the scrubber just removed the root, so an absolute-path command looked the same as the relative-path one. In practice, a failed relative-path attempt and the absolute-path retry that passed showed up as the same command.
- **Quoting.** `receiptEvidence` now builds the `cmd` string with a new `shellJoin` instead of `command.join(' ')`. Arguments that contain spaces or shell characters are single-quoted, so `bash -c 'bun run typecheck && bun test'` comes out as a command you can type, not as a flattened string that means something else.
- `commandSha256` is still the hash of the original argv. Only the displayed form changes.

### 2. The reviewed brief path is the default when there is a brief (`feat(skill)`)

- `plugin/skills/tracetoon/SKILL.md`: new step **2b**. When `prepare --json` returns a brief, the host agent drafts `change-map.json`, `title.txt` and `body.md` itself. It runs the required checks once with `tracetoon check` and loops `render --check` (at most three rounds). Then one fresh independent reviewer writes `review.json` v2, followed by one correction round that the **same** reviewer confirms. The three-role path (researcher, drafter, reviewer) is now used only when the user asks for the most thorough PR. The quick path (2a) still needs an explicit request.
- `src/commands/digest.ts` (`graphNext`) and `src/commands/publish.ts` (render's next-step and lean-mode hints) now describe the new default.

## Tests

- `tests/evidence.test.ts`: new test for `shellJoin`. It covers quoting a `bash -c` script, leaving `<repo>/…` paths unquoted and escaping an embedded `'`.
- `tests/graph.test.ts`: the `prepare` next-step assertions now expect the reviewed brief path.

title: Shell-quote check receipt commands and make the reviewed brief path the default
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR fixes how check receipts record commands and makes the reviewed brief path the default way to write a PR from an evidence brief, as part of the request to "research the last findings, find the sweet spot, plan what is next" and then carry out that plan.

## Receipt commands

Commit 96457dabc19c notes that in the conf21 Terra confirmation, four of six accuracy flags were Tracetoon's own Validation lines.

Previously, receipts joined argv with spaces, losing the quoting around a `bash -c` script, and the scrubber stripped the repository root, so an absolute path and a relative path to the same file looked identical.

`receiptEvidence` now formats each command with a new `shellJoin`, which quotes an argument that is empty or contains a character outside word characters and `@%+=:,./<>-`, escaping embedded single quotes. `prepareCheck` passes each argument through `atRepo` before scrubbing, which replaces the repository root (and its resolved real path, when that differs) with `<repo>`. Because the replacement is textual, a sibling path that shares the root's prefix is rewritten too. Since `<` and `>` are left unquoted, an argument such as `<repo>/dist/x.mjs` appears bare in the receipt.

A new case in `tests/evidence.test.ts` pins `shellJoin` output for a `&&` script, a `<repo>` path and an embedded single quote.

## Default path with a brief

According to commit c194a028fe22, a step-back analysis found the full independent reviewer is what wins, while the separate researcher and drafter roles add little separable value and cost about 1x. SKILL.md gains step 2b: with a brief, the coordinator drafts the description itself and one fresh independent reviewer checks it, after the required checks are run once with `tracetoon check` and `render --check` is looped; one correction round is confirmed by the same reviewer. The commit message describes the same flow, including that the coordinator finds required checks itself. Previously, `graphNext` told the agent to take the full path, with a researcher, a drafter and a reviewer. `graphNext` and the `renderCmd` next-step messages now point to the reviewed brief path; the `graphNext` text offers the three-role path and the quick path as options on the user's request. The graph test expectations follow the new wording.

title: feat(review): review run --all, review merge, and the Review recheck setting
body:
## Summary

One command runs every planned reviewer pass and returns one merged list, so the drafter applies findings in a single edit pass and reviewer rechecks become optional.

- **`tracetoon review run --all`** runs one pass per lens, plus any general passes beyond the lens count. The passes run concurrently, and each has its own packet, reply, findings and reviewed-body files. Each pass is imported the same way as a single `review run`. On partial failure, the passes that succeeded are imported, the failed ones are named with the rerun command, and the command exits non-zero. A rerun skips passes already imported for the current body. `--all --recheck` resumes every pass (with `contested`, only passes that have rejected findings). `--note` passes rejections along.
- **`tracetoon review merge`** builds the same merged list from passes already imported, for use with the agent runner.
- **`review-findings-merged.md`**:
  - findings deduplicated by normalized or near-duplicate quote (omissions by evidence)
  - the strongest verdict kept
  - claims listed before omissions
  - the passes that raised each finding named on its line
  - capped at 12 findings
- **`Review recheck: once|contested|none`** is a new SKILL line, with a matching `prepare --review-recheck` option. It is stored in `review-plan.json` when it isn't `once`. The publish gate never needs a recheck. The next steps from prepare, render and review follow the setting.
- **SKILL step 2b**: one review command (or merge), one edit pass, and a recheck only if the setting asks for one. A single `review run` without `--lens` now also works when the plan asks for general passes beyond the lenses.

### Follow-ups added while preparing the PR
- **Deterministic merged-list order** (`src/commands/review.ts`): `writeMergedList` sorted passes by pass number. Under `--all` that is import order, which depends on which concurrent reviewer finishes first. This made the "runs every planned pass concurrently" test flaky (`[lens d, general 2, general]` vs `[lens d, general, general 2]`). Passes are now ordered by plan: lenses by letter, then general passes by slot, then by pass number.
- **`tests/review-run.test.ts` timeout**: each test spawns several CLI and fake-reviewer processes and took about 6 s on a loaded host, which is past bun's 5 s default. The file now uses `setDefaultTimeout(60_000)`, like the other subprocess-heavy test files.

## Testing
- `bun run typecheck`: passes.
- `bun run test`: **43/43 source test files pass**. Before the two follow-ups, `tests/review-run.test.ts` failed: 11 tests hit the 5 s timeout and 1 failed on the ordering above.
- `tests/review-run.test.ts`: 17/17 pass when run alone. The merged-list tests passed in 3 repeated runs after the ordering fix.
- Packaged suites (`test:bundled`, `test:compiled`) were not run locally and are left to CI, which runs them on every PR.

## Notes
- `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` is **not** regenerated. Main already has ~45 source commits since the last bundle refresh, so rebundling here would pull unrelated changes into this PR. Regenerate it in the next batch or release refresh.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The goal of this PR is to prepare the next code round of the drafting pipeline: reviewing a draft took one reviewer command per lens plus separate general reviewers, each with its own edit round and usually a recheck. This PR adds one command that launches the reviewers the plan requires and returns one merged list, so the drafter applies findings in a single edit pass and rechecks become optional.

Previously the SKILL told the drafter to invoke `tracetoon review run --run <id>` once per lens. SKILL step 2b now asks for one review command (or merge), one edit pass, and a recheck only per the setting line.

`tracetoon review run --all` launches one reviewer per lens plus the general reviewers beyond the lens count, concurrently, each slot with its own packet, reply, findings and reviewed-body files, and imports each the way a single `review run` is imported. When some slots break, it still imports the others, lists the broken slots with a command to retry them and returns an error status; without `--recheck`, that retry skips slots already imported for the current body unless `--fresh` is given. `tracetoon review merge` builds the same merged list from reviews imported by the agent runner.

The merged list, review-findings-merged.md, dedupes findings by normalized and near-duplicate quote (omissions without a quote by their evidence refs), keeps the strongest verdict, orders claims before omissions, names the source reviewers on each line and caps the list at 12; claims whose quote is missing from the current body are left out as already fixed. Identical normalized quotes match; otherwise a quote with fewer than three tokens is not treated as a near-duplicate.

A new `Review recheck: once|contested|none` SKILL line, also settable with `prepare --review-recheck`, shapes the suggested next step after review (it is not part of the publish gate); review-plan.json records it when it is not `once`. With `contested`, `--all --recheck` resumes only the reviewers with a rejected finding, meaning a claim they raised that is still verbatim in a body that changed since; under `once` or `none`, `--recheck` resumes every earlier reviewer. With `--recheck`, `--note <text>` hands the author's rejections to each reviewer being resumed. The next steps printed by prepare, render and review follow the setting. A single `review run` without `--lens` on a plan with lenses starts one general reviewer when the plan asks for more reviewers than lenses, and otherwise refuses and points to `--lens` and `--all`.

The new tests in tests/review-run.test.ts drive a fake codex from tests/fake-codex-review.ts, so they exercise the code around the reviewer rather than a real codex. tests/merge-findings.test.ts covers deduping and the cap, and tests/skill-settings.test.ts checks the step 2b wording. title: feat: add `tracetoon update` to upgrade in place
body:
## Summary

Adds `tracetoon update`, which upgrades an installed Tracetoon in place, so users no longer have to re-run the installer.

- **Lookup and verification:** reads the releases list, checks downloads against the release's SHA-256 checksums, and confirms the skill and runtime are the same build before changing anything.
- **Atomic-ish replace:** replaces the binary, comic assets, every installed skill copy and the hooks together. If any step fails, the old files are restored.
- **Options:**
  - `--check` only reports. Add `--exit-code` to exit with code 10 when a newer release exists.
  - `--channel stable|latest`: `stable` skips release candidates.
  - `--to <version>` installs a specific release, which is also how to roll back.
  - `TRACETOON_DISABLE_UPDATES=1` blocks the command.
- **Refuses** to replace a Claude Code plugin or bundle copy, a `TRACETOON_BIN` override, or a binary it didn't install. Plugin users are pointed to `/plugin marketplace update`.
- **Version ordering:** a semver comparator orders prerelease numbers numerically, so `rc.2` comes before `rc.10`.
- **Installers:** `install.sh` and `install.ps1` now write `install.json`, recording the install method, version, tag and path, so `update` knows which copy it owns.
- **Testing hook:** `TRACETOON_UPDATE_URL` points the lookup and downloads at a test server. `tests/update.test.ts` uses it.
- README update section rewritten. The bundle and `build.json` build identity are regenerated.

New code lives in `src/commands/update.ts` and `src/update/` (`release.ts`, `version.ts`, `layout.ts`, `apply.ts`).

title: feat: add `tracetoon update` to upgrade in place
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Tracetoon has no way to upgrade short of re-running `install.sh` or `install.ps1`; the goal here is an upgrade from the CLI without a reinstall. This PR adds a `tracetoon update` command that looks up published releases and installs the chosen one over the current copy.

## Design

`updateCmd` refuses to run when the `TRACETOON_DISABLE_UPDATES` variable is set to 1, rejects any `--channel` other than `stable` or `latest`, and defaults to `latest`, which includes release candidates while `stable` does not. With `--to <version>` it targets that exact release among the ones the lookup returns (from GitHub, the 30 most recent), which may be older, so it doubles as a rollback; without `--to` it does not move backwards and reports "up to date" when the picked release is not newer. `--check` reports without installing, and `--check --exit-code` exits 10 when a newer release exists; `--exit-code` has no effect without `--check`.

Release parsing skips drafts and tags that are not versions, and `pickRelease` takes the newest by publish time, using version order only to break ties. That version comparator orders candidates numerically, so `rc.2` sorts before `rc.10`, and a release outranks its own candidates. `TRACETOON_UPDATE_URL` points the lookup and downloads at a test server instead of GitHub, according to the commit message.

Before replacing anything, `updatable` checks that the running process is the binary the installer placed: it refuses when `TRACETOON_BIN` is set, when the executable's file name is not a `tracetoon` binary name (treated as a plugin or source bundle and pointed at `/plugin marketplace update`), or when it is some other `tracetoon` binary. Per the commit message, the install step in `src/update/apply.ts` verifies SHA-256 checksums and that the skill and runtime are one build, then replaces the binary, comic assets, installed skill copies and hooks, restoring the old files if a step fails. In the code, hooks are re-registered with `hook install` after the swap is final, so a failure there is not rolled back: the update succeeds and prints a manual `tracetoon hook install` step. On Windows the old exe is renamed aside rather than overwritten, and its removal may fail while in use, leaving a copy for the next update to clear.

## Consequences

Both installers now write an `install.json` receipt recording the method, version, tag and path; the scripts discard any error from that write (`|| true` in `install.sh`, an empty `catch` in `install.ps1`). The README documents the new command, and the bundle and build id are regenerated. The `install.ps1` change is Windows-only and the recorded runs were on linux/x64, so none shows that path running.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (Source test files: 50 passed, 0 failed (up to 4 fresh processes)).

Where to start: `updateCmd` in `src/commands/update.ts`, which owns the disable switch, channel handling, the `--check`/`--to` decisions and the call into `applyRelease`.

Feedback wanted: should a plain `tracetoon update` keep defaulting to the `latest` channel (release candidates included) until 1.0.0 ships, or default to `stable`?
