title: fix: recognise the VEX AIM's user serial port and write full buffers to it
body:
## Summary

Two fixes to make the VEX AIM's user (REPL/console) serial port work over USB.

**Recognise the AIM's user serial port** (`types_by_location()`)
- The AIM enumerates as a composite device with a UVC camera on interfaces 2 and 3, so its serial ports are interfaces 0 (system) and **4** (user), not 0 and 2 like the V5 Brain. Interface 4 previously hit the "Unknown location" branch and was dropped, so `find_devices()` returned the AIM with `user_port() == None` and `read_user()`/`write_user()` silently fell back to the system port.
- Interface 4 on the AIM (PID `0x0700`) is now classified as `User`.
- `types_by_location()` now returns `None` when it recognises nothing (it returned `Some(empty)` before), so the name-based fallbacks in `find_ports()` can actually run.

**Write the whole buffer in `write_user()`**
- On the user port, `write_user()` did a single `AsyncWrite::write()`, which may accept only part of the buffer, then reported that partial count and never flushed. It now uses `write_all()` + `flush()` and returns the full length, matching the system-port `send()` path.

## Tests

Added unit tests in `serial.rs` for AIM interfaces 0/4, the V5 Brain 0/2 layout (regression), and the unrecognised-ports → `None` case. The test helper feeds interface numbers the way each OS reports them, since `serialport` reports the CDC data interface (communication + 1) on macOS and `types_by_location()` subtracts 1 there.

⚠️ No Rust toolchain was available in the environment that prepared this PR, so `cargo test` / `cargo build` were **not run** locally. I checked by hand that the imports and `UsbPortInfo` fields the tests use are there (the `usbportinfo-interface` feature is enabled). Please let CI or a local `cargo test -p vex-v5-serial` confirm. title: fix(serial): recognise the VEX AIM's user port and write the full buffer in write_user
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR fixes the serial ports on VEX AIM devices, as requested: "submit the PR to the vex-v5-serial project for the bug with the serial ports on the vex aim devices".

## Problem

Previously, `types_by_location()` knew the V5 Brain layout, where interface 0 is the system port and interface 2 is the user port. The AIM enumerates as a composite device with a UVC camera on interfaces 2 and 3, so its two serial ports are interfaces 0 and 4. According to the commit message, interface 4 fell into the "Unknown location" branch and was dropped, so the AIM came back with no user port and user reads and writes silently went through the system-port fallback.

Separately, `write_user()` previously used a single `write()` on the user port, which may accept only part of the buffer, and returned that count without flushing.

## Design

- When the device PID is the AIM's (0x0700) and the location is interface 4, `types_by_location()` treats that port as the user port; Brain interfaces 0 and 2 keep their existing mapping.
- For any device where `types_by_location()` recognised no ports, it now returns `None` instead of `Some(empty)`; per the commit message, this lets the name-based fallbacks in `find_ports()` run.
- When a user port exists, `write_user()` uses `write_all()` followed by `flush()` and returns the full length; the commit message notes this matches the system-port `send()` path.

Unit tests cover the AIM layout, the Brain layout and unrecognised ports; their helper feeds interface numbers the way each OS reports them, because `serialport` reports the CDC data interface (communication + 1) on macOS and `types_by_location()` subtracts 1 there.

## Consequences and limits

On an AIM, interface 4 now maps to the user port, so user reads and writes go to it instead of the system-port fallback. The unit tests added here target port classification; none of them calls `write_user()`.

The change touches a macOS-specific branch (`cfg!(target_os = "macos")`), but the recorded test runs were on Linux, so the macOS path has not been seen running. CI results for the pushed head are not known yet.


Where to start: `types_by_location` in `packages/vex-v5-serial/src/serial.rs`, which owns the AIM user-port mapping and the `None` fallback.

Feedback wanted: is matching on PID 0x0700 plus interface 4 the right way to identify the AIM's user port, or should other AIM PIDs or firmware layouts be considered?

- **Truncation hint for `exec`**: when a run times out after ≥1500 bytes of stdout, the human output explains that the robot's USB buffer overflows past ~2 KB per burst. The JSON output gets `possible_output_truncation`.
- **Prebuilt Linux x86_64 binary** at `skill/vex-aim/bin/linux-x86_64/vexaim`, with `SHA256SUMS` (the checksum matches the committed binary).

title: vexaim: add snap command and truncation hint, plus CI build and API reference
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR lets the `vexaim` CLI save a frame from the AIM robot's camera, and warns when a timed-out program probably lost output, so an agent driving the robot can see what it sees and tell a quiet program from a clipped one.

## Design

`vexaim snap [-o FILE]` is a new subcommand backed by `snap::snap`. The robot's camera shows up as an ordinary USB webcam, so the command uses the `nokhwa` crate (native input backends) instead of the REPL. It lists cameras and keeps those whose name contains "aim"; if none match, it fails with the names it found and a hint to plug in the robot or grant camera access. The AIM exposes two video nodes of which one streams, so it moves to the next node when one fails to open, stream or yield a frame, requests 640x480 MJPEG, and keeps the last of eight frames while auto-exposure settles. If the camera delivers anything other than MJPEG it returns an error; otherwise `trim_jpeg` strips trailing zero padding and the JPEG is written to the given path, or to `vexaim-snap-<unix-time>.jpg` when no path is given. With `--json` it reports path, width, height and byte count.

`run_exec` changed too. Previously a timeout appended just "[timed out after Ns: program interrupted]" to the human output. Now, when a run times out and stdout is at least 1500 bytes, the human output adds a hint that the robot's USB buffer drops output past about 2 KB per burst, and the JSON output sets `possible_output_truncation`, a field that every exec JSON result now carries and that is false otherwise. Two unit tests cover `trim_jpeg`: zero padding after the end-of-image marker is dropped, and an unpadded JPEG is returned unchanged.

Alongside this:

- `skill/vex-aim/references/api.md` lists the REPL API names; it notes that the firmware exposes no signatures, so the signatures come from VEX's public AIM docs; each call is marked RAN (executed on a test robot) or DOC (not yet run), and the documented `robot.get_name()` is recorded as absent on this firmware.
- `.github/workflows/build.yml` installs libudev-dev on Linux, runs `scripts/setup-upstream.sh`, then builds release binaries and runs `cargo test` on push and manual dispatch across a Linux, Windows and macOS matrix and uploads them as artifacts. No run of the workflow appears in the session logs, and none of the recorded runs covered the Windows, macOS or arm64 paths; those runs were on linux/x64.
- `scripts/setup-upstream.sh` clones vexide/vex-v5-serial, checks out a pinned commit and applies the AIM patch with `git am`; it is a new helper that no recorded session ran, so it is reviewed from the diff alone.

title: Find AIM REPL on USB iface 4; 10/10 round trips; experimental upload tools
body:
## Summary

This PR finds the VEX AIM MicroPython REPL on **USB interface 4** and shows it answers reliably: **10/10 PING→PONG round trips**, about 50 ms each (min 50.2, max 50.3, mean 50.2 ms, on `/dev/ttyACM1`). It also adds some experimental file tools for the system port.

### REPL scripts (`tests/`)
- `capture.py`: logs everything received on a port, and can send lines after 4 s. The line ending is set by the `EOL` env var.
- `repl.py`: sends expressions with CRLF and prints what comes back.
- `pingpong.py`: runs N round trips and prints JSON. The robot prints `"AIM_AGENT_V1 "+"PONG"` (built by joining two strings), so the script can tell the robot's output apart from the echo of what it sent.

### Probe binaries (`crates/vexaim-probe`)
- `dirlist` (**read-only**): lists the files for each `FileVendor`. It sends only FILE_DIR and FILE_DIR_ENTRY.
- `aimload run|stop`: sends FILE_LOAD on vendor User. `stop` uses `"null"` as the file name, the same way VAIMRC-Console does.
- `aimupload` (**EXPERIMENTAL**): writes `slot_N.ini` and `slot_N.bin` to vendor User. The file format is a guess based on cargo-v5 PR#22 and VAIMRC-Console. It does not run the program.
- Turns on the `file-commands` feature of `vex-v5-serial`.

### Evidence and references
- `build/run1.log` and `build/run2.log`: raw captures. Run 1 sent lines with no CR: the input was echoed but nothing ran. Run 2 sent CRLF and got real REPL `NameError` tracebacks back.
- `build/pingpong-run1.json`: the 10/10 result. `build/main.mpy` is a small compiled test file.
- `refs/VAIMRC-Console` and `refs/aim-ai`: reference repos added as gitlinks.

## Checks
- `python3 -m py_compile tests/*.py`: passes.
- `cargo check`: **not run**. This environment has no Rust toolchain, and the crate's path dependency (`../../upstream/packages/vex-v5-serial`) is not in the checkout.
- Hardware results were recorded on a real robot and could not be re-run here.

## Notes for reviewers
- `refs/*` are added as submodule gitlinks, but there is no `.gitmodules`, so a fresh clone cannot initialise them. Either add a `.gitmodules` or swap them for plain URLs in the docs.
- `build/` artifacts and logs are committed on purpose as evidence. Move them if you'd rather keep them out of the tree.
- `aimupload` and `aimload run` write to and run things on the robot. Only use them on a robot you have to yourself.

title: Add AIM REPL serial test scripts and experimental file-transfer probes
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The purpose of this PR is captured in its commit message: "Find AIM REPL on USB iface 4; 10/10 round trips; experimental upload tools". It adds small tools for reaching the VEX AIM robot's Python REPL over USB serial, a recorded round-trip result, and Rust probes that exercise the vendor file protocol.

**REPL scripts.** `tests/repl.py` sends each argument line with CRLF and prints what comes back, using `drain` to collect input for a fixed window. `tests/capture.py` logs everything received and, when lines are given, sends them once after four seconds. `tests/pingpong.py` sends Ctrl-C to get a clean prompt, then runs N round trips (default 10) via `rt`, which writes `print("AIM_AGENT_V1 "+"PONG")` so the echoed command can't be mistaken for output, and counts a trip as ok only when the joined reply and `>>> ` prompt appear within the timeout. The checked-in `build/pingpong-run1.json` records 10 of 10 ok trips on `/dev/ttyACM1` at about 50 ms each, and `build/run2.log` shows a bare `PING` raising `NameError`, i.e. the port speaks a Python REPL.

**Rust probes.** Enabling the `file-commands` feature of `vex-v5-serial` lets three binaries use the file protocol:
- `dirlist` is read-only: it sends only directory count/entry requests for six vendors and prints up to 64 entries each (name, size, load address, CRC, metadata), printing an error line in place of any entry it cannot read.
- `aimload run|stop` sends a file-load action on vendor User; `stop` uses the name "null" to match VAIMRC-Console, and `run` defaults to `slot_1.bin` when no name is given.
- `aimupload` writes `slot_N.ini` (name "AIM Agent Bridge", zero-based slot N-1) and `slot_N.bin` to vendor User in QSPI flash and leaves program launch to `aimload`, with the bin's extension type `Vm` unless the third argument is `bin`. Its header comment marks it experimental, for instructor-approved use on an exclusive robot, and describes the format as a hypothesis based on cargo-v5 and VAIMRC-Console.

VAIMRC-Console and aim-ai are pinned as submodules under `refs/` for reference. Generated artifacts (`build/main.mpy`, logs, `Cargo.lock`) are included too.


Where to start: `main` in `crates/vexaim-probe/src/bin/aimupload.rs`, which builds the slot ini and uploads both files.

Feedback wanted: should the upload binary stay in this crate while its file format is still a hypothesis, or move behind a feature flag?

This PR records the results of the unplug/replug hardware tests and the kicker retest done with the user at the robot, and fixes the two error messages those tests showed were misleading. This PR packages the `vexaim` CLI as an agent skill meant to let a Goose or Claude agent control a USB-connected VEX AIM robot without VEXcode, and makes `vexaim doctor` report the robot's interpreter version in a form an agent can explain correctly.

## Design

The skill lives in `skill/vex-aim/`: `SKILL.md` tells the agent to start with `vexaim doctor`, then send Python with `vexaim exec`, and lists known pitfalls (output buffer overflow above about 2 KB, constants that need `from vex_globals import *`, which `exec` already imports unless `--no-preamble` is set, the fixed x/y position frame, the missing `robot.get_name()`). A `linux/` folder carries a udev rule and an installer that needs sudo so ModemManager leaves the robot's port alone. The vendored `refs/` checkouts are untracked and `.claude/` is ignored.

Previously `doctor` reported only `sys.version` under a `micropython` key; it now reports `micropython_core` (from `sys.implementation.version`) and `python_compat` (the language level `sys.version` claims), and the skill tells the agent to give both when asked which Python the robot runs.

title: AGENTS.md: handle the no-robot case and other gaps found by a cold run
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR to the agent setup runbook (`AGENTS.md`) closes gaps that showed up when the student prompt was re-run against the merged repo and release: the commit message says a fresh agent completed the install but flagged no stop condition for diagnostic retries, no guidance for when the robot cannot be reached, and a udev step pointing at a path that does not exist for single-agent installs.

Previously, per the commit message, the runbook had no stop condition for diagnostic retries and its udev step referenced a path missing for single-agent installs.

What changes in the runbook:

- The udev step now runs `sh install.sh --udev` from the repository root instead of `sh ~/.agents/skills/vex-aim/linux/install-udev.sh`, and gives a sample permission question explaining that the modem manager disturbs the USB connection for about 25 seconds after each plug-in, that the rule only affects the VEX AIM, and that it needs sudo.
- A new "If the diagnostic does not say `ready`" section: on Linux check `lsusb | grep 2888:0700` first; with no output the agent cannot fix it and asks the student to check the power switch, the USB data cable that came with the robot, a direct connection with no hub, and a re-plug. Then wait about 30 seconds (a first failure after plugging in is normal on Linux without the udev rule) and re-run `doctor` at most 3 times before handing back. When the robot is visible but `doctor` still fails, the agent reads the `fix:` lines and `docs/troubleshooting.md`, and a sandboxed agent (for example a Flatpak Goose) needs a non-sandboxed install.
- The agent must never invent a battery level: when the robot cannot be reached it reports what `doctor` printed, gives no battery number, and still finishes with the new-session step.
- It lists the tools the installer needs (`sh`, `curl` or `wget`, `tar`, `sha256sum` or `shasum`; PowerShell 5.1+ on Windows) so the agent can tell the student which one is missing.

The change is documentation only; the installer and `vexaim` code are untouched by this diff.


Where to start: the "If the diagnostic does not say `ready`" section and Step 5 in `AGENTS.md`, which own the retry limit and the no-battery reporting.

CI results for the pushed head are not yet known.

title: Add fast contact play and reliable stationary tag search (0.5.1)
body:
## Summary
Release 0.5.1: fast contact play and reliable stationary tag search.

- **Stationary tag search**: `find`, `approach`, `deliver` and named vision macros now take brief stationary native-camera readings at eight viewpoints, not continuous rotation. Cargo acquisition is still a quick continuous sweep.
- **Fast contact mode**: `behaviors.configure(verification="contact", tag_turn_dps=90)` opts into fast play. It skips the diagnostic retention reverses, the repeated possession gates and the host camera round trips. Result evidence marks completion as assumed, and it does not invent native attachment or release confirmation. The default stays `verification="vision"`. Missing targets, transport errors, cancellation and whole-activity deadlines still stop the sequence.
- **Short native moves** now leave a margin for acceleration and status reporting, and still return as soon as the move completes.
- Version bumped to 0.5.1 (VERSION, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock). Updated README, device-commands, hardware-notes, release notes and the bundled skill (`SKILL.md`, `references/behaviors.md`).

## Testing
- `python3 dev/test_behaviors.py`: 32 tests pass. They cover stationary-only tag decoding, missing targets, false-negative possession, assumed placement, and cancellation/deadlines.
- `python3 dev/check-release.py`: release inputs and skill/site links are valid for 0.5.1.
- All other `dev/test_*.py` pass except `test_ble_feasibility.py` (needs `bleak`) and `test_turn_frames.py` (needs `cv2`). Those modules aren't installed in this environment, so these two tests didn't run.
- Rust build/tests and installer tests weren't run here because `cargo` isn't available. CI will run them.
- Tests use simulated radios only. **Full hardware acceptance of the new contact mode hasn't been done yet** (see `docs/hardware-notes.md`).

title: Add fast contact play and reliable stationary tag search
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR wraps a working robot behavior into the project so kids can use it, with a faster, more trusting play mode: camera checks and stop-and-think pauses suit testing, but a kid's run should assume the pickup worked and keep moving. Implementing that plan, version 0.5.1 adds stationary tag search and opt-in contact-based play.

**Contact play.** `configure` gains `verification` (`'vision'` or `'contact'`, default `'vision'`) and `tag_turn_dps` (defaults to `turn_dps`, capped at 150 DPS), and rejects other verification values. Under `'contact'`, capture stops once native possession is reported without a camera confirmation, a contact move that hits its time limit returns instead of raising, and `collect` reports `evidence: 'contact_assumed'` with `collected: None` when possession was not observed. `collect` and `deliver` results gain `completed: True`. With `'contact'`, delivery skips the camera entry check only when the same activity already collected that cargo, skips the pre-placement check, and does not raise on an unconfirmed release; it returns `place_assumed` with `delivered: None` unless possession was seen before placing and release after. Under `'contact'`, the approach to a tag skips the abort that fires after 600 ms without native possession. Previously, a delivery raised `release_not_confirmed` whenever the camera could not confirm release. With the default `'vision'`, those checks stay in place.

**Stationary tag search.** A code comment says a continuous sweep missed a tag that stationary views then found on a real robot. When `find` targets a tag, it hands off to `find_tag`, which stops, waits, samples the detector up to three times, then turns 45° at `tag_turn_dps`, for up to eight views; the 20 s budget is checked after each view, so the last view can run past it. Tag reacquisition also pauses 300 ms before each look. `motion` raises its time limit to at least 1.5 s; it remains a maximum, not a delay.

The hardware notes record that a final hardware run of the 0.5.1 source did not reacquire the blue barrel and that full hardware acceptance of the new mode is pending. Tests in `dev/test_behaviors.py` cover stationary views in both directions, the bounded search when the marker is absent, contact play continuing when held cargo vanishes, contact mode still refusing missing targets, and the shared deadline. CI results for the final head were not available when this was written. These tests drive simulated robot objects, not hardware. README, skill and docs describe the new mode, alongside a version bump and regenerated lockfile.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `python3 -m unittest discover -s dev -p test_behaviors.py` (Ran 32 tests in 0.378s), `python3 dev/check-release.py`.

Where to start: `find_tag` in `cli/vexaim/src/behaviors.py` (stationary views and their view/time bound).

Feedback wanted: should contact mode report `collected: None` / `delivered: None` when unconfirmed, or would `True` with an `evidence` field be easier for kids' programs to handle?

title: Add Illustrator 2026 and Photoshop 2026 application templates
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR adds WinApps application templates for Adobe Illustrator 2026 and Adobe Photoshop 2026, so users running the 2026 releases in their Windows VM can get desktop shortcuts and file associations for them alongside the existing per-version Adobe templates.

## Design

Each template is a new `apps/<name>/` folder with an `info` file and an `icon.svg`, following the layout of the existing `photoshop-2025` and `illustrator-2024` templates. Compared with those, the new `info` files keep the categories (`WinApps;Adobe`), MIME types (`image/vnd.adobe.photoshop;` and `application/illustrator;`) and system icon names, and change the display name, the `FULL_NAME` (also used as the window class) and the version number in the executable path, giving `C:\Program Files\Adobe\Adobe Photoshop 2026\Photoshop.exe` and `C:\Program Files\Adobe\Adobe Illustrator 2026\Support Files\Contents\Windows\Illustrator.exe`.

The `icon.svg` files are identical copies of the `photoshop-2025` and `illustrator-2024` icons, so no new artwork is introduced.

## Consequences

The templates assume Adobe keeps its install folder naming for the 2026 releases; if the real install path differs, the template will not point at the right executable. Both new templates register the same MIME types as the older Photoshop and Illustrator templates, so a machine with several versions installed can end up with more than one handler for `.psd` and `.ai` files.


## AI disclosure

The commit and this description were prepared with AI assistance (Claude), and the description was checked against the diff.

Where to start: `apps/photoshop-2026/info`, whose `WIN_EXECUTABLE` names the Photoshop 2026 executable.

Feedback wanted: can someone with a 2026 install confirm both executable paths, especially Illustrator's `Support Files\Contents\Windows` subfolder?

title: Use SDL FreeRDP client for full desktop mode on Wayland
body:
## Summary

On Wayland sessions (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`), `winapps windows` (the full Windows desktop view) now uses the SDL FreeRDP client, which runs natively on Wayland, instead of `xfreerdp` under XWayland. RemoteApp launches (`manual`, `check`, and app names) still use the existing `xfreerdp` path.

## Changes (`bin/winapps`)

- `waGetFreeRDPCommand` now takes the launch mode. When the mode is `windows` and the session is Wayland, it looks for these clients in order:
  1. `sdl-freerdp3`
  2. `sdl3-freerdp`
  3. `sdl-freerdp`
  4. the FreeRDP Flatpak (`flatpak run --command=sdl-freerdp com.freerdp.FreeRDP`, which also sets `RDP_FLATPAK=1`)
- If none of these is found, it falls back to the existing `xfreerdp` → `xfreerdp3` → Flatpak `xfreerdp` lookup.
- The final "command exists" check also accepts the Flatpak `sdl-freerdp` command.
- An explicit `FREERDP_COMMAND` in the user's config still takes precedence, as before.
- The main script passes `"$1"` to `waGetFreeRDPCommand`.

## Notes for reviewers

- The full-desktop launch still passes `/wm-class:"Microsoft Windows"` and `+dynamic-resolution`. Please confirm that the SDL client versions you care about accept these options, or ignore them without failing.
- The Wayland Flatpak branch doesn't check that FreeRDP is version 3 or later; the `xfreerdp` Flatpak fallback does.

## Testing

- `bash -n bin/winapps`: passes
- `shellcheck -S warning bin/winapps`: no findings
- I couldn't test with a real Wayland session, SDL FreeRDP client or Windows VM here.

title: Use SDL FreeRDP client for full desktop mode on Wayland
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
On Wayland sessions, this PR prefers the SDL FreeRDP client (including the FreeRDP Flatpak) for the full Windows desktop view, which the author adopted for better performance. According to the author, RemoteApp/RAIL support in the SDL client is not fully implemented, so this change is limited to the full desktop (`windows`) mode and app launches keep the existing `xfreerdp` path. It is kept small and easy to diff for upstream, and it covers the versioned and unversioned SDL binary names plus the FreeRDP Flatpak.

Previously, `waGetFreeRDPCommand` checked for `xfreerdp` first when `FREERDP_COMMAND` was empty, then fell back to the Flatpak's `xfreerdp`.

## Design

`waGetFreeRDPCommand` now receives the first script argument. When `FREERDP_COMMAND` is unset, the argument is `windows` and `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` is `wayland`, it tries `sdl-freerdp3`, then `sdl3-freerdp`, then `sdl-freerdp`, then, if the `flatpak` command exists and the `com.freerdp.FreeRDP` Flatpak is installed, `flatpak run --command=sdl-freerdp com.freerdp.FreeRDP` (setting `RDP_FLATPAK=1`, which existing code later in the script reads). The existing `xfreerdp` check is now additionally gated on `FREERDP_COMMAND` still being empty; the `xfreerdp3` and Flatpak `xfreerdp` fallbacks were already gated that way, so none of them run once an SDL client is chosen, and all of them run as before when no SDL candidate is found or the conditions don't hold. The final validity check also accepts the Flatpak SDL command string, so the configured `RDP_FLAGS` are appended to the SDL command the same way as for `xfreerdp`.

## Consequences

- A user-set `FREERDP_COMMAND` still takes precedence; the SDL detection runs when it is empty.
- Any script argument other than `windows`, including RemoteApp launches, and non-Wayland sessions keep resolving to `xfreerdp` as before.
- Unlike the `xfreerdp` path, the SDL candidates are not checked for a FreeRDP major version of 3 or newer, so an unversioned `sdl-freerdp` is assumed to be suitable.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- `shellcheck bin/winapps`: passed, run on the submitted content.
- `pre-commit run --files bin/winapps`: could not run in this environment (transport 'https' not allowed); it got no result on the code.
- `shfmt -d -i 4 -ci -s bin/winapps`: could not run in this environment (- dprint "ERROR: FREERDP VERSION 3 IS NOT INSTALLED. EXITING."); it got no result on the code.

Where to start: `waGetFreeRDPCommand` in `bin/winapps`, which owns the Wayland desktop SDL client selection.

Feedback wanted: should the unversioned `sdl-freerdp` candidate be version-checked like `xfreerdp`, or is assuming it is FreeRDP 3 acceptable on the distributions you package for?

title: test: walk every authored book step
body:
## Summary

Adds a full-book walk: a harness that runs every authored step of every book through the compiled CLI, in persistent per-book workspaces, and smoke-launches the graphical programs. It also fixes the CLI bugs the walk turned up.

### Book walk harness
- `scripts/walk-books.ts` (`bun run test:books`) runs each step in order against the built binary and writes `test-results/book-walk/report.json`. Flags: `--binary`, `--book`, `--from`, `--report`, `--skip-smoke`, `--keep-workspace`.
- New reusable workflow `.github/workflows/book-walk.yml`. It installs the JDK, Maven, Python with pygame-ce and Pillow, the JUnit console, and Xvfb/xdotool, builds the binary, runs the walk under `xvfb-run`, and uploads the report.
- `ci.yml` calls the workflow, and `release.yml` now needs it to pass before `release`.
- The Dockerfile test image gets the same GUI runtimes.

### CLI fixes
- **Project checkpoints (`run`)**: when a scaffolded project moves to a new checkpoint, files recorded for an earlier checkpoint are now removed if they are unchanged. If the learner has edited one, `run` stops with `checkpoint_conflict` and leaves the file alone. Stale ownership records are dropped. Files removed by `clean` are forgotten too.
- **`GeneratedFileStore`**: adds `recordsUnder(root)` and `forget(path)`.
- **`replay execute`**:
  - When a command doesn't match, the JSON output now includes `command`, `timedOut`, `stdout` and `stderr`, so you can see why.
  - New `--relax-output` flag skips the exact stdout/stderr comparison. It only works when `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK=1` is set, so only the harness can use it.
- **Replay `rm` shortcut**: it now only fires for a single plain or quoted argument, so a script like `rm a b` falls through to the shell.
- **Native learn**: when a program fails, its output is now shown, both as a TUI card and as plain text.

### Content
- `@aifirst/content` is pinned to commit `57ef4bc` (embedded pack 2.0.1). The Java chapter 6 eco-mode step now cleans up `ThermostatApp.java`.
- Version bumped to 0.13.2.

## Testing
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json`: passes.
- `bun test` on the touched suites (`book-walk-workflow`, `generated-files`, `native-learn`, `replay-flow`, `run`): 72 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `run.test.ts › book scoping › never hands a Python reader a Java exercise`, which hits bun's 5 s default timeout. It fails the same way on `main` in this environment, so this branch didn't cause it.
- I didn't run the full book walk (`bun run test:books`) or the full `bun run check` locally. The walk needs the GUI and book runtimes, and the new `book-walk` CI job will run it.

title: Walk every authored book step through the compiled CLI in CI
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A reader hit a failure on Java exercise 6-05 that the existing per-sample checks did not catch, and the request was to "build a harness that runs through every sample in both books in order and fix any bugs that come out of the testing". Isolated verification proves each sample works alone; this PR adds an ordered pass that catches state left behind by earlier exercises in a shared reader workspace.

**Design.** `scripts/walk-books.ts` drives the compiled `aifirst` binary through each book's steps in document order, in one persistent workspace per book, and writes a JSON report; it accepts `--binary`, `--report`, `--book`, `--from`, `--skip-smoke` and `--keep-workspace`, and exits non-zero on a failed step, a failed graphical smoke or a version mismatch; after a failed step, the rest of that book is recorded as not run. Steps that launch an external program are replayed with relaxed output matching, and real Xvfb window smokes are limited to two graphical apps. A reusable `book-walk.yml` workflow installs the learner runtimes, runs the walk and uploads the report even on failure; `ci.yml` calls it, and the release job now also needs it.

Changes to existing code:
- `prepareExerciseFiles` in `run.ts` now reconciles a shared project: when a scaffold has a project root, tracked generated files the new exercise does not want are deleted and forgotten when they still match their recorded content, while a file the learner changed stops the run with a `checkpoint_conflict` error and is left alone, via the new `recordsUnder` and `forget` methods; `recordsUnder` returns no records when the store cannot be read.
- `replay` gains `--relax-output`, which is rejected as a bad option unless `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK=1` is set, and still requires the captured exit code.
- The portable shell's `rm` handling in `executor.ts` accepts a single quoted or bare argument, normalizing backslashes (the test covers removing more than one file).
- Previously the native learning UI put the result content or "Failed" in the tool card; for a failed result it now shows the command details via the new `renderExecutionFailure`.
- The chapter-6 Java step gains a `clean` list removing `src/main/java/ThermostatApp.java`.

The Dockerfile, `.gitignore` (ignoring `/test-results/book-walk/`), package version 0.13.2 are updated, the embedded pack version moves from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1, and `bun.lock` is regenerated.

**Limits.** The Windows-specific branches in `walk-books.ts` and `generatedFiles.ts` are unexercised on Windows. The new workflows have not been run in CI in the recorded work.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content and, on separate lines, the checks recorded in the session logs while the change was made.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`.
- `bun test`: failed (559 pass, 3 fail, Ran 599 tests across 63 files. [291.95s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.
- `bun scripts/walk-books.ts --binary bin/aifirst-linux-x64 --report test-results/book-walk/report.json`: passed (PASS book walk: 163/163 steps, 2/2 graphical smokes. Report: <local path>) in the session logs. An earlier run of `npx -y bun@1.4.0 test test/generated-files.test.ts test/run.test.ts test/native-learn.test.ts test/replay-flow.test.ts …` failed (69 pass, 1 fail).

Where to start: `prepareExerciseFiles` in `src/commands/run.ts`, which decides which previously generated files are obsolete.

Feedback wanted: is gating every PR on the full ordered walk an acceptable CI cost, or should PRs run a subset and releases the full walk?

title: fix: use Homebrew for Maven on immutable Linux
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
On Bazzite, starting the `java-11-01` exercise fails when it installs Maven. The CLI picks `dnf`, and Fedora Atomic images reject it with "Fedora Atomic images utilize rpm-ostree instead". The goal of this PR is to detect an immutable distribution and install Maven through Homebrew there instead.

Previously, on Linux `systemDependencyInstallPlan` chose APT, DNF or Alpine apk depending on which tool it found, so an rpm-ostree system that ships `dnf` got a DNF plan.

A new `isImmutableLinux` helper returns true when the platform is Linux and either `/run/ostree-booted` exists or `rpm-ostree` is on PATH. `systemDependencyInstallPlan` now runs that check before the APT/DNF/apk branches. If it returns true and `brew` is on PATH, the function returns a "Homebrew (immutable Linux)" plan that runs `brew install maven` using the resolved brew path, and that plan installs only Maven. If `brew` is missing, it returns no plan rather than falling through to `dnf`. Like `isImmutableLinux`, the function now also accepts an `exists` parameter, so tests can fake the filesystem check the same way they already fake `which`.

When no plan is found, `installDependencies` reports a failure. If all the missing dependencies are the `mvn` system command and the machine is immutable Linux, its message tells the user to install Homebrew, put `brew` on PATH and retry. Otherwise it keeps the generic "Install … and retry." text. This message check uses the real host probes, and none of the new tests cover it.

The manual verification checklist in `docs/learn-verification.md` now has a step for rpm-ostree systems: confirm Homebrew is chosen ahead of `dnf`, and that `dnf` doesn't run when Homebrew is missing. The package version is bumped to 0.10.3.

The new tests in `test/dependencies.test.ts` cover both detection signals, the Homebrew plan when `dnf` and `sudo` are also present, and the no-plan result without Homebrew, all using fake `which` and `exists` functions. The earlier "builds native Maven installation plans" test doesn't pass `exists`, so its APT/DNF expectations depend on whether the host has `/run/ostree-booted`. title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
## Summary

Claude Code hooks and skill commands no longer depend on `aifirst` being on Claude Code's inherited `PATH`. On Windows, a Windows Terminal, VS Code, or Claude Code process that was already running keeps the PATH it had before the PowerShell installer ran. In that state the bare `aifirst replay hook` command fails.

- `skill install --claude` now writes a launcher, `~/.claude/skills/aifirst/aifirst-cli.sh`, that `exec`s the current binary. When run from source under Bun, it uses Bun plus `src/index.ts`. Native Windows paths are converted to Git Bash form (`C:\…` → `/c/…`), and arguments are shell-quoted.
- The `UserPromptSubmit` replay hook calls `bash '<launcher>' replay hook` and carries a marker comment (`# aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1`). The legacy bare-command hook is still recognised, so existing installs migrate in place.
- `SKILL.md` and the slash commands render every CLI invocation through the launcher command.
- `claudeEntries()` takes the command prefix as a parameter. `allowlist` replaces legacy `Bash(aifirst …:*)` entries with launcher-based ones, `revoke` removes both forms, and the book-mode pre-approval check uses the launcher form.
- Docs (`docs/integrations/replay.md`) explain the launcher, how to migrate (`aifirst skill install --claude`, or the full `aifirst.exe` path on Windows), and which installer to use on each platform.

## Testing

- `tsc -p tsconfig.json`: passes.
- `bun test test/agents.test.ts test/permissions.test.ts test/upgrade.test.ts`: 69 pass, 0 fail. This includes new tests for path conversion, quoting, the launcher script, hook migration and legacy allowlist replacement.
- Full `bun test`: 444 pass, 37 skip (live and E2E tests gated by env vars), 1 fail.

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
On Windows, the Claude Code `UserPromptSubmit` hook could not find `aifirst`, because an already-running terminal, VS Code or Claude Code process can keep the `PATH` from before the PowerShell installer ran. This PR stops the Claude Code integration from looking up `aifirst` on the inherited `PATH`, for the hook as well as the instructions and permissions, by installing a stable Claude-owned Bash launcher that delegates to the current `aifirst` executable.

Previously the hook was the bare command `aifirst replay hook`, and the permission rules and generated skill instructions also named bare `aifirst`.

**Design.** `install` now writes `aifirst-cli.sh` into the Claude skill folder, which `exec`s the current executable with its arguments. `claudeCliCommand` renders `bash '<launcher>'` (so `bash` itself, on Windows Claude's Git Bash, is still resolved normally), and that command is used for the replay hook, the rendered `SKILL.md` and command files, and the `Bash(...)` permission entries. On `win32`, `bashPath` turns drive paths like `C:\...` into `/c/...` for Git Bash; on other platforms it just normalises slashes. `shellQuote` wraps each argument in single quotes so spaces and apostrophes don't allow shell expansion. When running under Bun from a `src/index.*` entrypoint, `currentCliArgv` keeps that entrypoint in the launcher; for a compiled binary (or any other entry) the launcher calls just the executable. The launcher records the executable path at install time, so if `aifirst` moves it needs a fresh `skill install`. The generated skill also gives platform-specific install instructions instead of sending Windows users to `install.sh`.

**Consequences.** Existing installs migrate when the skill is refreshed with `aifirst skill install --claude`, following the chosen migration approach: install rewrites the launcher, skill, command files and replay hook. The hook is recognised either by the legacy command or by a `# aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1` marker, so a reinstall replaces the old entry. When permissions are granted, the grant swaps legacy bare-command entries for the launcher form and leaves unrelated entries alone, and `revokePermissions` removes both forms. Book mode's pre-approval check and the permission status check look for the launcher-form entries, so an install holding just the legacy entries reports them as missing until it is refreshed. The replay docs explain the launcher, the migration command and the PowerShell fallback path.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`, `bun test` (445 pass, 0 fail, Ran 482 tests across 47 files. [148.17s]).

Where to start: `install` in `src/agents/claude.ts`, which writes the launcher and renders the skill and command files with the launcher command.

Feedback wanted: is the `bash '<launcher>'` prefix in permission entries the right granularity, or should the allowlist match more loosely so moving the skill folder doesn't invalidate it?

title: Improve learner replay display and run captured replays portably on Windows
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The purpose of this PR, per its commit "feat: improve learner replay experience", is a clearer replay view for learners and captured replays that run on Windows without external bash. The work continues the request "Continue".

**Reading a replay.** Replay operations and status events can now carry a `display` record (tool name, description, command), so the learner view can show what tool a step stands for instead of a raw command. Code longer than 40 lines is collapsed and `e` expands it (in the TUI, the latest collapsed block); tool calls and results are drawn as cards and code panels are line-numbered, and replies that carry `nativeBlocks` render status and text blocks separately. Previously the responder joined trailing events into one text string per segment; it now keeps them as typed blocks, and returns the reply unchanged when there are none. While the TUI waits for the learner to return from a document (`waitForDocumentReturn`), up/`k`, down/`j`, PageUp and PageDown scroll it and Enter or Esc returns. After a read-only prompt finishes typing, the learner presses Enter to continue; `pauseForEnter` waits on the TUI when one is active, returns without waiting when the terminal is not interactive, and treats an aborted readline as an interrupt. Choosing exit at that prompt ends the replay, and back re-shows it.

**Running a replay portably.** When a command operation's `portableCommand` starts with `<python>`, the executor substitutes the selected Python launcher; when it starts with `<shell>`, the async executor runs the script through Bun's shell in the operation's working directory rather than an external bash. With no Python runtime, a `<python>` command reports exit 127 and "Python 3 is unavailable." A new `timeoutMs` field bounds a spawned command (the `<shell>` path does not apply it), and a command with no exit status reports 124 when it timed out and 127 otherwise. For an operation marked `expectedTimeout`, `replayOperationFailed` returns true when the command's `timedOut` flag is not set. `nativeReplayOperation` replaces captured pygame window launches with a portable compile check. The `replay` command now awaits `executeReplayAsync`. The replay test fixtures and drivers were updated to match, including a test that executes the complete captured Save the Duckling timeline without external bash, and a test that opens progress and command reference as dismissible Home screens, and the package version goes to 0.10.5.

**Consequences.** A new `windows-duckling-replay` CI job targets `windows-latest`, installs Python 3.12 with pygame-ce and Pillow, and runs the Duckling test in portable mode. The recorded runs were on linux/x64, so none shows the Windows path, and no run of the workflow is in the session logs. title: fix: defer macOS setup outside piped installer

## Summary

On macOS, `curl … | bash` followed by `aifirst init </dev/tty` leaves guided setup unable to read input, because Bun can't poll stdin that was reopened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495). Running `aifirst init` directly works, because it inherits the real `/dev/ttysNNN` device.

- **`install/install.sh`**: on Darwin, skip the in-pipe setup and tell the user to run `aifirst init` in a new terminal. Linux behavior is unchanged.
- **`README.md`**: describe the extra macOS step.
- **Regression test** (`install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh` + `install/fixtures/macos_installer_tty_driver.py`): runs the real installer through a pipe inside a PTY. A fake `curl` serves the just-built binary and its checksum. The test then runs `aifirst init` directly and checks three things:
  - the installer prints the deferral message
  - the setup prompt appears only after the installer exits
  - the direct init accepts input
- **CI**: the test runs on the macOS build job (`ci.yml`) and the darwin release smoke step (`release.yml`). shellcheck now also lints the new script.

## Testing

- `shellcheck --shell=sh install/install.sh install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh`: clean
- `sh -n` on both scripts and `py_compile` on the driver: OK
- `bun test test/agents.test.ts test/platform.test.ts`: 60 pass, 0 fail
- **Not run:** the macOS PTY regression test itself. It only runs on Darwin and this environment is Linux, where it exits with code 2 as designed. The macOS CI job will be its first real run.

title: fix: defer macOS setup outside piped installer
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A Mac user reported that the piped installer reaches "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" and then accepts no keyboard input, while running the installed command directly afterwards works. This PR applies the safe workaround for that report until a durable Bun fix ships in a release, and adds the recommended smoke test.

Previously, `install.sh` ran `aifirst init` against `/dev/tty` whenever that device could be opened. Now, when the detected OS is darwin, the installer skips the `/dev/tty` probe and its non-interactive fallback entirely and prints "On macOS, finish setup in a new terminal:" followed by `aifirst init`; on other systems the existing `/dev/tty` path and its non-interactive fallback are unchanged. The README drops its "no second command" promise and tells macOS users to run `aifirst init` in a new terminal.

To guard the workaround, `install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh` pipes `install.sh` into `/bin/sh` inside a pseudo-terminal driven by a small Python fixture, serving a just-built binary through a stand-in `curl` so the installer's real download and checksum flow runs without a published tag, then runs `aifirst init` directly and checks that the setup prompt appears after the installer finishes and accepts input. The driver answers `n` to the prompt and gives up after a 45-second deadline; it fails when the child does not exit cleanly, and the shell script additionally greps the log for the deferral message and both finish markers. The script exits early with status 2 on anything other than macOS. CI runs it in the `check` job when `uname` reports Darwin, the release workflow runs it against each macOS build, and the shellcheck job now lints it too.

The new smoke test exits early outside macOS, so the recorded runs on Linux don't show it or the darwin installer branch executing. The workflow changes take effect in CI, and no run of them is recorded yet.

title: test: add real-Claude Showtail scenario harness
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR implements the "Claude/Showtail End-to-End Scenario Suite" plan: build real-Claude fixtures that capture an interactive Claude Code session with Showtail hooks, generate replayable AI First book content from it, run that content through `aifirst learn`, and require the replay to match the original exactly. The three scenarios are a multi-prompt train simulator, a plan-mode sandwich builder that answers plan questions with non-default choices, and an auto-then-plan habit tracker.

"Exact" is defined as canonical conversation events plus code artifacts, not raw terminal bytes, as chosen during planning, because PTY redraws, spinners and timestamps are volatile. `scripts/lib/claude-e2e-oracle.ts` normalizes Showtail report events and replay transcripts into `CanonicalEvent`s, and `scripts/capture-claude-showtail-e2e.ts` (exposed as `bun run capture:claude-e2e`) drives a capture, generates the book, replays it and verifies the result. Python PTY drivers under `test/fixtures/` type the prompts for authoring and replay.

The capture script won't overwrite a non-empty fixture directory unless `--replace` is given. A subprocess with a non-zero status raises an error unless that call sets `allowFailure`. When `--content-repo` or `--showtail-repo` is absent, the script defaults to `../aifirstcontent` and `../../Showtail` relative to this checkout. A Showtail verify exit of 3 is tolerated only when it reports the journal-entry type error, and that gap is stored as `showtailVerifyKnownRawEventGap` in `capture.json`.

The canonical form deliberately loosens some comparisons: temp workspace paths become `.` and test durations become `<time>`, Bash results drop stdout and stderr for an `ls -la` preflight and stderr for the `AIFIRST_REPLAY_ROOT=$(pwd)` reset, Read/Write/Edit calls outside the scenario's expected files and tools other than those plus Bash are dropped, and question answers on both sides come from the book's `canonicalAnswers` rather than the recorded selection.

The new test file has two tiers. The committed-oracle tier is enabled when the sibling `aifirstcontent` fixtures exist and compares author and learn events; the live tier re-drives Claude against source checkpoints and is enabled only with `AIFIRST_CLAUDE_E2E=1`, a `claude` binary and the fixtures.

One product change was needed for replay: previously, an exact replay step with a workflow and no pre-plan segments returned the planning reply without any text Claude wrote before entering plan mode. `respond` now delegates to `selectedReplayReply`, which prepends that trailing pre-plan text to the planning outcome, covered by a new planning test.

title: build: prepare releases for SignPath signing
body:
## Summary

Prepares the release pipeline and repository for SignPath Foundation code signing of the Windows binaries. The SignPath application is still pending, so **this PR does not submit any signing requests**. Windows executables stay unsigned for now, but they are built and checked so they meet SignPath's artifact requirements.

### Licensing and policy
- Changes the license from MIT to **Apache-2.0** (`LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `package.json`). Adds `TRADEMARKS.md`, which says the license does not grant rights to the AI First names or logos.
- Adds `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md` (project roles, privacy and network behaviour, system changes, release integrity) and links it from the README.
- Adds `.github/CODEOWNERS` covering the release workflow, build scripts, SignPath config and signing policy.

### Release workflow (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)
- Splits `build-linux-windows` into `build-linux` (Ubuntu) and **`build-windows` (windows-latest)**. Bun can only write PE version resources on a Windows host.
- `build-windows` checks ProductName, CompanyName, ProductVersion/FileVersion, FileDescription and LegalCopyright on every `.exe`. It then runs a smoke test on the x64 and x64-baseline binaries and uploads them as `binaries-windows-unsigned`.
- The darwin job now just runs `bun scripts/build.ts` (the host-OS default) instead of the two-step move dance.
- `workflow_dispatch` is now a build-and-verify dry run only. The tag-version check runs only on tag pushes, and the `release` job is gated on `push` of a `refs/tags/v*` ref. The old `tag` input is gone.
- Bun is pinned through `.bun-version` (1.4.0) in all workflows instead of `latest`.

### Build script
- The target-selection and argument logic moved into `scripts/build-config.ts`, which is pure and tested.
- By default it builds only the host OS's targets. `--all` is removed, and asking for a Windows target on a non-Windows host fails with an error.
- Windows builds get `--windows-title/-publisher/-version/-description/-copyright`. The version becomes four parts, e.g. `0.8.0` → `0.8.0.0`.
- Drops `--bytecode`, which embeds bytecode specific to the build host, from compiled releases.

### SignPath
- `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml` lists exactly the three Windows executables and enforces their PE metadata. `.signpath/README.md` records the expected project, policy and config slugs and the planned secret and variable names.

### Also included
- `chore(test)`: pins Claude Code to 2.1.252 (full compatibility suite passed upstream).

## Test plan
- [x] `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`: in sync (pack 1.5.0)
- [x] `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`: clean
- [x] `bun test`: 422 pass, 37 skip (live/e2e suites gated by env vars), 0 fail
- [x] `bun scripts/build.ts --local` on Linux, and the binary reports `0.8.0`
- [ ] The Windows-native build, PE metadata check and smoke test can only run on a `windows-latest` runner. Verify with a manual `workflow_dispatch` run of Release, which no longer publishes.
- [ ] The macOS build and codesign job also needs a run in CI.

Note: the local checks ran on Bun 1.3.14, not the pinned 1.4.0. CI will use the pinned version.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR prepares the CLI repository and its Windows release pipeline for a SignPath Foundation code-signing application, following a Windows user report where the installed `aifirst.exe` crashed on `--version` while a stock Bun runtime ran fine. Whether the native, bytecode-free Windows build resolves that crash is not shown on this head: the CI results recorded for this branch cover an earlier commit. The goal, per the agreed plan, is to meet SignPath's licensing, policy, provenance and PE metadata requirements without integrating the SignPath API yet; unsigned Windows publishing stays enabled until approval. Licensing follows the later decision to use Apache-2.0 instead of MIT.

**Licensing and policy.** The repository now ships the Apache License text, a `NOTICE` naming AI First Programming, trademark terms, a `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md` covering the pending SignPath application, and `"license": "Apache-2.0"` in `package.json`. CODEOWNERS adds `@steveonjava` for the release workflow and build script. A pending `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml` declares the Windows files to sign with product name "AI First CLI".

**Native Windows builds with PE metadata.** Previously `build.ts` defaulted to all non-darwin targets and accepted `--all`, so Windows executables could be cross-compiled from Linux. Target selection and compile arguments move into `scripts/build-config.ts`: with no flags it builds the host OS family's targets, `--all` is rejected, and an explicit Windows `--target` is rejected on a non-Windows host. When the target is Windows and the host is `win32`, `buildArgs` adds title, publisher, four-field version, description and copyright flags; non-Windows targets get none of them. `--bytecode` is dropped from compiled builds, and the `src/index.ts` comment that cited it is reworded. In `release.yml`, the combined `build-linux-windows` job is split into `build-linux` (ubuntu) and `build-windows` (windows-latest), which fails unless each `aifirst-windows-*.exe` reports the expected ProductName, CompanyName, ProductVersion, FileVersion, FileDescription and LegalCopyright, then smoke-runs the x64 and x64-baseline executables (the arm64 one is not executed), and the `release` job now carries an `if` requiring a push of a `v*` tag. Manual `workflow_dispatch` runs lose their `tag` input, skip the tag/package-version check and never publish, so replacement executables appear only after a `v*` tag push. A platform test asserts that `scripts/build.ts` no longer contains `--bytecode`; `test/build-config.test.ts` covers target selection and metadata arguments, and `test/signpath.test.ts` covers the policy, licensing and signing configuration.

Housekeeping: workflows read Bun from a new `.bun-version` (1.4.0), and the Claude Code pin moves to 2.1.252.

title: feat: improve learner TUI responsiveness
body:
## Summary

Makes the learner TUI stay responsive while exercises, replay commands and long reveals are running. Bumps the CLI to `0.13.4`.

- **Async process runner** (`src/process.ts`, new): `runAsyncProcess` streams stdout/stderr in chunks, takes interactive stdin, and supports timeouts and `AbortSignal` cancellation (whole process tree, including `taskkill /T` on Windows). It replaces blocking spawns, so the event loop and renderer keep running.
- **Exercise runs** (`src/commands/run.ts`): an `ExerciseRunOptions`/`ExerciseRunResult` API on top of the async runner. The TUI can stream program output live and let the reader type input for input-driven exercises without leaving the TUI.
- **Replay executor** (`src/replay/executor.ts`): ordinary commands now run asynchronously and respect their timeouts. PNG reads get a description instead of raw binary bytes.
- **TUI session** (`src/tui/session.ts`, `src/learn/native.ts`, `src/learn/terminalRenderer.ts`):
  - Any key or mouse click reveals the rest of a streaming plan or prompt. Running a prompt still requires Enter.
  - Long detailed pickers stay compact (`tuiChoiceLayout`) and long defaults scroll inside a detail panel.
  - After a menu selection, the output scrolls back to the latest content.
  - The final output chunk gets one frame to render before the next screen is built.

## Tests

New coverage in `graphical-run`, `replay-flow`, `run`, `terminal-renderer`, `tui-choice`, `tui-learn` and `tui-streaming`, with new driver fixtures under `test/fixtures/`.

## Verification

- `tsc -p tsconfig.json`: passes.
- `bun test`: 568 pass, 37 skip, 6 fail, 3 errors. I ran the failing files against `main` too, and they fail there in the same way:
  - `dependencies.test.ts`, "builds native Maven installation plans": fails on `main` too (depends on the environment).
  - `tui-learn.test.ts`, "opens progress and command reference as dismissible Home screens": fails on `main` too. In this sandbox the VS Code launch step exits with code 2.
  - `run.test.ts` "book scoping" cases, and one `duckling-learn-live` case: 5s timeouts that change from run to run and also happen on `main`, so they look like load-related flakiness.
- I did not run `test:books` or `test:learn:live` here.

title: Keep learner programs and prompts responsive inside the TUI
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR carries out the "TUI Quality-of-Life Improvements" plan: keep terminal programs inside the TUI with live output and an embedded input field when needed, reveal long prompts and plans on any ordinary keypress or click, replace binary image output with safe metadata, and remove synchronous process execution from the asynchronous replay path so that, per the plan, long-running commands such as PocketCFO stop freezing rendering.

**Process execution.** A new asynchronous process layer in `src/process.ts` (`runAsyncProcess`, `ProcessInput`) opens a stdin pipe when the caller requests one, forwards supplied input or interactive keystrokes, reports exit code 124 on timeout, and has a separate stop path on Windows. `executePreparedExercise` in `src/commands/run.ts` uses it and stops a multi-step run when a step exits non-zero, times out or is aborted; for a reader-input program the last command runs with no timeout. When a program produces no output, `run` prints a note saying so. Previously the timeout check read the `no-timeout` flag inline; it is now extracted into `executionTimeoutMs`. The replay executor runs non-shell commands through the async path, treats a graphical operation on Linux as a successful skip (exit 0, matching expectation) when neither `DISPLAY` nor `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, and describes binary files such as PNGs by type instead of printing their bytes. In `src/learn/native.ts`, `runExercise` now prepares the files and calls `executePreparedExercise` in-process with the TUI's output and input callbacks, and reports a stopped program from the result's `aborted` flag rather than the signal.

**TUI behavior.** In `LearnTuiSession`, a skip now ends prompt pacing as a cancel does, a menu selection that runs something returns the view to the latest output, the detail panel scrolls with PageUp/PageDown when it is scrollable, Ctrl+D ends input for an interactive program, and Esc or Ctrl+C stops a running command from the TUI. The terminal renderer accepts any key as a reveal when in any-key mode, and Enter is still required after a read-only prompt is revealed. Long detailed pickers stay compact.

**Consequences and limits.** The PR adds TUI driver fixtures under `test/fixtures` and updates the run, replay, renderer and TUI test files to match the new behavior; `test/graphical-run.test.ts` now expects a program to stream output and accept reader input without leaving the TUI. The `win32` stop path in `src/process.ts` deserves a try on Windows, since the work was done on Linux. The changed terminal-renderer tests replace collaborators with fakes. Interactive TTY handling in `run.ts` is worth trying by hand at a real terminal. The package version is bumped to 0.13.4.

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`.
- `bun test`: failed (572 pass, 2 fail, Ran 611 tests across 63 files. [280.63s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.

Feedback wanted: is exit code 124 on timeout and 127 for a missing exit code in `runAsyncProcess` the right contract for callers that previously used synchronous execution?

Moves the repository's committed content from MIT to the Apache License 2.0, and makes clear what the license does not cover.

`NOTICE` is **not** in the npm tarball. npm adds LICENSE files on its own, but not NOTICE, and the `files` list in `package.json` doesn't name it. title: License aifirstcontent under Apache 2.0 with NOTICE and trademark policy
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR puts the `aifirstcontent` repository under the Apache License 2.0 instead of MIT, as the first step of standardizing the AI First repositories on one license. The request gave the reasons: Apache 2.0 carries an explicit patent grant and patent retaliation clause, licenses contributions under the same terms by default, withholds trademark rights to protect the AI First name, and is already what `aifirstextension` uses, while staying permissive for commercial use. This is one part of a plan to standardize all four public repositories on Apache-2.0. The repository owner confirmed that all committed content (prompts, explanations, examples, replay data) can be released under it, and that attribution names three authors.

Previously `package.json` declared `"license": "MIT"`; it now declares `"Apache-2.0"`.

## Design

- A new `LICENSE` file holds the complete Apache License 2.0 text; there was no license file before, so only the `package.json` field carried MIT.
- A new `NOTICE` names "AI First Programming" with a 2026 copyright for Stephen Chin, Cassandra Chin, and Jennifer Reif, which is the attribution file the Apache license expects redistributors to carry forward.
- A new `TRADEMARKS.md` names Stephen Chin, Cassandra Chin, and Jennifer Reif as the trademark owners, says the license does not grant use of the "AI First" names or logos, allows accurate references to the project or compatible software, and requires written permission for anything implying sponsorship or affiliation.
- A new License section in `README.md` states what the license covers (committed source, schemas, examples, explanations, replay data and other content), and that the private source manuscripts and the separately published Apress books are not committed and not covered.
- The `.gitignore` comment for `manuscripts.json` is reworded to match: the private manuscripts are outside the Apache-licensed content.

## Consequences

Consumers of `@aifirst/content` (the CLI and the VS Code extension) get the Apache-2.0 metadata with the next published release, since the version stays at 1.5.0; no code or content files change.

The branch was pushed, but CI results for the final head have not been seen yet.

title: Verify every book step in isolation and in sequence, and gate releases on it
body:
## Summary

The exercise gate used to run each step on its own in a throwaway directory. That misses failures a learner actually hits when working through a book in order: files left over from earlier steps, a shared Maven project changing between chapters, or a local `math.py` hiding Python's standard library. This PR checks every step **both on its own and in book order**, and runs that check before releases as well as in CI.

### Verification runner (`scripts/run-exercises.ts`, `scripts/lib/verify.ts`)
- New `--isolated` / `--sequential` modes. With neither flag, both run.
- The sequential pass keeps one workspace per book under a temp root. For shared projects (`scaffold.projectRoot`), it removes files the previous step managed that the current step doesn't declare, and applies the step's `scaffold.clean` list.
- A book's sequential walk stops at its first failure. The failed workspace is kept and its path printed; `--keep-workspace` keeps it on success too.
- `--report <path>` writes a JSON summary plus per-step results. `--json` prints the same report to stdout.
- Steps with an external launch are reported as `delegated` to the compiled CLI book walk, not counted as passes.
- `verify()` accepts an optional caller-owned `directory`, and doesn't delete a directory it didn't create.

### Content fixes found by the sequential walk (pack version 2.0.0 → 2.0.1)
- **Python `py-2-12`**: now has its own `py-2-12/` project root, so `math.py` can't shadow the stdlib `math` module for later exercises.
- **Java Chapter 6 POMs**: add `maven.compiler.source`/`target` 17 alongside `release` so older Maven compiler plugins honour the level.
- **Java Chapter 6 ThermostatDemo step**: cleans up the stale `ThermostatApp.java` from the earlier step.

### CI
- New reusable `.github/workflows/exercise-walk.yml` (Bun, Python 3.12, Temurin 21 via `actions/setup-java@v5`, Maven, JUnit console launcher). It runs `--isolated --sequential` and uploads the report as an artifact even when the walk fails.
- `ci.yml` calls the reusable workflow in place of the old inline `run-exercises` job.
- `release.yml` now requires `exercise-walk` to pass before `release` runs.
- `/test-results/book-walk/` is gitignored.

### Tests
- `test/exercise-walk-workflow.test.ts`: checks that CI and release both call the reusable workflow, and that the workflow keeps its runtimes, both modes and the report.
- `test/filenames.test.ts`: `py-2-12` resolves to `py-2-12/math.py`.
- `test/java-chapter6-maven.test.ts`: the Chapter 6 POM declares source/target 17.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check` (repo audit, asset sync, schema validation, `bun test` 482 pass / 0 fail, both `tsc` configs): passes locally.
- [ ] `bun scripts/run-exercises.ts --isolated --sequential --report …`: **one failure locally, not yet confirmed on CI's toolchain.**
  - Result: 148 isolated and 116 sequential checks passed, 20 delegated, 1 step failed in both passes: `java-6-15` (`RestaurantTest`).
  - Cause: Mockito's inline mock maker can't instrument `java.time.Clock` (`Could not modify all classes [Object, Clock, InstantSource]`). The only JDK available locally is **27**, and the ByteBuddy version in that POM doesn't support it. CI pins **Temurin 21**, where this should pass, but I couldn't check that here.
  - Because the Java sequential walk stops at its first failure, the steps after `java-6-15` weren't run sequentially here.
  - The JUnit console jar wasn't in the local toolcache, so some standalone Java tests were reported as delegated rather than run.
  - The new `Full exercise walk` job on this PR is the authoritative result.

title: test: verify every book step in order through persistent workspaces
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
After a reader hit a broken Java exercise 6-05, the request was a harness that "runs through every sample in both books in order" and fixes the bugs it surfaces. The plan also chose an automatic exact checkpoint for cleaning shared project workspaces instead of manual cleanup.

## Design

`scripts/run-exercises.ts` now offers two modes, chosen with `--isolated` and `--sequential`; with neither flag it does both. Previously it verified each step once in its own temporary directory. The isolated mode keeps that behavior; the sequential mode walks each book in document order inside one persistent workspace per book, so files left by earlier steps stay in play.

To make that possible, `verify` accepts an optional caller-owned `directory`; when one is given it reuses it and skips deleting it, otherwise it still creates and removes its own temp directory. For steps that declare both a `projectRoot` and a `responsePath`, the walker deletes files the previous such step on that project root declared but the current step does not, then applies the step's `clean` list. `runSequentialBook` stops a book at its first broken step, keeping that workspace for inspection. Steps on the `external` launch surface, and any step `verify` itself skips, are recorded as "delegated" to the CLI book walk, which lives outside this repository. `--report <path>` writes a JSON summary to disk and `--json` prints it to stdout; the campaign workspace is removed when there are no failures unless `--keep-workspace` is given.

## Content fixes

The Java chapter 6 `pom.xml` scaffolds now set `maven.compiler.source` and `target` to 17 alongside `release`, and one Thermostat step adds a `clean` entry for `ThermostatApp.java`. Python `py-2-12` now places `math.py` in its own `py-2-12` project root, so it cannot shadow the standard library `math` module for later exercises.

title: fix: make Python replays portable across platforms
body:
## Summary

Python replays were recorded as `bash -lc "python3 ..."` commands, so they only played back on POSIX hosts with a `python3` on PATH. This PR makes them portable across platforms.

- **Schema / types** (`schema/content.schema.json`, `src/types.ts`):
  - `portableCommand` on command operations: a cross-platform argv that playback uses instead of the captured shell command. `<shell>` and `<python>` are placeholders that the player resolves for each host.
  - `display` (`ReplayToolDisplay`: `toolName`, `description`, `command`) on write/edit/read/command operations and on status events, so playback shows the original tool call accurately.
  - `timeoutMs` / `expectedTimeout` on command operations.
- **Importer** (`scripts/lib/import-showtail.ts`): for Python replays, emits `portableCommand` (rewriting `python3` invocations to `<python>`) and `display` metadata for shell tool calls.
- **Validator** (`scripts/validate.ts`): Python steps whose bash commands use POSIX-only constructs (`python3`, `rm`, `timeout`, `ls`, `VAR=` assignments) now fail without a `<shell>` portable command. It also rejects an empty `portableCommand`, and `expectedTimeout` without `timeoutMs`.
- **Content**: regenerated `books/ai-first-python-programming.json` and the Claude showtail e2e fixtures with the new fields.
- Bumps the package to `1.7.2`.

## Notes for reviewers

- `timeoutMs` / `expectedTimeout` are added to the schema and validator, but no content in this PR uses them yet.
- The `<shell>` / `<python>` placeholders only take effect once the consumers (aifirst CLI, VS Code extension) resolve them. That change isn't in this repo.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check` passed: repository privacy audit, asset sync check, `validate` (schema valid), `bun test` (459 pass, 0 fail), and both `tsc` configs.

title: fix: make Python replays portable across platforms
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Python book replays store captured shell commands as `bash -lc …` argv with a literal `python3`. This PR makes those replays portable: each captured command keeps its original argv but also carries a cross-platform form, and the label the author actually saw (for example a `PowerShell` tool call) is kept separately from what gets executed. The asks were to "Continue" that work and then to "commit, push, and release".

**Design.** Every `ReplayOperation` kind gains an optional `display` (a new `ReplayToolDisplay` with `toolName` plus optional `description` and `command`), status events accept a `display` too, and command operations also gain optional `portableCommand` (an argv starting with a `<shell>` placeholder), `timeoutMs` and `expectedTimeout`; the schema adds the matching definitions. The importer sets `display` only on command operations: when it builds one and any source path ends in `.py`, it adds `portableCommand` (via `portableShellCommand`) and `display` (via `toolDisplay`, which falls back to `"Tool"` when no tool name was captured and includes `description`/`command` when present). `portableShellCommand` rewrites `python3` to `<python>` when it is directly followed by `--version`, `-c`, `-m` or an unquoted `.py` path, so `python3 "$AIFIRST_REPLAY_ROOT"/habit_tracker.py` in the habit-auto-plan fixture keeps `python3` inside its `<shell>` command.

**Validation rules.** `validateOperation` now rejects an empty `portableCommand`, and an `expectedTimeout` without `timeoutMs`. For Python steps, the `requirePortable` flag is threaded through replay events, pre-plan events, workflow interludes and variants, and a `bash` command whose script mentions `python`/`python3`, `rm`, `timeout`, `ls` or an assignment whose name starts with an uppercase letter or underscore (such as `SDL_VIDEODRIVER=`) fails unless its `portableCommand` starts with `<shell>`.

**Consequences.** The Python book, the rocket fixture and the Claude e2e fixtures (habit-auto-plan, sandwich-custom-plan, train-multiprompt) are regenerated with the new fields, e.g. a pre-plan step now carries `<python> --version; <python> -c "import pygame; print(pygame.ver)"`. The replay privacy equivalence test ignores `display` and `portableCommand` when comparing. New audit tests require every captured shell command in chapters 9 and 10 to have a `<shell>` portable command and check that `py-9-01` keeps its `PowerShell` label. The package version is bumped to 1.7.2.

title: Record the exercise a replay starts from so exercises can run independently
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The goal is that exercises can be run independently of each other: py-10-01 on its own could not find the file from the chapter 9 level-editor exercise. This PR records, in the content itself, which earlier exercise's files a replay expects to find on disk.

Previously `processBundle` handed the previous exercise's scaffold to `deriveReplay` as `initialFiles` inline, with no exercise id attached.

**Design.** `Replay` gains an optional `initialState: { fromExercise: string }`, mirrored in `src/types.ts` and in `schema/content.schema.json`, which requires a non-empty string `fromExercise` and no other keys. `processBundle` stores that scaffold in `initialFiles` and, when both it and a previous exercise exist, sets `initialExerciseId` to the previous step's id, falling back to its parent's id. `deriveReplay` calls a new module-level function, `replayNeedsInitialState`, which walks the pre-plan, interlude and completion events; it returns true when a `read` or `edit` touches a path that is in the initial files and was not first created by an earlier `write`/`edit` in the replay. It returns false when there are no initial files. `initialState` is emitted when an `initialExerciseId` is set and that check is true; otherwise the replay has no `initialState`.

**Consequences.** The Python book now carries `initialState` for six chapter 9/10 replays, pointing at py-9-01, py-9-02, py-9-03, py-10-01, py-10-02 and py-10-03. `scripts/validate.ts` fails content whose `initialState.fromExercise` names an unknown step or a step with no scaffold files. The chapter 9 retrofit test expects no `initialState` on py-9-01 and the preceding exercise on py-9-02 and py-9-03; the chapter 10 test expects each of py-10-01 through py-10-04 to point at its predecessor. No replay runner in this repository reads `initialState` in this diff; it is recorded and validated here. The picker loop reported alongside this bug (py-9-01 repeatedly showing "Several AI First exercises may match") is not addressed here.

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes the extension's Apache License 2.0 status explicit and adds the attribution and trademark notices that go with it, as part of standardizing AI First repositories on Apache-2.0 instead of MIT. The request gave the reasons: Apache-2.0 carries an explicit patent grant and retaliation clause, covers source, documentation and compiled artifacts, stays permissive for commercial use, and explicitly withholds trademark rights, which helps protect the AI First name. This repository already ships an Apache `LICENSE` file, so the change here is about declaring it consistently and filling in the supporting notices rather than swapping license text.

## What changes

Previously the README's License section only said "See the LICENSE file for details". It now states that the extension source, documentation, generated artifacts and distributable examples are released under Apache-2.0, points to `NOTICE` for attribution, and says the license does not grant rights to the AI First names or logos, linking to `TRADEMARKS.md`.

A new `NOTICE` file carries the "AI First Programming" attribution with a 2026 copyright to Stephen Chin, Cassandra Chin and Jennifer Reif. The three named authors follow the attribution choice recorded for this work.

A new `TRADEMARKS.md` names "AI First", "AI First Programming" and the associated logos as trademarks of the same three authors. It allows accurate references to the project or compatible software, but forbids uses suggesting sponsorship, endorsement or official affiliation without written permission.

`package.json` gains `"license": "Apache-2.0"`; the regenerated lockfile picks up the same field.

## Consequences

No runtime code changes; the effect is on how the published extension declares its license and how others may use the AI First branding.

Updates the site and the hosted installers for the guided install flow: after installing, the CLI runs setup itself, so there is no separate `aifirst init` step.

No aifirstcli checkout was available here, so I couldn't check whether that has already happened.
