title: Continue hosted installers straight into guided setup and document the offline learner
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The CLI now has a guided setup and a built-in offline learner (the "Seamless Install and Native Learning" plan), so the hosted installers and the site should lead a new reader into it rather than handing them a second command to copy.

Previously the installers finished with a "Next:" list naming `aifirst init` and `aifirst next`, and when the install folder was not on PATH, `install.sh` printed a line for the reader to add to their shell profile by hand.

**Installers.** Unless `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` is set, both scripts now run `aifirst init` at the end of the install; with it set, no next-step hint is printed. In `install.sh` this happens when `/dev/tty` can be opened, with init reading from it; otherwise the script says interactive setup was skipped because no terminal is attached. `install.ps1` does the same when `$IsInteractiveHost` is true, and in both scripts a non-zero exit from init prints "Setup was not completed; run aifirst later to resume." When the install folder is missing from PATH and the shell is zsh, bash or fish, `install.sh` appends a `# Added by aifirst` comment and an export line (or `fish_add_path` for fish) to `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc` / `~/.bash_profile` (macOS), or `~/.config/fish/config.fish`, skipping the write if that exact line is already there, and reports the change. For other shells it writes nothing and prints a reminder to add the folder later; whatever the shell, it then adds the folder to PATH for the rest of the script.

**Docs.** The home page now describes a guided offline learner that needs no AI account or tool and adds VS Code to the Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity integrations. The CLI page explains that AI tool integration is optional and offered during setup, and adds a "Built-in learning" section for `aifirst learn` covering rendered Markdown, highlighted code panels, animation that Space or Enter skips, and `--no-animation`. The old note that setup writes only into its own `aifirst` folder and that `aifirst skill remove` undoes it was dropped from that page.

**Consequences.** For zsh, bash and fish users whose install folder is not on PATH, the one-line installer now edits their shell profile, and it starts an interactive session when a terminal is present; CI or scripted installs can opt out with `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1`. title: fix: defer macOS installer setup to a new terminal (Bun /dev/tty bug)
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the guided setup that `install.sh` starts right after installing doesn't work. The installer reopens stdin from `/dev/tty`, and Bun can't currently poll stdin opened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias (oven-sh/bun#41495), so `aifirst init` can't take input when it runs inside `curl … | sh`.

- **`static/install.sh`**: on `darwin`, skip the inline `aifirst init </dev/tty` call. Instead, tell the user to run `aifirst init` in a new terminal. Run directly, it inherits the real `/dev/ttysNNN` device and stays interactive. Linux and the no-TTY path are unchanged.
- **`content/cli/_index.md`**: update the install docs to say that on macOS you need to run `aifirst init` yourself, and that this extra step is temporary.

## Note for reviewers

`static/install.sh` is meant to be a synced copy of `aifirstcli/install/install.sh` (see `scripts/sync-installers.sh`). This PR edits it directly. The same change has to land in `aifirstcli`, or the next `sync-installers.sh` run will quietly undo the macOS workaround.

## Testing

- `sh -n static/install.sh` passed. This is the same check `sync-installers.sh` runs.
- `shellcheck static/install.sh` reported nothing.
- I pulled out the first-setup block and ran it with `OS=darwin`, which printed the "finish setup in a new terminal / aifirst init" hint. With `OS=linux` and no TTY, it took the existing "Interactive setup skipped" path.
- Not tested: a real `curl | sh` install on macOS (no macOS host here), and a Hugo build (`hugo` isn't installed here).

title: Defer installer setup on macOS to avoid Bun terminal-input bug
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A macOS user reported that the hosted installer reaches the "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" prompt and then accepts no keyboard input, while running the installed command afterwards works fine; the same user had hit the same symptom with another Bun-based installer. This PR applies a safe workaround in the installer and docs while a durable fix lands in a Bun release.

Now, when `$OS` is `darwin`, the installer skips the inline `aifirst init` and instead prints a message telling the user to finish setup in a new terminal by running `aifirst init`. Because the `darwin` test comes before the `/dev/tty` test, a macOS install skips both the inline setup and the non-interactive fallback, even when `/dev/tty` is readable. On other platforms the existing branches are unchanged: setup still runs inline when `/dev/tty` is readable, falls back to the old non-interactive path otherwise, and `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` still skips setup entirely.

The CLI page in `content/cli/_index.md` now says that on Linux and Windows the installer continues directly into guided setup (in the script, that inline step needs a readable `/dev/tty`), and that macOS users open a new terminal and run `aifirst init` as a temporary extra step.

The consequence is one extra manual step for macOS users until the upstream Bun fix ships, after which this branch should be removed.

title: Publish the code signing and trademark policy on the website
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
AI First Programming is applying to the SignPath Foundation for free open-source Windows code signing, and the project chose to standardize its public repositories on Apache License 2.0 instead of MIT for its explicit patent grant and because it excludes trademark rights, protecting the AI First name. This PR brings the website in line with that plan: it states the licensing and attribution clearly, publishes a trademark policy, and tells CLI users where the signing status stands.

**Licensing and attribution.** Previously the README's License section said only "Apache License 2.0 - See LICENSE file for details." It now says the website source and documentation are released under Apache 2.0, points to a new `NOTICE` for attribution, and states that the license grants no rights to the AI First names or logos, linking to `TRADEMARKS.md`. The `NOTICE` names AI First Programming with a 2026 copyright line for Stephen Chin, Cassandra Chin, and Jennifer Reif, the three named authors chosen for attribution.

**Trademarks.** The new `TRADEMARKS.md` identifies "AI First", "AI First Programming", and the associated names and logos as trademarks of the same three authors. It allows using the names to accurately refer to the project or compatible software, and requires prior written permission for any use suggesting sponsorship, endorsement, or official affiliation.

**Code signing on the CLI page.** The CLI download page gains a "Security and code signing" section, placed after the release links and before the "Then set up your AI tools" step, saying the project has applied to the SignPath Foundation and that Windows executables remain unsigned while the application is pending. That matches the decision to keep publishing unsigned Windows binaries until approval. The section links to `CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md` in the `aifirstcli` repository for privacy and network behavior, system changes, project roles, and release approval; that link only resolves once the CLI repository's policy file is merged on `main`.

title: Fix stale portal after gaming mode exit
body:
## Summary

When Bazzite moves from Gaming Mode back to Plasma, both sessions can share the same user systemd manager. `xdg-desktop-portal` stays running from the Gamescope session with no KDE backend attached. Flatpaks that need portal interfaces then fail after you return to the desktop. Deskflow, which needs `InputCapture`, is one example.

On the next Plasma login, a fresh broker starts with the KDE environment and backend. The `-` prefix makes it best-effort, so a closing user bus or a shutdown won't mark the Gamescope unit failed. - **`tests/test-units.sh`** (new): checks the hook count, order and failure semantics, and validates the drop-in with `systemd-analyze`.
- **`tests/test-ensure.sh`**: shellcheck cleanups (made executable, `source=/dev/null`, exported var in subshell, documented indirect-use disables). No behaviour change.
- **README**: covers the portal cleanup and how to diagnose and recover a stale portal by hand, notes that the installer should be re-run after updating, and lists the new test.

- `./tests/test-ensure.sh`: all pass
- `./tests/test-units.sh`: all pass, including `systemd-analyze` validation of the drop-in

title: Stop stale xdg-desktop-portal when leaving Gaming Mode
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Returning from Gaming Mode to Plasma can leave Flatpak apps such as Deskflow broken because the portal broker survives without its KDE backend, and the purpose of this PR is to inspect that and apply a targeted fix, the narrow "targeted hardening" option chosen over a broader rework.

**Design.** The Gamescope session drop-in, which hooks the `gamescope-session-plus@.service` template and so covers every client instance, gains a first `ExecStopPost` that runs `systemctl --user stop xdg-desktop-portal.service`. Gamescope and Plasma can share one user systemd manager, so, per the drop-in comment, stopping the generic broker synchronously during teardown lets the next Plasma session activate a fresh broker; the KDE backend unit itself is not stopped. The `-` prefix makes this hook best-effort, so a closing user bus or a shutdown cannot mark the Gamescope unit as broken. The existing autologin-clearing `ExecStopPost` keeps its command and still reports failures, but now runs after the portal stop.

**Consequences.** Existing installs only get the hook after re-running the installer, which the README now says replaces the drop-in and reloads the user manager. The README also documents the new hook, a `gdbus introspect` check for the `InputCapture`, `FileChooser` and `Settings` interfaces, and recovery that restarts `plasma-xdg-desktop-portal-kde.service` then `xdg-desktop-portal.service` in a session that is already affected.

**Tests.** A new `tests/test-units.sh` statically checks the drop-in: exactly one startup hook, two teardown hooks, the portal stop first with its `-` prefix, and the autologin clear second. When `systemd-analyze` and the Gamescope base unit are present, it also verifies the drop-in against the real unit; otherwise it prints SKIP for that part. `tests/test-ensure.sh` gets shellcheck-driven edits (directive comments and an `export` inside one subshell) and its executable bit.

title: fix(digest): don't count commands quoted inside scripts or heredocs
body:
## Summary

Commands that an agent wrote *inside* an inline script or heredoc were being counted as real commands. The digest split command lines on `;`, `|`, `&&`, `||` and newlines without checking for quotes or heredocs. So a line in `python -c "..."` or `cat <<'EOF' ... EOF` that mentioned `bun test` counted as a test run, and its grouping key came out as junk like `bun test',`. This closes the gap noted in #8.

## Changes

- **`src/util/shell.ts` (new):** `splitCommands()` splits a command line into the commands it runs. It respects single, double and backtick quotes and backslash escapes, and skips heredoc bodies (`<<EOF`, `<<-EOF`, `<<'EOF'`, `<<"EOF"`). Commands after a heredoc's terminator are still picked up.
- **`src/digest/build.ts`:** `testSegment()` and `commandKey()` now use `splitCommands()`. Grouping keys also drop heredoc and redirection tokens (`<<'PY'`, `> file`, `2>&1`), so `cd repo && python - <<'PY' ...` groups as `python`.
- **`src/correlate/correlate.ts`:** `makesCommit()` uses the same splitter, so a quoted `git commit` no longer counts as the session making a commit.
- **Version bump** to `1.0.0-rc.12` in `package.json`, `src/version.ts`, `plugin.json` and `VERSION`. The bundle `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` is rebuilt.

## Known limits

This is a heuristic splitter, not a full shell parser. `$(...)` subshells, `case` arms (`;;`) and nested heredocs aren't modeled specially, and a single `&` is not treated as a separator.

## Testing

- New `tests/shell.test.ts` covers chain/pipe splitting, quoted scripts with escaped quotes, heredoc bodies (including a pipe after the heredoc marker), test detection inside scripts, and grouping keys.
- `bun run typecheck`: clean.
- `bun test`: 96 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run bundle`: output is byte-identical to the committed bundle.

title: fix(digest): don't count commands quoted inside scripts or heredocs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes the digest stop treating commands that only appear as text inside an inline script or a heredoc as commands the agent ran. It fixes a known gap noted in PR #8, per the commit message. It was built while dogfooding Tracetoon for its own PR ("Can you dogfood this and use it for a PR.").

Previously, command lines were split on `;`, `|` and newlines even inside quotes and heredoc bodies, so a `bun test` mentioned inside a `python -c` string or a `cat <<'EOF'` body was taken for a test command; per the commit message, its grouping key came out as `bun test',`.

## Design

A quote- and heredoc-aware splitter, `splitCommands` in `src/util/shell.ts`, now splits a command line on `&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` and newlines that sit outside quotes and heredoc bodies (`a && b; c | d`); it does not split on a single `&`, subshells or comments. While inside single, double or backtick quotes it does not split; a backslash escapes the next character except inside single quotes. When it sees a `<<` or `<<-` heredoc operator, it skips the body from the end of that line to the closing delimiter, and keeps splitting what follows it. If the closing delimiter never appears on a line of its own, the rest of the command is skipped as body.

Test detection (`testSegment`), command grouping (`commandKey`) and commit detection (`makesCommit` in `src/correlate/correlate.ts`) now all go through this splitter instead of their own splitting. So commit detection changes too: `makesCommit` no longer matches a commit command that appears only inside a quoted string or heredoc body. `commandKey` also drops heredoc and redirection tokens when it builds a grouping key.

## Consequences

As a result, a test runner named only inside a quoted script is not treated as a test command, and grouping keys come from the real first command of the line. Commands chained with `&&`, `;` or pipes outside quotes are still split as before. The new tests in `tests/shell.test.ts` cover chains and pipes, quoted scripts, heredoc bodies and what follows them, and the grouping key case. The version moves from 1.0.0-rc.11 to 1.0.0-rc.12, and the generated bundle is updated.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (96 pass, 0 fail, Ran 96 tests across 9 files. [46.05s]), `bun run bundle`.

title: fix(digest): summaries checked against real work, with an evidence panel (1.0.0-rc.6)
body:
Tracetoon's digests sometimes claimed work that wasn't part of the PR, or missed work that was. This PR fixes the cases we found and adds a way to check summaries against what actually happened.

## How it was measured
`scripts/eval-summaries.ts` rebuilds digests for six real stretches of work where we know the right answer, and checks each one. It runs only on a local machine because it reads that machine's agent logs. Its report goes to `.git/tracetoon/eval/`, and none of its output is committed. It started at 41/48 checks and now passes 50/50.

## Digest fixes (`src/correlate/`, `src/digest/`, `src/git/pr.ts`, `src/trace/claude.ts`, `src/story/`)
- **Work already in the base branch is left out.** The cutoff is the last time the session committed something the base branch already has. Turns that finished before that point are dropped. A turn that spans the cutoff keeps its conversation.
- **Test failures are read from the test output**, so piped runs like `bun test | tail` count, and "tests went from failing to passing" now shows up.
- **Feedback typed while rejecting a tool call** is kept as a prompt and continues the turn.
- **Quiet commits** (`git commit -q`) are recognized by their subject line.
- **Files under `.git`** (Tracetoon's own run files) no longer count as repo edits. Binary files now count as changed. Work after the last commit belongs to the next PR.
- **Sharing a session** no longer turns two PRs into a saga.
- **Test commands are labeled by their test runner** instead of by the first command in the line.

## Descriptions
- The preview (`src/preview/html.ts`) has a new **Evidence** section that lists the digest's facts.
- `references/writing-guide.md` now asks the agent to check each claim against the evidence before rendering.

## Release
- Version bumped to `1.0.0-rc.6` in all four places, and the bundle (`dist/tracetoon.mjs`) is rebuilt.
- New regression tests are in `tests/summary-fixes.test.ts`, and `tests/comic.test.ts` is adjusted.

Run locally, following CI:
- `bun run typecheck`: clean
- `bun test`: 65 pass, 0 fail

title: fix: clickable preview links, and keep unrelated work out of a PR's story (rc.8)
body:
## Summary

Fixes found while using tracetoon on its own PRs, plus a release-candidate bump to **1.0.0-rc.8**.

### Preview link you can click (`b95f159`)
- `render` and `preview` used to print a bare path, and agents passed it on as a relative path the user couldn't open. Both now print an absolute `file:///…/preview.html` URL (Ctrl+click works in terminals) and return it as `previewUrl` in `--json`. The comic image path is printed the same way.
- `SKILL.md` step 7 now tells agents to pass the link on exactly as printed.

### Keeping earlier work and viewed commits out of a PR's story (`f167fc6`)
- **Earlier turns:** a turn's end time was taken from every edit in it. So if the agent edited a file outside the repo (a report, notes) after the last base commit, the whole earlier turn and its prompts stayed in the PR. Now only edits inside the repo count (`dropEarlierWork`).
- **Commit authorship:** if a commit's SHA showed up in any command's output, the session was counted as having made it. That meant running `git log` in another repo claimed authorship. Now the SHA only counts when the command creates commits (`commit`, `merge`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`, `am`, `rebase`, `pull`). This works when the command is part of a chain too.
- `scripts/eval-summaries.ts`: two eval cases are pinned to fixed SHAs, because their branches have since been merged or committed and the results kept drifting.

### `cd`-prefixed commands (`c973ef3`)
- Agents log a command with the directory the shell was in *before* it ran. So `cd ../other-repo && bun test` was filed under this repo, and its test failures showed up in this PR. The new `leadingCd()` resolves where the command actually runs (`cd`, `pushd`, `Set-Location`/`sl`, `~`, and Git Bash `/c/...` paths on Windows), and `belongs()` judges the command by that directory.

## Testing
- `bun run typecheck`: passes
- `bun test`: 71 pass, 0 fail
- `bun run bundle`: the committed `dist/tracetoon.mjs` is unchanged, so it is up to date
- New tests:
  - `tests/units.test.ts`: commit detection and `leadingCd`
  - `tests/flow.test.ts`: `previewUrl` and the printed link
  - `tests/summary-fixes.test.ts`: an edit outside the repo doesn't stretch an earlier turn
- Not run: `scripts/eval-summaries.ts`. It needs real session logs and repos on a developer machine.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR stops some work from other repos and earlier turns from showing up in a PR's digest, and makes the preview a link the user can open: "Ideally it should be displayed as a URL the user control-clicks to open." Both digest problems were found while dogfooding this PR.

**Commands that change directory first.** Agents log a command with the shell's directory from before it ran, so `cd ../other-repo && bun test` was filed under this repo and its test failures showed up in the PR. The new `leadingCd` in `src/trace/pathMatch.ts` reads a leading `cd`, `pushd`, `Set-Location` or `sl`, expands `~` to the home directory and, on Windows, maps a Git Bash `/c/x` path to `C:/x`. When it finds a directory, `belongs` judges the command by that directory (or a mention of a repo root in the command); other commands still use the logged cwd and mention checks. It returns nothing for a relative target when no cwd is known.

**Earlier turns and viewed commits.** Previously, a turn's end was judged by any edit, so editing a file outside the repo (a report, notes) after the last base commit kept a whole earlier turn, and its prompts, in this PR. Now only edits in the repo count in `dropEarlierWork`, when the turn has any; a turn with none still falls back to all its records. title: Add --aggregate-only for sealed runs; lean reviewed path in gates; perf gate validation-unavailable limitation
body:
## Summary

Three changes to the harness. The headline change is a sealed-run mode for the scoring tools.

**`--aggregate-only` for `prbench score`, `scripts/paired-delta.ts` and `scripts/qualify-cases.ts`**
- For sealed runs, where per-case data must stay unseen until release: prints only overall tables (composite and interval, W/T/L, errors, cost). No per-case rows or deltas, no leave-one-case-out ranges, no case names.
- With `--json`, the tools print aggregates only (`score` uses the new `aggregateScores`).
- Tests assert that no case id appears in aggregate-only output. `docs/reproduce-graph-vs-base.md` documents the flag.

**Adoption gate and admission: lean reviewed path**
- Accepts a candidate whose current v2 review meets the run's review plan: one pass per planned reviewer, each from a distinct reviewer agent id; the planned lenses; the planned reviewer model and effort; tool-run verified passes when the plan asks for them. The three-role rule still works as an alternative.
- `meta.workflow` now records `reviewPlan` and `reviewPasses`, read from Tracetoon's `review-plan.json` and `review.json`. Workflow gaps name each failed requirement.

**Performance gate: validation unavailable to both arms**
- When no validation completed for either writer in any pair (the sandbox could not run it), the report sets `validationUnavailable` and records an explicit limitation, also listed in the comparison summary. Timing and tokens then decide, instead of the gate staying inconclusive. Matched, unmatched, one-sided and mixed results keep their effect.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck` passes
- [x] Changed test files (`gates`, `operations`, `paired-delta`, `performance`, `score`): 30 pass, 0 fail
- [x] Full suite (`bun test --timeout 30000`): 293 pass, 1 skip, 3 fail

title: Add --aggregate-only for sealed runs; accept the lean reviewed path in the gate
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR's purpose is to help get prbench into a releasable state with "a set of test cases we can trust for the final benchmark", which means fresh held-out cases nobody has looked at. This PR adds `--aggregate-only` to `prbench score`, `scripts/paired-delta.ts` and `scripts/qualify-cases.ts` so sealed runs can be reported without naming cases. The work began from a request to switch codex back to the neo4j subscription.

**Aggregate-only output.** When the flag is set, the tools print dataset-wide tables (for example composite with its interval, W/T/L, errors, cost) with no per-case rows or deltas, no leave-one-case-out ranges and no case names. With `--json` as well, they print the aggregates only. In paired-delta, `aggregatePairedDelta` strips the per-case rows from the result for `--json`, while Markdown output hands the flag to `pairedDeltaMarkdown`. In qualify-cases, `qualifyAggregate` pools per-case rows into counts, pair-weighted shares and a case-clustered composite. In score, `aggregateScores` builds the arm table, and with `--json` it prints arms and paired deltas without the per-case map. Tests check that no case id appears in this output.

**Lean reviewed path in the gates.** Previously, the adoption gate and admission required three declared independent roles with a current v2 review. They now also accept a candidate whose current v2 review meets its review plan: distinct reviewer agent ids, one reviewer per planned lens, and the planned reviewer model and effort. When the plan's runner is `tracetoon`, each reviewer record must also come from a Tracetoon run with a verified model, otherwise a gap is recorded. The three-role rule stays an accepted alternative. `meta.workflow` records the stored review plan and reviewer records as `reviewPlan` and `reviewPasses` from Tracetoon's `review-plan.json` and `review.json`, and workflow gaps name each unmet requirement. New tests cover the lean path, its gap messages and the stored workflow record.

**Validation unavailable to both arms.** The commit treats the case where neither writer completed any validation in any pair as the sandbox being unable to run it. In that case the report now records `validationUnavailable` and an explicit limitation (listed in the comparison summary too) instead of leaving the gate inconclusive for that alone. Matched, unmatched, one-sided and mixed results keep their effect. A new test covers validation being unavailable to both writers in every pair.

title: compare --systems; cross-model composite delta in score
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The goal is to show whether the graph candidate can match or beat the main skill on the composite score at much lower cost, and to recommend a default model per provider for that trade-off. Two things got in the way: a comparison run had no way to skip native writers when only candidate vs baseline mattered, and the cross-model accuracy table had no column for the composite the win is judged on.

`compare --systems native,baseline,candidate` now picks the writer systems for a run. On a new run with no list, all of the provider's systems are selected. Baseline and candidate are required, and full names and the provider's native name are accepted as well as the short names, and an unknown name is rejected with an error listing the accepted ones. Previously each comparison was judged against both `tracetoon-baseline` and the provider's native system. When native is left out, no native writers run and only candidate vs baseline is judged, in both orders. Planned counts and rebuild's expected order count scale with the number of comparisons judged, `qualityGate` takes a null native when the run had none, and the `--plan` output gains `systems` and `judgedAgainst` fields.

A subset is recorded in the manifest settings, while runs with all three systems omit it; the commit message says this keeps earlier experiments' identity. A resume without `--systems` keeps the systems the experiment was frozen with, and a comparison test expects a resume asking for different systems to be rejected.

In the score report, the candidate-vs-baseline accuracy table gains a "Composite Δ [95% CI]" column: candidate minus baseline over per-case means, with a bootstrap interval over cases. A new test in tests/score.test.ts checks the composite mean and interval bounds on three cases and that rendering is reproducible.

tests/comparison.test.ts adds cases checking that `--systems baseline,candidate` plans no native writers and judges only against baseline, and that such a run completes and records its systems; the comparison ones use a fake comparison setup rather than the real one.

title: Add crossjudge: judge candidate drafts of one run against baseline drafts of another
body:
## Summary

Adds `prbench crossjudge`, which judges the `tracetoon-candidate` drafts from one finished `compare` run against the `tracetoon-baseline` drafts from another. A typical use is comparing runs from different writer models. It uses the artifacts both runs already saved, so no writer runs again.

- **Input checks:** both runs must be `prbench.comparison/v2` with exactly one writer model. Their judge contract, judges, rubric version, replicates, split and case set (id@hash) must match each other. The judge contract must also match this harness.
- **Judging:** every configured judge judges each pair in both orders. Results go through the same consensus rule `compare` uses for its quality gate: a pair counts as a win only when every judge's two orders pick the same draft. The output also includes composite scores per draft and the judge cost.
- **`--plan`:** checks the inputs and prints the planned judge calls without calling any model, so it needs no Claude login.
- **Other flags:** `--cache` (defaults to `<parent of --out>/.prbench-cache/v2`) and `--parallel`.
- **Small change elsewhere:** `modelRoot` in `src/comparison.ts` is now exported so crossjudge can find each run's drafts.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` (the local binary) passes. `bun run typecheck` (`bun x tsc`) hit the 15-minute tool timeout before printing anything, so I ran the local binary instead. The host was heavily loaded by unrelated processes.
- Full `bun test --timeout 30000`: 267 pass, 3 fail. The 3 failures are tracetoon environment checks in `agents`, `claude-comparison` and `codex`. They fail because this shell sets `TRACETOON=0`, which leaks into the "Tracetoon on" arm.

title: Add crossjudge: judge one run's candidate drafts against another run's baselines
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

The approved research plan notes that claims that one writer model beats another rest on composites from separate runs, which are noisy, and that prbench does not judge one model's draft against another's. This PR adds a `prbench crossjudge` command for that: it pairs the tracetoon-candidate drafts from one finished compare run (`--candidate`) with the tracetoon-baseline drafts from another (`--baseline`), for example runs with different writer models, and reuses their saved artifacts instead of regenerating drafts.

## Design

Both runs must be `prbench.comparison/v2` experiments with exactly one writer model each. If their judge contract, judges, rubric version, replicates, split or cases differ, the command refuses with the list of differences; it also refuses, with a separate error, when the runs' rubric version or judge contract differs from this harness's. Each saved draft is checked against its receipt, and a missing draft stops the run before any judge call. When the inputs pass, each pair is judged in both orders by each configured judge and summarised with compare's consensus rule, plus per-draft composite scores, error rates and judge cost. Results land in `--out` as `crossjudge.json` (the inputs), `pairs.json`, `summary.json` and `summary.md`; if a judge job fails, `pairs.json` is still written with the pairs that finished. Judge pairs run concurrently, four by default; `--parallel` must be a positive integer, and `--cache` defaults to `<parent of --out>/.prbench-cache/v2`. With `--plan`, it verifies the inputs and prints the planned judge-call count without calling models or requiring a Claude login. Outside `--plan`, an `--out` directory whose `crossjudge.json` describes different inputs is refused. To share the replicate path layout, `modelRoot` in `src/comparison.ts` is now exported.

## Consequences

Cross-run claims can rest on paired judgments rather than composites from separate runs, provided both runs share this harness's rubric version and judge contract hash; the error asks you to check out the judging code those runs used. The tests in `tests/crossjudge.test.ts` use fake judges, so they cover pairing, refusals and the summary, not real judge behaviour.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run prbench validate`, `bun run test` (268 pass, 0 fail, Ran 269 tests across 39 files. [473.69s]).

Where to start: `crossJudge` in `src/crossjudge.ts`, which validates both runs, pairs the drafts, runs the judges and writes the summary.

Feedback wanted: is requiring an identical judge contract across both runs and this harness too strict for comparing older runs, or should crossjudge allow an explicit override?

title: Document how to reproduce the Tracetoon graph-vs-base comparison
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR documents how to rerun the comparison between Tracetoon's original skill and its evidence-graph skill, so that someone outside our machines can repeat it with the same inputs, controls and scoring. It also adds an Unreleased section to the changelog that records the comparison-related features landed since 0.2.0.

## Design

The new guide, `docs/reproduce-graph-vs-base.md`, walks through the comparison step by step: the run, scoring and analysis steps are prbench commands, while building the two skill bundles uses git, bun and cp. It defines the two arms (the baseline skill built from `main`, the candidate built from the graph commit) and states that they share the writer model, effort, `PR_PROMPT`, budget and sandbox, differing only in the installed skill. Native writers are not run (`--systems baseline,candidate`), so each case and replicate yields one candidate draft and one baseline draft, and every judge compares the two drafts in both orders.

From there the guide covers prerequisites (the pinned Bun version and separate benchmark logins for Claude and Codex), building the two skill bundles, the skill settings, the `compare` commands for each provider, reusing baseline drafts with `--cache`, scoring, paired analysis across runs, expected cost and time, and reference results. The release confirmation run section is still a placeholder awaiting final numbers.

The changelog entry lists the end-to-end `compare --provider codex|claude|both` job graph, `--systems` subsets (a subset is part of the experiment identity), `prbench score` for absolute per-draft scores, per-model Codex pricing, writer and judge retries, safe concurrent controllers, timeout variables, `crossjudge` (one run's candidate drafts against another run's baseline drafts), `scripts/paired-delta.ts` (two runs compared pair by pair against their own baselines), the new guide, and assorted fixes.

## Consequences

The change is documentation only; no code or behavior changes. The example commands name specific writer models and a local Claude CLI path, and the arm table pins a bundle version, so readers will need to adapt those to their own setup.

title: Retry timed-out judges, fix isolation-proof resume for effort arms, all-thread Codex usage in scores
body:
## Summary

**Judges: retry on timeout**
- A judge call that times out (or fails for a transient reason) is now retried up to 3 attempts in all, with backoff, instead of invalidating the run. This also applies on resume when a timeout was already saved. Retries stop if the run is cancelled.
- Codex judges now report timeouts as timeouts (`codex judge timed out after N ms`), not as a generic exit-code failure.
- Failed judge attempts record which judge failed. The score report adds a judge-reliability table (`collectJudgeFailures`) next to the writer-reliability table.

**Isolation: resuming arms that set an effort**
- Probes saved the bare model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), but resume compared them against the arm spec (`claude-sonnet-5-5@medium`). So every resume of an arm with an effort was refused with "Saved isolation proof does not match this experiment."
- Probes now record the arm. Proofs saved before this change match on the bare model; the experiment id still ties them to the exact arm list.

**Score / usage** (earlier commit on this branch)
- Codex writer tokens and estimated cost now add up every thread the run spawned (the main rollout plus forked subagent rollouts). Each model response is counted once by response id, so parent history replayed into a subagent isn't double counted. Runs record `meta.usageScope` and `meta.subagentThreads`. For older runs, `score` recomputes all-thread usage from the saved traces.
- The judgment walk skips `<order>.json.attempts` folders, whose accepted copies duplicate the final judgments.
- Paired composite deltas gain a leave-one-case-out range, and the report adds a per-case composite delta table for each model.
- The writer environment hash (Codex and Claude) now ignores shell, terminal and session variables (`PWD`, `SHLVL`, `_`, `TERM_SESSION_ID`, `CLAUDE_*`, …). Experiments frozen with the old hash keep it as long as it still matches.

## Testing

- `bun x tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `bun test`, full suite, run twice: 251 pass / 3 fail on the first run, 247 pass / 7 fail / 1 error on the second.
  - **3 failures in both runs** (`agents`, `codex`, `claude-comparison` tracetoon tests checking `tracetoonOff`): caused by `TRACETOON=0` set in the test machine's shell, which leaks into the fake agents. With that variable unset, these files pass (37/37).
  - **Failures only in the second run** (`comparison`, `parallel-compare`): a 240 s test timeout, a fake Codex judge killed with exit 143, and "Isolation probe failed" under full-suite load. Re-running `comparison`, `parallel-compare` and `recovery` on their own (with `TRACETOON` unset and a longer per-test timeout) gave 14/14 pass. I did not confirm whether these load-related failures also happen on `main`.

title: Retry timed-out judges, count Codex subagent usage, and fix effort-arm isolation resume
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes comparison runs survive flaky judges and makes the reported cost of Codex writers include their subagent threads where the usage data allows it.

**Judge retries.** Previously the judge retry loop stopped on any failure kind other than transient, so a timed-out judge call was not retried. Timed-out and transient judge calls are now retried up to 3 attempts with backoff, including on resume after an interrupted comparison persisted a timeout, and they stop once the cancellation signal is aborted. Resume also proceeds past a persisted format failure unless its format repair was already used. Codex judges now report a timeout as a timeout error. Failed judge attempts record which judge made them, and the score report adds a per-judge reliability table next to writer reliability, both from the CLI and from `rebuildComparison`.

**Effort-arm isolation.** The commit message says probes saved the bare model while resume compared against the arm spec (`model@effort`), so resuming an arm with an effort was refused. Probes now record the arm, and proofs saved before that match on the bare model, since the experiment id already binds the exact arm list.

**Codex subagent usage.** `codex exec --json` reports usage for the main thread, so skills that spawn subagents looked cheaper than they were. When rollouts exist and hold at least the input stdout reported, writer tokens and estimated cost sum the main rollout and forked subagent rollouts, counting each model response once by response id so replayed parent history is not counted twice; otherwise the stdout counts stay, marked main-thread. Live runs read the new rollouts from the sandbox `CODEX_HOME` and record `usageScope` (`all-threads` or `main-thread`) and the subagent thread count. `checkArtifact` accepts these two optional fields and rejects any other `usageScope` value. For older Codex runs without a recorded cost, `score` uses usage recomputed from the accepted attempt's saved traces when it is at least the recorded count, and the score table gains Cost covers and Subagents/draft columns.

**Scoring and environment identity.** The judgment walk skips `.attempts` folders so judgments are counted once, and paired deltas gain a leave-one-case-out range plus a per-case table of candidate minus same-model baseline, one column per model. The writer environment hash for Codex and Claude ignores shell, terminal and session bookkeeping (terminal, multiplexer, editor, SSH and desktop-session variables such as `PWD` and `SHLVL`, plus the `PRBENCH_SHELL_` prefix); a frozen manifest that recorded the current hash uses it, and one that recorded only the legacy hash keeps that.

Test coverage is split by file: tests/codex-usage.test.ts for Codex usage, tests/environment-hash.test.ts for the hash, tests/score.test.ts for judge reliability and per-case deltas, tests/comparison.test.ts and tests/recovery.test.ts for judge timeouts, and tests/claude-comparison.test.ts for effort-arm resume. The comparison tests use a fake comparison setup, so they check the code around it rather than a real comparison.

title: Run comparisons in parallel on Codex or Claude
body:
## Summary

`prbench compare` can now run a comparison on Claude as well as on Codex, and runs writers, judges and isolation probes in parallel.

- **Providers:** `--provider codex|claude|both` picks who writes and who judges. Codex keeps Sol and Terra, and its frozen identity doesn't change. `claude` runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort, and the same two models judge. `both` runs two separate comparisons, in `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`. A comparison never mixes providers, and a frozen experiment refuses to resume under a different provider. `prbench auth claude` stores a setup token with mode 0600.
- **Parallel runs:** `--parallel <n>` (default 4) schedules all the work as one job graph. A judge starts as soon as both drafts it compares exist. Results are saved in a fixed order, so they don't depend on timing. `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. After a failure no new job starts; running jobs finish and are saved.
- **Codex login:** concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login through a symlink instead of waiting for exclusive copies. Verified with codex-cli 0.164, including three forced token refreshes at once. Windows keeps the copy mode.
- **Writer models:** `compare --models <ids>` swaps the writer models but keeps the provider's judges, so a cheap writer and a strong writer are scored by the same judges. `--provider both` rejects this option.
- **Judge schema:** each judge call gets a schema whose reference fields only allow the IDs that side may cite. Before, Claude judges sometimes made up fact IDs or cited the other draft's evidence.
- **Fixes:**
  - Windows-recorded cases now replay correctly on POSIX hosts. Before, the Tracetoon arms got no edit attribution; pr8 now links 92 edits and pr5 links 45.
  - `gh ... --help` no longer counts as a PR creation in the sandbox's fake `gh`.
  - An escaped dot in a shell glob (`'!\.agents/**'`) is no longer flagged as a host path.
  - The Claude environment identity no longer depends on the directory the comparison was launched from (`PWD`, `npm_*`).

The README has a new "Providers and parallel runs" section. Running the `claude` provider on its own models is a known limitation; the two providers' runs are reported separately and never pooled.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck` passes.
- Full suite (`bun test --timeout 30000`): 225 passed, 4 failed, 1 skipped, in about 12 minutes. All 4 failures pass when rerun on their own:
  - 2 tests in `tests/agents.test.ts` and `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` failed because the environment I ran in set `TRACETOON=0`, which reached the fake Claude. They pass with that variable unset.
  - 2 tests in `tests/codex.test.ts` failed on timing: a 30 s timeout and a check that allows 4 s but took 6 s. Both pass when `tests/codex.test.ts` runs alone.

title: Run comparisons in parallel, end to end on Codex or Claude
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes `prbench compare` usable for users who have Claude or ChatGPT but not both: a run is either a Claude run or a Codex run end to end, judges included, with a third option that runs both, never mixing the two, and as much work as possible runs in parallel so results come back quickly. The plan noted that the dev split's writers and judges ran one at a time and that models, judges, identity, isolation probe and writer runner were all hard-wired to Codex.

`compare --provider codex|claude|both` picks who writes and who judges. Codex keeps Sol and Terra and its frozen identity; claude runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort with the same models judging; both runs two independent comparisons in `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`. Providers are never mixed, and a frozen experiment refuses to resume under another provider. The quality gate's consensus check compares tracetoon-baseline against the provider's native arm instead of always `codex-native`. `--provider both` prefixes each child's output with its provider and exits with the worst child exit code. Claude's Tracetoon arms install the frozen skill and runtime, and Claude writers get a stripped Anthropic and Claude Code environment, no MCP servers, stage timings and an early stop on the result event. A Claude isolation probe reads the startup catalogue, and Claude judges run with no tools and no hooks. `prbench auth claude` stores a setup token with mode 0600.

`--parallel <n>` (default 4) schedules writers and judges as one job graph, and isolation probes run up to n at once beforehand; a judge runs as soon as the two drafts it compares exist, results are persisted in a fixed order, and `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order. After a failure nothing new starts, and running jobs finish and are saved. Concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login through a symlink instead of queuing on exclusive copies; Windows keeps the copy mode.

To test whether a cheaper writer can match a stronger one, `compare --models <ids>` replaces the provider's writer models, while the provider's judges stay the same. Models must be distinct ids, and `--provider both` refuses the option.

Fixes found while running it:
- The commit message reports Claude judges inventing fact IDs and citing the other draft's evidence, so each judge call now gets a schema whose reference fields, when that side has IDs of that kind, are enums of exactly those IDs; checkJudgment still validates the rest.
- The Claude profile hashed PWD, OLDPWD, INIT_CWD and npm_* variables, which blocked `--reuse-from` from another directory; writers run in their own sandbox cwd, and the Codex hash is unchanged.
- Previously the sandbox named a Windows-recorded checkout with the host's basename and stopped rewriting session paths at the mapped prefix, losing edit attribution; the checkout now takes the recorded path's last segment, mapped Windows paths get POSIX separators on POSIX sandboxes, and unrelated host paths keep their spelling. The commit message reports pr8 now linking 92 replayed edits and pr5 45 edits, up from 0.
- The scope audit turned every backslash into a path separator, so `rg --files -g '!\.agents/**'` was flagged as host agent state; a backslash escaping a leading dot is now dropped when the token has no other backslashes.
- The fake `gh` took `gh pr create --help` as a second PR creation; help invocations (`--help`, `-h`, `gh help`) now print help and record a help call instead of a PR.

New and updated tests cover the escaped-glob audit, Claude writers and isolation probe, the per-prompt judge schema, parallel versus serial results and provider resume refusal, the job pool, and Windows path replay. The comparison tests replace Claude, Codex and `gh` with fakes, so they cover the orchestration around those tools rather than the real CLIs. The CLI's interactive terminal handling has no recorded coverage with a user at the keyboard.

## Validation

title: Performance gate: pass on paired priced cost per draft, not time and tokens
body:
## Summary

The performance gate (`prbench.performance/v3`) now decides on paired **priced cost per draft**, not on writer wall time and tokens.

- **Pass rule:** the candidate/baseline geometric mean of paired per-draft priced cost must be ≤ 1.000. Pairs share the same model, case and replicate. Log ratios are averaged within each case first, then across cases. The case-clustered 95% interval is reported but not required.
- **Pricing:** uses the same cost `prbench score` reports, through a new shared `draftCost` in `src/report/score.ts`. It uses reported totals where available, prices every model at its own rate, prices cached input at its own rate, and counts Codex usage across all threads.
- **Inconclusive:** any paired draft without a priced cost makes the gate inconclusive. Causes are an unknown model price, missing tokens, or Codex usage from the main thread only. These drafts are listed in `unpricedDrafts` and in `summary.md`, which also states the rule.
- **Information only:** writer wall time and token counts stay in the report but no longer decide the gate.
- **Unchanged:** validation-comparability handling.
- **Policy hash:** changing `src/performance.ts` changes the gate policy hash. README and CHANGELOG are updated.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit`: passes.
- `bun run test`: 303 of 306 pass. The 3 failures are in `tests/agents.test.ts`, `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` and `tests/codex.test.ts`. The test host's shell sets `TRACETOON=0`, which leaks into the fake agents, so tests expecting the variable to be unset fail. This branch doesn't touch those files. With the variable unset (`env -u TRACETOON bun test …`), all 37 tests in those files pass.
- New and updated tests are in `tests/performance.test.ts` and `tests/comparison.test.ts`.

title: Performance gate: pass on paired priced cost per draft, not time and tokens
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The performance gate demanded better writer wall time and no more input tokens, which works against a candidate that spends extra time and cached input on review; the recorded decision for that trade-off was "Cost-based". This PR makes the gate judge what a draft costs.

Previously, a pair was counted when both writers had a positive wall time, each model's median writer time had to improve and its median input tokens could not rise, and the writer-ratio 95% interval had to sit below 1. Now a candidate with a matching baseline forms a pair whether or not wall time is recorded, and a pooled cost ratio above 1.000 is the sole reason for a fail verdict. The gate's criterion is now that the candidate/baseline geometric mean of paired per-draft priced cost (same model, case and replicate; log ratios averaged within each case, then across cases) is at most 1.000.

Cost is the one `prbench score` reports (new shared `draftCost`: reported totals where available, every model at its own price, cached input at its own rate, Codex across all threads). When no all-thread Codex usage is found, `draftCost` still prices the main-thread tokens and marks them as main-thread scope. The pricing logic is extracted from `collectDraftScores` into `draftCost`, and `rebuildComparison` attaches that cost to each writer row.

Any paired draft without a priced cost makes the gate inconclusive and is listed. Within a matched pair, a draft is listed as unpriced when its cost is undefined, when it is an estimate covering the Codex main thread alone, or when the cost is not positive. A candidate with no baseline is not paired, so it shows up through the expected-pair count rather than the unpriced list. `summary.md` now states the rule, labels the cost ratio as the criterion and the writer ratio as information, and prints one line per unpriced draft. Writer wall time and token counts stay as information. Validation-comparability handling is unchanged. The report schema moves from `prbench.performance/v2` to `v3`, and the CHANGELOG notes that changing `src/performance.ts` changes the gate policy hash. The README now describes the gate in terms of cost.

The updated tests name the cases they target: cheaper but slower with more input tokens, pricier but faster, and a paired draft without a priced cost; `tests/comparison.test.ts` now expects the v3 schema, the Rule line and a priced cost on writer rows.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run prbench validate`, `bun run test` (305 pass, 0 fail, Ran 306 tests across 42 files. [383.71s]).

title: Absolute per-draft scoring, effort-aware arms, and writer retries
body:
## Summary

Adds absolute per-draft scoring and makes comparison runs robust to individual writer failures.

**Scoring and cost**
- New `prbench score <roots…>`, plus a Scores section in every compare summary. Each draft gets coverage (claims, context, uncertainties), a rubric score, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, averaged over all judgments of that draft. These combine into a documented 0–100 composite, with case-clustered bootstrap intervals and paired candidate deltas. It also works on old runs.
- An Accuracy section reports, per arm, the error rate (share of judgments with ≥1 factual error) and the error classes (validation, code structure, attribution, motivation, pipeline). It also compares every candidate arm with every baseline arm, using a 0.05 claim-coverage guard and showing the cost ratio.
- `src/report/prices.json` estimates the cost in USD from token counts when a run doesn't report it (Codex).

**Effort as part of the arm**
- `compare --models model@effort`: writers get the bare model plus that effort (default `medium`, as before). Saved artifacts must match both model and effort.
- Isolation probes run at the configured effort, not the arm's: Haiku@low misreported the skill path and stopped whole runs.

**Writer retries (up to 3 attempts, reported per arm in a writer reliability table)**
- **No draft:** `failureKind` "produced no PR" becomes `no-draft`. `failure.json` names the arm.
- **Scope-rejected:** the rejected draft is never scored, and the retry runs in a fresh sandbox. Writer output is now cached only after the scope audit passes, so a retry no longer collides with an immutable cache entry.
- **Timed out:** retried the same way, with timed-out attempts counted in their own column.
- fake gh supports `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose`, which take the title and body from the branch's commits. Explicit `--title`/`--body` still win.

## Testing
- `bun run typecheck`: passes.
- `bun run test`: 237 pass, 1 skip, 3 fail in this environment. The 3 failures (`agents.test.ts` tracetoon install, `comparison.test.ts` tracetoon arm, `codex.test.ts` same prompt/model/effort) happen because the host shell exports `TRACETOON=0`, which the fake Claude/Codex fixtures pass through. With `env -u TRACETOON`, those three files pass (21/21). Should the tests clear that variable themselves? That's a possible follow-up.

## Notes
- `RUBRIC_VERSION` is unchanged: the judging prompt isn't modified; only the reporting on top of it is.
- `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/` aren't updated in this branch.

title: Score drafts on an absolute scale, run writers at a chosen effort, and retry flaky writers
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The goal of this PR is to move the benchmark "from A or B better to a score based evaluation", since progress is hard to see with only an A/B preference, and to let cheap writers such as Luna be compared at a lower effort.

**Scores.** `prbench score <roots…>` and a Scores section in compare summaries report per-draft coverage (claims, context, uncertainties), rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, averaged over the draft's rubric-v6 judgments whose case has a fact sheet, with a 0-100 composite and case-clustered bootstrap intervals. The commit message says this works on old runs retroactively. Coverage components are fractions over applicable items (a component with no applicable items counts as 1), and mistakes subtract with the composite floored at zero: claims 35, context 15, uncertainties 15 and rubric 35, minus 15 per factual error, 7 per unsupported claim and 10 per trap. An Accuracy section compares error rates per arm and each candidate arm against each baseline arm, with a 0.05 claim coverage guard and the cost ratio. When a run reports no USD cost (Codex) and its model is listed in `src/report/prices.json` (third-party list prices), the cost is estimated from token counts, so cost and score can be compared per draft.

**Effort as part of the arm.** `compare --models model@effort` makes effort part of the arm: writers get the bare model and that effort (default medium), and a saved artifact must match the model and, when the spec names one, the effort. Arm specs must be distinct and use an effort the provider accepts. Previously the writer got `effort: "medium"` and the raw model string. Isolation probes use the configured effort rather than the arm's, since Haiku@low misreported the skill path twice and stopped whole runs.

**Writer reliability.** A low-effort writer can finish without a PR (Luna@low refused to publish, and Sonnet@low used `gh pr create --fill`); both invalidated whole runs. `failureKind` now maps "produced no PR" to `no-draft`, retried like a transient failure (3 attempts), and a scope-audit rejection to `scope`. For a scope rejection, the rejected draft stays rejected and is never scored; per the commit message, a new sample runs in a fresh sandbox, so one mistyped absolute path does not invalidate a whole run. `compareV2` retries transient, no-draft, scope and timeout failures up to 3 attempts, and compare summaries add a writer reliability table that counts no-draft, scope-rejected and timed-out attempts per arm. Generations are cached only after they pass the scope audit, so a rejected sample's retry does not hit the immutable cache entry. Previously a generation was cached before the scope audit. The fake `gh` accepts `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose`, taking title and body from the branch's commits unless `--title`/`--body` are given.

The existing frozen comparison test now has the fake Codex writer type one mangled out-of-sandbox path and expects one recorded scope failure; `tests/arm.test.ts` and `tests/score.test.ts` cover arm parsing and matching, and the score components, cost and draft collection. The comparison and sandbox tests use fakes (fake Codex writer, `fake-gh.ts`), so they cover the logic around those steps, not real writers.

## Validation

title: Keep shell bookkeeping out of writers and out of the environment identity
body:
## Summary

A Claude comparison could not be resumed from a new shell. The Claude environment hash covered every inherited variable, including per-process ones like `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`, so the identity changed between shells. The same variables also reached writers, so `CLAUDE_EFFORT` from the host session could change a writer's effort.

- `src/run/sandbox.ts`: adds exported `VOLATILE_ENV` (per-login/per-process bookkeeping like `INVOCATION_ID`, `SHLVL`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` and `_`) and `VOLATILE_PREFIXES` (`KONSOLE_`, `CLAUDE_`). Sandboxes now drop both. `CLAUDE_` takes the place of the narrower `CLAUDE_CODE_` prefix, so `CLAUDE_PID` and `CLAUDE_EFFORT` no longer reach a writer's Claude Code.
- `src/run/provider.ts`: `claudeComparableEnv()` skips exactly the same list, so the hash still changes with anything a writer can see.
- `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts`: tests that volatile variables are kept out of writers and don't change the environment identity.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`: passes.
- `bun run test`: 227 pass, 1 skip, 3 fail. The 3 failures also happen on `main`. This session's shell has `TRACETOON=0` set, and the sandbox passes it through, so the tests that check `tracetoonOff` is unset fail:
  - `agent systems > tracetoon: installs into the sandbox…`
  - `claude comparison writers > tracetoon arm installs only the pinned skill and runtime`

title: Keep shell bookkeeping out of writers and out of the Claude environment identity
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The goal of this PR is a comparison that is measured on exactly what a writer can see, so that cached stages stay valid when the same experiment is restarted elsewhere.

According to the commit message, a Claude comparison could not resume from a new shell because the environment hash included per-process variables such as `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`. The same variables also reached writers, and `CLAUDE_EFFORT` from the host session could change a writer's effort. Previously the sandbox's prefix list was `CODEX_`, `ANTHROPIC_` and `CLAUDE_CODE_`; it is now `CODEX_`, `ANTHROPIC_`, `KONSOLE_` and `CLAUDE_`.

## Design

`sandbox.ts` now exports one list of per-login and per-process bookkeeping (`VOLATILE_ENV`: systemd, D-Bus, XDG session, SSH agent, `SHLVL`, `OLDPWD`, `_` and similar) plus `VOLATILE_PREFIXES` (`KONSOLE_`, `CLAUDE_`). `sandboxEnv` deletes any variable whose upper-cased name is in that list or starts with one of those prefixes, alongside the existing dropped tokens. `claudeComparableEnv` in `provider.ts` imports the same list and skips those names when computing the hash.

Because both sides import a single list, the hash skips the same bookkeeping names the sandbox drops, so it still changes with variables a writer can see. The new test in `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` sets `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `INVOCATION_ID` and `SHLVL`, checks that the hash is unchanged and that none of them reach a sandbox, then sets an unrelated variable and checks that the hash moves.

## Consequences

- `sandboxEnv` drops host variables whose upper-cased name starts with `CLAUDE_`, which covers `CLAUDE_EFFORT` and `CLAUDE_PID`.
- Writers lose host bookkeeping such as `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS`, `GPG_TTY`, `WINDOWID` and `KONSOLE_*`, so a writer no longer reaches the host's SSH agent or D-Bus session.
- The hash previously skipped `CLAUDE_CODE_*` but now skips every `CLAUDE_*` name and the bookkeeping list, so existing cached Claude stages whose hash included any of them will compute a different key once.
- The sandbox upper-cases names before matching, while the hash filter compares names as written, so a mixed-case name such as `Shlvl` is dropped for writers but still counted in the hash.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run prbench validate`, `bun run test` (230 pass, 0 fail, Ran 231 tests across 32 files. [231.35s]).

Where to start: `sandboxEnv` in `src/run/sandbox.ts`, which owns the drop list that the hash mirrors.

Feedback wanted: should any `CLAUDE_*` host variable still reach a writer's Claude Code despite the prefix drop?

title: fix: recover shell exit codes from Claude tool results
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR recovers shell exit codes from Claude tool results whose status appears in the result text rather than in a numeric field. The work supports an end-to-end exercise in which a Showtail report generated from a real Claude Code run has to reproduce that run faithfully, with the chapter 9 exercises serving as acceptance criteria.

A Claude tool result block can carry its shell status as a leading `Exit code <n>` line in its content, with `is_error` set and no numeric exit-code field. Previously `rawToolResult` read an exit code from the structured result or from numeric `exitCode`/`exit_code`/`code` fields on the block itself, so such a result came through with no exit code.

**Design.** A new helper, `resultTextExitCode`, reads the block's `content` as a string and matches a leading `Exit code <n>` line (negative numbers allowed; nothing else may follow the number on that line, which must end in LF, CRLF or end of text). It returns `undefined` when the content is empty or not a string, when the first line doesn't match, or when the parsed value isn't an integer. `rawToolResult` uses it as the last fallback: a structured exit code wins first, then a numeric field on the block, and the text is consulted when both are absent. Results that already carried a structured code therefore keep it unchanged.

**Consequences.** A tool result whose content starts with `Exit code 1` and that has no numeric code field now yields an exit code of 1. An `Exit code` mention after the first line, or a first line with text after the number (such as `Exit code 1 (signal)`), yields no code; output whose first line is exactly `Exit code <n>` is still read as a status. The text match does not consult `is_error`, so a leading `Exit code 0` yields 0. The fixture in `tests/claudeToolCall.test.ts` now begins with an `Exit code 1` line and asserts the recovered `exitCode: 1` on its `tool_result` event.

This PR sets up a local Docker test environment for exercising Showtail, modeled after the scripts used for aifirstcli, so the compiled CLI and the live capture tests can run against real Claude Code and Codex installs inside a sandbox that never writes to the host checkout or the host's agent configuration.

The design follows the plan for two workflows: a persistent manual sandbox and a one-shot runner for the existing source-level live capture tests. A `Dockerfile` compiles the current checkout into a standalone binary, keeps Bun, sources, and tests for the live runner, and fetches the upstream Claude Code and Codex install scripts into `/opt` at build time, unpinned, so those layers pick up new releases only when Docker rebuilds them. `.dockerignore` keeps `.showtail` trails, `.claude`, `.codex`, `.git`, `.env` files, and key files out of the build context. Shared helpers in `scripts/docker-common.sh` map `x86_64`/`amd64` and `aarch64`/`arm64` hosts to a Bun build target and fail with an error on any other architecture, build the image, prepare the named volumes, and start every container with `--init`, `--cap-drop ALL`, and `no-new-privileges`.

`scripts/docker-test.sh` rebuilds the image before its `shell`, `login`, and default commands, while `--help` and `clean` exit first. Each command runs a fresh `--rm` container; agent login state and scratch projects persist in two named volumes. Following the decision to copy minimal auth, the host's `.claude.json`, `.claude/.credentials.json`, and `.codex/auth.json` are mounted read-only and copied only when the volume doesn't already have that file, so a later host login won't replace the sandbox copy; settings, transcripts, and hooks are not copied. `login claude` runs `claude auth login`; `login codex` pipes `OPENAI_API_KEY` over stdin when it is set, otherwise runs device login, refusing without an interactive terminal. `clean` removes each volume when `docker volume inspect` finds it and reports it as already absent otherwise.

`scripts/docker-live-test.sh --check` verifies installation and authentication without spending model quota: it exits 20 when `claude auth status` fails and 21 when `codex login status` fails. title: Add a showtail upgrade command for installer builds
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

The request: "Make a showtail upgrade command to upgrade showtail from an install so users don't have to re-run the installer." This PR adds `showtail upgrade` so an installed copy can update itself in place.

## Design

`runUpgrade` calls `selfUpgrade`, which looks up the latest GitHub Release, maps the host platform and architecture to the published asset name (`showtail-<platform>-<arch>` for Linux and macOS, `showtail-windows-x64.exe` for Windows x64), and compares versions numerically. When the installed version equals the latest release it reports "already up to date"; when it is newer it reports that and makes no changes. Otherwise it downloads the binary next to the installed executable, runs the downloaded binary to verify it reports the expected version, then downloads the bundled `showtail.vsix`. On Linux and macOS it moves the current binary and extension to backups, swaps in the new files, restores the backups if a replacement fails, and then re-runs `setup --first-run` to refresh capture integrations; if that refresh fails, the upgrade still reports success and says integrations will refresh the next time Showtail runs. On Windows the running executable cannot be overwritten, so it schedules a helper that waits for the command to exit and then swaps both files, and the command reports the upgrade as pending; the helper waits at most 30 seconds and, if the command has not exited, deletes the staged download and leaves the installed files unchanged. The command refuses to replace a Bun/source invocation or runtime-managed executable, before making any network request. `--json` prints the result object instead of text, `upgrade` skips the first-run setup bootstrap other commands get, `GITHUB_TOKEN` is sent with the release lookup when set, and `SHOWTAIL_REPO` overrides the repository.

## Consequences

Installer users get a single command for updates; the README, installation guide, CLI reference, classroom workflow and changelog now point to it. The macOS and arm64 code paths have platform-specific branches that the linux/x64 sessions did not exercise. The Windows swap helper was also not run in any recorded session. The tests in `tests/selfUpgrade.test.ts` inject fake fetch, verify and replace functions, covering asset mapping, version comparison, the text of the generated Windows helper script, the up-to-date case, and keeping installed files intact when verification fails; `tests/cli.test.ts` checks that a Bun/source invocation is refused.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`.
- `bun test`: failed (631 pass, 62 fail, Ran 697 tests across 95 files. [84.79s]), run on the submitted content.

**Feedback wanted:** When integrations cannot be refreshed after the binary swap, should `upgrade` exit with an error instead of printing a note?

title: Prepare SignPath Foundation code signing and harden release pipeline
body:
## Summary

Prepares Showtail for applying to the SignPath Foundation's free code-signing program, and hardens the release pipeline so the Windows executable gets Authenticode-signed before it ships.

**Release pipeline (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)**
- New `validate` job: the tag must match `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, agree with both `package.json` and `src/core/version.ts`, and point at a commit that is already on `main`.
- Builds are split. `build-non-windows` produces the Linux/macOS binaries and the VSIX. `build-sign-windows` builds the `.exe` with version metadata (`scripts/build-windows.ps1`), sends it to SignPath, and checks the result: Authenticode status, SignPath Foundation signer, Product/File version, and the `--version` output.
- `publish` puts all artifacts together and adds an SPDX SBOM, `LICENSE`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and `SHA256SUMS`, then publishes the release with `.github/release-preamble.md`.
- Default permissions are now `contents: read`. Only `publish` gets write access. Every action is pinned to a commit SHA and Bun is pinned to 1.4.0 (also in `.bun-version`).

**Supply chain / repo hygiene**
- Adds CodeQL, Dependabot and CODEOWNERS.
- Adds a dependency-review workflow. It only runs when the `DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED` variable is `true`, because the action fails while Dependency Graph is off.
- Adds `scripts/verify-licenses.ts` (`bun run license:check`), which runs in CI and in release.
- CI and docs workflows now use pinned actions and the pinned Bun version.

**Docs / policy**
- New pages: `SECURITY.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, `docs/code-signing-policy.md`, `docs/getting-started/uninstallation.md`.
- Privacy and installation docs updated. The installers now mention signing.
- `.signpath/` records the expected SignPath project, policy and artifact configuration.
- `.github/SIGNPATH_APPLICATION_CHECKLIST.md` lists the steps for submitting the application.

**Tests**
- Adds `tests/signingReadiness.test.ts`, which checks that the docs, the policy files and the release workflow agree with each other.

## ⚠️ Behaviour change for maintainers

After this merges, **pushing a release tag fails in `build-sign-windows`** until SignPath onboarding is done and these are configured: variables `SIGNPATH_ENABLED=true` and `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID`, and secret `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN`. This is intentional, so no unsigned Windows build can ship. It does mean no release can be cut until onboarding finishes. Dependency review stays off until `DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED=true` is set and Dependency Graph is enabled.

## Testing

Run locally on Linux:
- `bun run typecheck`: passes
- `bun run format:check`: passes
- `bun run license:check`: passes
- `bun test tests/signingReadiness.test.ts`: 4 pass
- `bun test` (full suite): 625 pass, 4 skip, 63–64 fail. **The same 62 tests fail on `main` in this environment.** They are hook / end-to-end stdin capture tests, e.g. `post-edit hook snapshots the edited file as an artifact` (expected 1 artifact, got 0). No source under `src/` changes on this branch. Across two full runs, two extra tests failed once on the branch (`Stop reconcile imports clean per-file diffs…` and `--json output … emit clean, parseable JSON`). Both pass when run on their own, so they look like load-related flakes.

Not tested here: the release, CodeQL and dependency-review workflows themselves, the Windows build script, and the SignPath signing round-trip. These need GitHub Actions, a Windows runner and SignPath credentials.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR prepares the repository for a SignPath Foundation application for Windows code signing, while deferring the application itself until public reputation evidence exists. The goal is to keep Showtail under Apache-2.0 and limit the signed scope to the Windows executable; the new checklist notes the Foundation may still reject an application that meets every published requirement.

**Licensing.** A new `license:check` script asserts that the root package and the VS Code extension declare Apache-2.0, that the extension LICENSE matches the root one, and that the declared production dependencies match the reviewed list hard-coded in the script (Commander, Turbo Stream) with their expected licenses. CI runs it when `matrix.os == 'ubuntu-latest'`.

**Release pipeline.** Previously the release workflow copied whichever `showtail-*.vsix` was newest; it now copies the file named for the extension version. The single build job is replaced by a validate job (tag must match vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, equal the package and source versions, and be an ancestor of `main`), a non-Windows build, a Windows build that submits a SignPath signing request, and a publish job that needs all of them. The Windows job refuses to continue until the `SIGNPATH_ENABLED` repository variable is set after onboarding, so there is no unsigned Windows fallback. The publish job also attaches an SPDX SBOM, `SHA256SUMS`, LICENSE and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, and takes the release body from `release-preamble.md`. A SignPath artifact configuration for the `Showtail` product is checked in under `.signpath/`. Bun is pinned in `.bun-version`, and the Windows build script checks the executable's version metadata; CI runs that check when `matrix.os == 'windows-latest'`. `build:all` now builds only non-Windows targets and prints how to run the Windows build on Windows.

**Supply chain and policy.** CodeQL runs on pushes and pull requests to `main` and on a schedule. Dependency review runs on pull requests when `DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED` is `'true'`; the workflow comment says the action hard-fails while Dependency Graph is disabled. External actions are pinned to commit SHAs, Dependabot is configured, and CODEOWNERS covers workflows. New pages cover the code-signing policy and uninstallation, and the existing privacy page now replaces "no external API calls" with a list of user-initiated network operations. `tests/signingReadiness.test.ts` asserts the policy, roles, privacy and removal text, the Bun pin and Windows metadata, origin-verified signing before publication, and SHA-pinned actions.

title: feat: migrate legacy trails from local AI-tool transcripts
body:
## Summary

Adds `showtail migrate`, which recovers transcript detail that older Showtail versions didn't capture: replies, edits, plans, decisions, models, tool calls/results, and recap stats. It does this by matching existing sessions to the AI tools' local transcripts (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI/IDE, Copilot CLI, Copilot Chat).

- **Project command:** `showtail migrate [tool]` with `--session`, `--file`, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, `--json`, and `--resume`. `showtail migrate undo [batch-id]` removes a batch and writes a declared `migration-undo` marker so `verify` accepts the rewrite.
- **One-time upgrade offer:** an existing generation-1 install gets a single consented home scan, a bulk preview and one confirmation (`src/commands/upgrade.ts`, `migrateAll.ts`, `core/projectDiscovery.ts`). Fresh installs aren't prompted. Noninteractive runs and `--json` defer the offer. Bulk progress is stored in `~/.showtail-cli/migrations/`. Hooks now record the projects they see in `knownProjects` in the global config.
- **Append-only:** existing journal bytes are never rewritten. Recovered events keep the provider's timestamps and order. Separate `enrichment` journal entries record when recovery happened and which provider session id and transcript digest it came from. Absolute transcript paths are never committed. Migration batches (`mig_` prefix) are excluded from `import undo`.
- Each provider plugin gains a `migration` capability (discover transcripts, parse, plan files).
- Docs: CLI reference, data layout, installation and CHANGELOG.

### Follow-up fix in this PR (separate commit)

The feature commit broke live hook capture. `cli.ts` now loads `migrate.ts` and `upgrade.ts` up front, and both did a top-level `import { stdin } from 'node:process'`. Under Bun, touching stdin at module load loses piped input that is read later, so every `showtail hook …` call got an empty payload and captured nothing. On the feature commit alone, **60 tests failed** across hook, capture, reattach, plan, catch-up and capability tests. Commit 1a803f8 reads `process.stdin`/`process.stdout` lazily at the call sites instead.

## Test plan
