title: Make AGENTS.md handle the no-robot case and other setup gaps
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR tightens the agent runbook in `AGENTS.md` so that an agent setting up a VEX AIM robot for a student knows what to do when things don't go to plan, above all when the robot can't be reached. The work came from re-running the student prompt after the previous merge and being asked to try again. The commit message says a fresh agent following the runbook finished the install but flagged gaps: no stop condition for diagnostic retries, no guidance on what to say when the robot is unreachable, a udev path that doesn't exist for single-agent installs, no sample sudo question, no `lsusb` check and no Flatpak/VM hints.

The change is documentation only; no code or scripts change.

The commit message names the missing retry stop condition as one of the gaps. A new "If the diagnostic does not say `ready`" section now sets out the steps in order:

- On Linux, run `lsusb | grep 2888:0700` first. No output means the computer can't see the robot at all, so the student has to check power, the data cable, a direct connection with no hub, or VM USB passthrough.
- Wait about 30 seconds between `doctor` attempts (on Linux without the udev rule, a first failure right after plugging in is normal) and retry at most 3 times, then hand back to the student.
- If the OS sees the robot but `doctor` still fails, read its `fix:` lines and `docs/troubleshooting.md`. Sandboxed agents such as a Flatpak Goose can't see USB devices, so the agent should use a non-sandboxed install.
- Never invent a battery level. Report what `doctor` printed and still finish step 5, because the install doesn't depend on the robot.

When the robot was unreachable, step 5 now asks the agent to give no battery number, quote what `doctor` printed and tell the student what to check.

title: vexaim 0.5.1: fast contact play and reliable stationary tag search

## Summary

Release 0.5.1: reliable stationary tag search and an opt-in fast contact-play mode for composed behaviors.

- **Stationary tag search**: `find`, `approach`, `deliver` and named vision macros now take brief stationary native-camera readings at eight viewpoints (45° apart, settle then read three times) instead of relying on continuous rotation. Cargo acquisition stays a continuous sweep.
- **Contact play**: `behaviors.configure(verification="contact", tag_turn_dps=90)` finishes bounded contact, drives to the marker and operates the kicker without retention reverses, repeated possession gates or host camera round trips. Result evidence marks completion as *assumed*; it does not fake native attachment/release confirmation. Missing targets, transport errors, cancellation and activity deadlines still stop the sequence. Default `verification="vision"` is unchanged.
- Short native moves allow acceleration/status-reporting margin while still returning as soon as they complete.
- Version bumped to 0.5.1 (VERSION, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock); README, device-commands, skill `SKILL.md`/`references/behaviors.md`, release notes and hardware notes updated together.

## Hardware evidence (not verified by CI)

See `docs/hardware-notes.md`. The earlier stationary-view continuation found Tag 0 and placed the blue barrel; the camera confirmed it. The final 0.5.1 source check did **not** reacquire blue in the current layout. It stopped after a bounded search. **Full hardware acceptance of the new mode is still pending.**

title: Add fast contact play and stationary tag search to vision behaviors
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes the composed vision behaviors usable as a quick game for kids: once a hardware run picked up the blue barrel and found the purple tag, the request was to package it so that a child's run assumes success and moves briskly, while the camera checks and pauses that helped during testing stay available. It also changes tag search to look from stationary viewpoints instead of during a continuous turn. The session's opening request was to implement the plan.

**Stationary tag search.** When `find` is given a tag, it now hands off to `find_tag`, which stops, waits, and samples the detector up to three times at each of up to eight 45-degree viewpoints. A code comment attributes this to real AIM hardware, where stationary views found a marker that a continuous sweep missed. It ends with `not_found` after the eighth view or once its 20-second search budget is spent, and reports a `tag_search_view` event per view. Turns between views use a new `tag_turn_dps` setting, which defaults to `turn_dps`. Reacquiring a tag also pauses before each sample. Cargo search keeps its continuous sweep.

**Opt-in contact play.** `behaviors.configure` now accepts `verification="contact"`; the default stays `"vision"` and any other value is rejected. In contact mode, capture counts as done after the bounded contact stroke whether or not native possession is seen; possession only decides whether the pickup is recorded as verified. A contact move that stops short (for example at a pen wall) is returned as an attempt instead of raising a stall. Approach stops checking native possession of the carried cargo, and delivery skips the post-approach camera check and does not raise when release is unconfirmed. Delivery still requires camera confirmation of the cargo up front unless an earlier collect recorded it as carried. Previously, a delivery whose release the camera could not confirm raised `release_not_confirmed`; vision mode still does. Results now include `completed: True`, and in contact mode a step native sensing did not confirm reports `collected`/`delivered` as `None` with `contact_assumed` or `place_assumed` evidence. Short native moves now get at least a 1.5-second limit to allow for acceleration and late stop reports, and still return as soon as they finish.

New tests in `dev/test_behaviors.py` cover stationary-only tag decoding in both directions, a bounded search with no marker, and contact play that must not invent attachment or skip a missing target. The version moves to 0.5.1, and the docs describe the new mode.

**Limits.** The release notes say full hardware acceptance of the new mode is still pending, and that the final 0.5.1 source run could not reacquire the blue barrel and stopped after a bounded search. CI results for the pushed head are not known yet.

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

**Where to start:** `find_tag` in `cli/vexaim/src/behaviors.py`, which owns the stationary-view loop and its view and 20-second bounds.

**Feedback wanted:** Should contact mode keep requiring camera confirmation at delivery when no earlier collect recorded the cargo, or should a kid's game assume it is carried there too?

This PR adds pre-defined WinApps templates for Adobe Photoshop 2026 and Adobe Illustrator 2026, so the 2026 releases sit alongside the older Adobe templates already in `apps/`.

title: Use SDL FreeRDP client for full desktop mode on Wayland
body:
## Summary

On Wayland sessions (`XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland`), `winapps windows` now uses the SDL FreeRDP client for the full Windows desktop view. App launches (RemoteApp) still use the `xfreerdp` path as before.

## Changes (`bin/winapps`)

- `waGetFreeRDPCommand` now receives the subcommand (`waGetFreeRDPCommand "$1"`).
- When the mode is `windows` on Wayland and `FREERDP_COMMAND` isn't set, it checks for these clients in order:
  1. `sdl-freerdp3`
  2. `sdl3-freerdp`
  3. `sdl-freerdp`
  4. the FreeRDP Flatpak (`flatpak run --command=sdl-freerdp com.freerdp.FreeRDP`), which also sets `RDP_FLATPAK=1`
- If none of these are found, it falls back to the existing `xfreerdp`/`xfreerdp3`/Flatpak detection.
- The command validity check now also accepts the Flatpak `sdl-freerdp` command string.
- If the user sets `FREERDP_COMMAND` explicitly, that value still wins.

## Testing

- `bash -n bin/winapps`: passes
- `shellcheck -S warning bin/winapps`: no warnings
- Not tested at runtime. This environment has no Wayland session, Windows VM or FreeRDP install.

## Notes for reviewers

- The `windows` invocation still passes `/wm-class:"Microsoft Windows"` and `+dynamic-resolution`. Please check that the SDL client accepts these flags, or ignores them harmlessly, for the FreeRDP 3.x versions you care about.

title: Use SDL FreeRDP client for full desktop mode on Wayland
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The author adopted FreeRDP's SDL client for performance, then found that its RemoteApp/RAIL support was not fully implemented, so the SDL client is kept out of app launches. This PR prefers an installed SDL client for the full Windows desktop view on Wayland sessions when `FREERDP_COMMAND` is unset, with `xfreerdp` as the fallback, as a minimal change that is easy to review upstream.

Previously, when `FREERDP_COMMAND` was unset, `waGetFreeRDPCommand` checked for `xfreerdp` first, then the FreeRDP Flatpak.

**Design.** The main-script call changes from bare `waGetFreeRDPCommand` to `waGetFreeRDPCommand "$1"`, so the function sees the launch mode. When `FREERDP_COMMAND` is empty, the first argument is `windows` and `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` is `wayland`, the function looks for an SDL client in this order: `sdl-freerdp3`, `sdl3-freerdp`, `sdl-freerdp`, then the `com.freerdp.FreeRDP` Flatpak run with `--command=sdl-freerdp` (which also sets `RDP_FLATPAK=1`). All three names are probed because naming varies, and on some systems the unversioned `sdl-freerdp` is already FreeRDP 3. The Flatpak SDL command string is also accepted by the final command-validity check.

**Consequences.**
- The `xfreerdp` test gains a new `[ -z "$FREERDP_COMMAND" ]` guard, so it is skipped once an SDL command is set; if no SDL client is found in Wayland desktop mode, it falls through to the existing path.
- A user-set `FREERDP_COMMAND` still takes precedence, because the whole probe sits inside the empty-variable check.
- The commit message says other modes (RemoteApp/app launches) keep the existing `xfreerdp` path, and the diff's `windows` + `wayland` guard matches that.
- The `xfreerdp` branch checks the FreeRDP major version, but the new SDL branch has no such check in the diff.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- `shellcheck bin/winapps`: passed, run on the submitted content.
- `pre-commit run --files bin/winapps`: could not run in this environment (transport 'https' not allowed); it got no result on the code.

Where to start: `waGetFreeRDPCommand` in `bin/winapps`, which owns the Wayland desktop-mode SDL probe and the fallback to `xfreerdp`.

Feedback wanted: should the SDL branch of `waGetFreeRDPCommand` also check that the FreeRDP major version is at least 3, as the `xfreerdp` branch does?

title: test: walk every authored book step
body:
## Summary

Adds a full-book walk: every authored step in each book runs through the compiled CLI, using persistent per-book workspaces. Graphical launches get a smoke test. CI and release are both gated on the walk.

### New harness
- `scripts/walk-books.ts` (`bun run test:books`) builds a persistent workspace for each book and runs every step in order with the learner binary. It also smoke-tests graphical launches under Xvfb and writes `test-results/book-walk/report.json`. Flags: `--binary`, `--book`, `--from`, `--report`, `--skip-smoke`, `--keep-workspace`.
- `.github/workflows/book-walk.yml` is a reusable workflow. It installs JDK 21, Python 3.12, Maven, pygame-ce/Pillow, the JUnit console jar, Xvfb and xdotool, builds the binary, runs the walk and uploads the report. `ci.yml` calls it, and so does `release.yml`, where `release` now `needs: book-walk`.
- The Dockerfile test image gets the same graphical runtimes (`libgtk-3-0`, `xauth`, `xdotool`, `xvfb`).

### CLI fixes found by the walk
- **Project checkpoints:** when an exercise has a scaffold `projectRoot`, `prepareExerciseFiles` now deletes generated files from earlier checkpoints that are no longer wanted. It only does this if the file is unchanged. If the learner edited one, it stops with a `checkpoint_conflict` error. It also drops ownership records for files that are missing or cleaned up. Supporting changes are the new `GeneratedFileStore.recordsUnder()` and `forget()`.
- **Replay:** `aifirst replay execute` gains a `--relax-output` flag that only the harness can use (it requires `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK=1`). With it, a command can pass even when its stdout/stderr differs from the recording. When a command doesn't match, the JSON output now includes its `command`, `timedOut`, `stdout` and `stderr`.
- **Replay `rm` parsing:** `simpleRemoveArgument` now accepts only a single plain or quoted path.
- **Native learn:** when a program fails, the learner now sees the failure output in both TUI and plain mode, not just "did not run cleanly".

### Content
- The content pin moves to `aifirstcontent@57ef4bc` (pack 2.0.1). Java `chapter-6-testing` now cleans up `ThermostatApp.java`.
- The CLI version goes to 0.13.2.

## Testing

- `bun run check` (content sync check, `tsc`, `bun test`): 560 pass, 37 skip, 2 fail. Both failures also happen on `main` with this environment, so this branch didn't cause them:
  - `system command dependencies > builds native Maven installation plans` (Maven here comes from Linuxbrew)
  - `OpenTUI learning interface > opens progress and command reference as dismissible Home screens` (the test tries to open VS Code)
- Local run of `xvfb-run -a bun scripts/walk-books.ts --binary bin/aifirst-linux-x64` (incomplete because the local toolchain differs from CI): 94 of 163 steps passed and both graphical smokes passed. The walk stops at the first failure in each book, so each book had one failure and 67 steps didn't run:
  - `java-6-15`: Mockito can't mock `java.time.Clock` on this host's JDK 27. CI pins JDK 21, so this is probably specific to this environment. The JUnit console jar that CI downloads also wasn't present here.
  - `py-5-04`: `playing_high_card.py` fails because a `math.py` written by an earlier step in the shared `py` workspace hides the standard `math` module (`random` imports it). This ran on Python 3.15. CI uses 3.12, which would most likely hit the same problem, so the `py` book walk may fail in CI until the content renames that file. Worth checking on the first CI run.

title: test: walk every authored book step in order and reconcile generated files
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR builds a harness that walks the samples of both books in order, so bugs like the java-6-05 breakage reported from the learning TUI are caught automatically, and includes the fixes the request asked for alongside it. Isolated verification already exists; the ordered pass targets state left in a shared project by earlier exercises.

## Design

`scripts/walk-books.ts` (`bun run test:books`) drives the compiled CLI through the authored steps of both books in document order with one persistent workspace per book; `--book` and `--from` narrow the walk, and `--skip-smoke` skips the Xvfb window smoke tests for two representative graphical projects (py-9-01 and java-11-01). It writes a JSON report and sets a nonzero exit code when the walk is not ok. A reusable `book-walk.yml` workflow installs the learner runtimes, runs the walk and uploads the report even when the walk step fails; CI and the release workflow call it, and the release job now needs it. The Dockerfile test image adds libgtk-3-0, xauth, xdotool and xvfb, and `.gitignore` ignores `/test-results/book-walk/`.

`prepareExerciseFiles` now reconciles a shared project: generated records under the project root that the next exercise doesn't want and that still match what was generated are treated as obsolete, while one the reader edited is left alone and stops the exercise with `checkpoint_conflict` and a move-or-restore hint. The new `recordsUnder` returns an empty list when the record store can't be read and otherwise keeps valid records inside one managed project.

Other fixes:
- A new `renderExecutionFailure` shows the command output in a failure card, with a fixed placeholder when the output is empty.
- The portable shell `rm` can remove more than one file and normalizes backslashes.
- `replay --relax-output` is rejected with `bad_option` unless `AIFIRST_BOOK_WALK=1` is set. `replay execute --format json` adds command, stdout, stderr and timeout details for commands that miss their expectation.
- The Java book's Thermostat step gains a `clean` entry for `src/main/java/ThermostatApp.java`.

The content pack goes to 2.0.1, `@aifirst/content` is pinned to a commit instead of the v2.0.0 tag, and the CLI goes to 0.13.2, with a regenerated `bun.lock`.

## Limits

The `win32` branches in `walk-books.ts` and `generatedFiles.ts` did not run on the recorded linux/x64 runs. There is no record of the new workflows or of CI for the pushed head.

title: fix: use Homebrew for Maven on immutable Linux
body:
## Summary

On rpm-ostree systems (Bazzite, Fedora Silverblue, etc.) `dnf` can't install packages into the immutable base image. So when Maven is missing, the `java-11-01` dependency prompt fails or does the wrong thing.

- Adds `isImmutableLinux()`. It detects `/run/ostree-booted` or an `rpm-ostree` binary on Linux.
- `systemDependencyInstallPlan` checks for immutable Linux **before** the APT/dnf branches:
  - If `brew` is on PATH, the plan is `brew install maven`, labelled "Homebrew (immutable Linux)".
  - If not, it returns no plan, so it never falls through to `dnf`.
- If no plan is available on immutable Linux, `installDependencies` tells the user to install Homebrew, put `brew` on PATH and retry, instead of the generic "Install Maven and retry."
- Updates step 18 in `docs/learn-verification.md` to cover the rpm-ostree case.
- Bumps the version to 0.10.3.
- Follow-up commit: the existing APT plan test now stubs `exists`. Without that it read the real filesystem and failed on hosts that are themselves rpm-ostree systems.

## Testing

- `bun test test/dependencies.test.ts`: 11 pass. New tests cover marker/command detection, choosing Homebrew over dnf, and no dnf fallback when Homebrew is missing.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json`: clean.
- Full `bun run check` on an rpm-ostree host: 516 pass, 36 skip, 2 fail. One failure was the APT test fixed above. The other, `test/run.test.ts > book scoping > never hands a Python reader a Java exercise`, hit the 5s timeout under full-suite load. It passes when run alone on both this branch and `main` (21/21), so it looks unrelated and flaky.

title: fix: use Homebrew for Maven on immutable Linux
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
On Bazzite, the Maven install that `java-11-01` needs fails because Fedora Atomic images use rpm-ostree and discourage `dnf`; the goal is to detect an immutable distribution and install Maven through Homebrew there instead.

Previously, on Linux `systemDependencyInstallPlan` chose the first available package manager among APT, DNF and Alpine apk, and used Homebrew on macOS when `brew` was on PATH.

## Design

A new `isImmutableLinux` treats a Linux host as immutable when `/run/ostree-booted` exists or `rpm-ostree` is on PATH; on any other platform it returns false. The `which` and `exists` lookups are injectable so the tests can fake both signals.

When `isImmutableLinux` is true, `systemDependencyInstallPlan` returns a "Homebrew (immutable Linux)" plan running `brew install maven` with the resolved `brew` path, checked before the APT/DNF/apk branches. If Homebrew is not on PATH there, it returns no plan rather than falling through to `dnf`.

## Consequences

When no plan exists, the missing dependencies are all Maven and the host is immutable Linux, `installDependencies` now tells the user to install Homebrew, put `brew` on PATH and retry; other cases keep the generic "Install … and retry." message. Step 18 of the manual verification checklist now also asks to confirm Homebrew is selected ahead of `dnf` on rpm-ostree systems such as Bazzite or Fedora Silverblue. The package version moves to 0.10.3.

New tests in test/dependencies.test.ts cover both detection signals, the Homebrew plan on an ostree-booted host, and the no-Homebrew case. The tests fake the detection lookups, so no run on a real rpm-ostree machine with Homebrew is recorded, and no added test covers the immutable-Linux message in `installDependencies`.

The branch was pushed; CI results for the final head are not yet known.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`.
- `bun test`: failed (515 pass, 3 fail, Ran 554 tests across 59 files. [446.93s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
## Summary

The Claude Code integration used to call a bare `aifirst` command from its `UserPromptSubmit` replay hook, skill instructions, and permission allowlist. That breaks when Claude Code's inherited `PATH` doesn't include `aifirst`. The common case is Windows: a Windows Terminal, VS Code, or Claude Code process that was already running before the PowerShell installer ran keeps its old PATH.

This PR makes the Claude integration independent of PATH:

- **Stable launcher.** `aifirst skill install --claude` now writes `~/.claude/skills/aifirst/aifirst-cli.sh`, which `exec`s the absolute path of the current binary. When running from source under Bun, it also passes the `src/index.ts` entrypoint so dev installs still work.
- **Hook command.** The replay hook becomes `bash '<launcher>' replay hook # aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1`. The marker lets us recognize our own hook later. On refresh, the old bare `aifirst replay hook` entry is detected and replaced.
- **Skill and commands.** `SKILL.md` and the slash-command files are rendered with the launcher command in place of bare `aifirst`.
- **Permissions.** `claudeEntries(command)` builds allowlist entries for the launcher prefix. `grantPermissions` replaces legacy bare-`aifirst` entries and reports how many it replaced. `revokePermissions` removes both forms. The book-mode pre-approval check uses the new entries.
- **Windows paths.** The new `bashPath()` helper turns `C:\...` into `/c/...` for Claude's Git Bash, and `shellQuote()` single-quotes each argument.
- **Docs.** `docs/integrations/replay.md` explains the launcher, how to migrate (`aifirst skill install --claude`, or the full `%LOCALAPPDATA%` path if PowerShell can't find `aifirst` yet), and which installer to use on which platform.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`: passes
- `bun test`: 445 passed, 37 skipped, 0 failed. The skipped tests are live, opt-in suites that need `AIFIRST_CLAUDE_LIVE` / `AIFIRST_ROCKET_E2E` and a real Claude client, so they weren't run here.
- New and updated tests in `test/agents.test.ts`, `test/permissions.test.ts`, and `test/upgrade.test.ts` cover:
  - generating the launcher
  - converting Windows paths
  - quoting
  - migrating the legacy hook and permissions
  - revoking both forms

Not tested: running the launcher on a real Windows machine.

title: fix: make Claude hooks independent of PATH
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
On Windows, Claude Code's Git Bash could not find `aifirst` on `PATH`, so the `UserPromptSubmit` hook and Bash tool calls reported `command not found`. This PR stops the whole Claude Code integration from looking up `aifirst` on the parent process's `PATH` (each command still invokes `bash`) — hooks, generated instructions and permission rules, not just the hook — as the plan "Durable Claude Code Windows PATH Fix" set out.

Previously, the replay hook was the bare command `aifirst replay hook` and permission entries were `Bash(aifirst <cmd>:*)`, both resolved through `PATH`.

`install` now writes a small Bash launcher, `aifirst-cli.sh`, into the Claude skill folder; it `exec`s the current `aifirst` executable by absolute path. When running from source under Bun, the launcher also keeps the `src/index.ts` entrypoint; otherwise it calls just the executable. On `win32`, `bashPath` turns drive paths like `C:\…` into `/c/…` for Git Bash; on other platforms it converts backslashes to slashes. Arguments are single-quoted so spaces and apostrophes don't allow shell expansion.

Everything Claude runs then goes through `bash '<launcher>'`: the replay hook (tagged with a `# aifirst-managed-replay-hook-v1` marker so it can be recognized later), the rendered `SKILL.md` and command files, and the permission allowlist. `claudeEntries` takes the command prefix as a parameter, defaulting to `aifirst`.

Existing installations migrate on skill install, as decided for Windows users. The hook check accepts either the legacy command or the marker, and the permission step replaces legacy bare-command entries while leaving unrelated entries alone; it leaves `settings.json` untouched when the list is unchanged. `checkPermissions` and bookmode's `preApproved` check now look for the launcher-based entries, so a legacy-only allowlist reads as missing. `revokePermissions` removes both legacy and launcher-based entries. Install instructions in the replay docs and skill content are now platform-specific instead of sending Windows users to `install.sh`.

One consequence: the launcher records the absolute executable path at install time, so moving or reinstalling the CLI elsewhere needs `aifirst skill install --claude` again; the replay docs give a PowerShell form using the default `aifirst.exe` path for when `aifirst` isn't on `PATH`.

- `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`: passed, run on the submitted content.

title: Launch Maven JavaFX projects with mvn javafx:run

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The Chapter 11 JavaFX project could not be started from **Run the program**: as reported, "the final launch is not working". This PR makes the CLI launch Maven-based JavaFX projects the way they are built, with `mvn javafx:run`, and treats them as programs that open their own window.

Previously, `commandsFor` ran non-test Java examples with the single-file launcher, or with `java -cp out` when the scaffold had extra `.java` sources, regardless of any `pom.xml`.

## Design

A new helper, `mavenJavaFxCommand`, in `src/projects.ts` returns `["mvn", "javafx:run"]` when the step's language is Java and the raw text of its scaffold `pom.xml` contains `<artifactId>javafx-maven-plugin</artifactId>` (a plain substring check, not an XML parse); otherwise it returns `undefined`. Three callers use it:

- `commandsFor` in `src/commands/run.ts` returns the Maven command for non-test Java examples when the helper matches, and falls back to the existing launchers otherwise. It is now exported so tests can call it.
- `next` in `src/commands/next.ts` uses the same command for the run hint when it matches, keeping the old logic as the fallback.
- `opensExternalWindow` in `src/learn/native.ts` now also returns true whenever `mavenJavaFxCommand` matches, with no entrypoint requirement, while the pygame branch still requires a scaffold entrypoint.

Java steps without that plugin in `pom.xml` keep their current launch path. The manual checklist in `docs/learn-verification.md` gains step 19, which has a tester run `java-11-01` and confirm the launch uses `mvn javafx:run`, keeps the learning UI active while JavaFX is open, and succeeds when the window is closed; the package version moves from 0.10.3 to 0.10.4.

`test/graphical-run.test.ts` adds "launches Maven JavaFX projects as external-window programs", which loads the authored `java-11-01` step and asserts that `mavenJavaFxCommand` and `commandsFor` return `mvn javafx:run` and that `opensExternalWindow` is true. `test/run.test.ts` runs `aifirst run java-11-01` against a stub `mvn` on non-Windows hosts and asserts exit 0, a reported command of `mvn javafx:run`, and that the stub received `javafx:run`; the real window launch is covered by the new manual step, not by these tests. title: feat: improve learner replay experience
body:
## Summary

Makes built-in learner replays clearer and more portable.

- **Exercise prompt screen**: each exercise now shows its heading and then the prompt on its own screen (`renderExercisePrompt` / `TuiSession.presentPrompt`). From there the learner can run the exercise, go back, or exit.
- **Tool activity**: captured tool calls, their results, and Claude `status` events are now shown as tool cards in the TUI, or as dim bullet lines in plain terminals. Replay content can set `display` (`toolName`, `description`, `command`) to control how a call is labelled. Responder replies carry `nativeBlocks` so text and status boundaries survive into the learner.
- **Long code**: code previews stop at 40 lines. In a plain terminal, pressing `e` shows the full file; the TUI uses `appendCode`.
- **Async replay execution**: `executeReplayAsync` and `executeReplayOperationAsync` replace the synchronous executors in `replay` and native learn, so the UI keeps responding while commands run. Commands can now set `timeoutMs`, `expectedTimeout` and `portableCommand`.
- **Portable pygame replays**: native learn checks pygame game entrypoints with `py_compile` (through a portable `<python>` command) instead of opening a window.
- **Home menu**: removed "Browse books and exercises" and "Connect an AI assistant". "View progress" and "Command reference" now open as screens you dismiss with Enter or Esc to return Home.
- **CI**: new `windows-duckling-replay` job that runs the portable Save the Duckling replay on `windows-latest`.
- Version bumped to 0.10.5.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`: content in sync (pack 1.7.2)
- [x] `tsc -p tsconfig.json`: clean
- [ ] `bun test`: 523 pass, 37 skip, **2 fail**. Both failures come from the machine the tests ran on (details below).
  - `system command dependencies > builds native Maven installation plans`: the host is an ostree (immutable) Linux system, so the planner picks Homebrew rather than APT, as intended since 06e4fc7. This test and the code it covers aren't changed in this PR.
  - `OpenTUI learning interface > opens progress and command reference as dismissible Home screens` (new in this PR): VS Code is installed at `/usr/bin/code` on the host, so Home adds an "Open VS Code" item. The scripted `down: 1` / `down: 3` presses then land on the wrong menu items. On machines without VS Code in `/usr/bin` or `/bin` the test should pass. A follow-up could hide editor detection inside this test, or have it select items by label so it doesn't depend on the host.

title: Improve learner replay presentation and portable command execution
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes guided replays easier to follow and lets portable replay operations run on Windows, with `<shell>` scripts running in-process instead of through an external bash, shipping it as 0.10.5.

## What changes

**Presentation.** Replay segments now carry typed `blocks` that keep text and status boundaries, so the learner sees status lines apart from commentary. When a reply has `nativeBlocks`, the native renderer renders each block by kind, and tool calls and results render as tool cards. In the TUI, `appendCode` numbers each line, highlights it by filetype, and collapses a panel longer than 40 lines behind a footer that expands on click; the e key expands the most recent collapsed panel. Outside the TUI, `renderCode` likewise shows the first 40 lines and offers e to expand. In a document view, up/k, down/j, PageUp and PageDown scroll, and Enter or Esc return to Home. In a terminal or the TUI, the non-editable exercise prompt now waits for Enter after it finishes typing; in the native flow a prompt action of `exit` returns and `back` restarts the learn loop.

**Portable execution.** Replay operations gain optional `portableCommand`, `timeoutMs` and `expectedTimeout` fields; the executor runs `portableCommand` when it is present, else `command`. A `<python>` command is materialized with the selected Python runtime, and in the async executor a `<shell>` script runs through the in-process shell, with `<python>` and `<workspace>` substituted. In the native learn flow, a step with a pygame dependency has its window launch replaced with a `py_compile` check. A command with no exit status now reports 124 when it timed out, and 127 otherwise. For an operation with `expectedTimeout: true`, the native flow counts a command that did not time out as a divergence. The `replay` command now awaits `executeReplayAsync` instead of the synchronous executor.

**CI and tests.** A new `windows-duckling-replay` job on `windows-latest` runs the full captured Save the Duckling timeline. The workflow runs in CI, and no run of it is recorded yet, so the Windows path has not been seen running. The interactive TTY handling in `native.ts` and `terminalRenderer.ts` has not been shown with a user at the keyboard. A TUI test covers opening progress and the command reference as dismissible Home screens, and new driver fixtures back the replay, planning, streaming and Windows timeline tests.

title: fix: defer macOS setup outside piped installer
body:
## Summary

On macOS, `curl ... | bash` followed by `aifirst init </dev/tty` hangs: Bun can't poll stdin when it's reopened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias ([oven-sh/bun#41495](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/41495)). Running `aifirst init` directly inherits the real `/dev/ttysNNN` device and works.

- **`install/install.sh`**: on Darwin, the installer no longer runs guided setup inside the pipe. It tells the user to run `aifirst init` in a new terminal. Linux behaviour is unchanged.
- **`install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh`** + **`install/fixtures/macos_installer_tty_driver.py`**: a new macOS regression test. It pipes the real `install.sh` into `/bin/sh` inside a PTY, with a stub `curl` that serves the just-built binary so the real download and checksum steps still run. It then checks two things:
  - the installer prints the deferral message and shows no prompt
  - a direct `aifirst init` afterwards shows its `[Y/n]` prompt and accepts input
- **CI**: the new test runs in the Darwin leg of `ci.yml` and in the macOS release smoke test in `release.yml`. It's also added to the shellcheck lint job.
- **README**: documents the extra `aifirst init` step on macOS.

## Testing

- `shellcheck --shell=sh install/install.sh install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh`: passes
- `sh -n` on both scripts and `py_compile` on the driver: pass
- **Not run here:** the macOS PTY regression test itself needs Darwin and a darwin binary, and this PR was prepared on Linux. On Linux the script correctly exits early with "only runs on macOS". The macOS CI jobs above cover it.

title: fix: defer macOS setup outside the piped installer
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
A macOS user reported that the piped installer reaches "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" and then accepts no keyboard input, while running the installed command afterwards works fine. This PR applies the safe workaround until a durable fix ships in a Bun release, and adds the recommended smoke test.

When setup is not skipped and the detected OS is `darwin`, the installer does not launch setup; it prints "On macOS, finish setup in a new terminal:" followed by `aifirst init`. On other systems the existing `/dev/tty` path and its fallback are unchanged. A comment in `install.sh` links the hang to oven-sh/bun#41495, Bun being unable to poll stdin reopened through macOS's `/dev/tty` alias. The README now splits the flow into Linux/Windows and macOS and drops its "no second command" claim.

The new `install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh` exits with status 2 on anything other than Darwin or without an executable binary argument. On macOS it pipes the real installer, with its download and checksum flow, into `sh` against a fake `curl` that serves the freshly built binary, then runs `aifirst init` directly in the same pseudo-terminal through `install/fixtures/macos_installer_tty_driver.py`, which answers `n` to the setup prompt. The driver fails on a 45-second timeout, when the prompt never appears, or when the child does not exit cleanly with status 0. The script then checks the output for the macOS message, the installer finishing before the setup prompt, and "Nothing installed.", so it exercises input handling rather than a tool install. CI runs the script after the smoke test when `uname -s` is Darwin and adds it to the shellcheck job; the release workflow runs it for each darwin binary.

As a result, macOS users run `aifirst init` themselves after installing. The recorded runs were on Linux, so none shows the macOS path or the new test script executing; the workflow changes run in CI, and no run of them appears here. The PTY driver answers the prompt programmatically, so it does not show the path with a user at the keyboard.

## Validation

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `shellcheck --shell=sh install/install.sh install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh`, `sh -n install/install.sh install/test-macos-installer-tty.sh`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`.

Where to start: `main` in `install/fixtures/macos_installer_tty_driver.py`, which forks the PTY child and checks its exit status.

title: test: add Claude Showtail scenario harness
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR adds an end-to-end harness that drives real Claude Code sessions through three scenarios, keeps the Showtail report and checkpoints as authoring evidence, replays generated book content through `aifirst learn`, and requires the two sides to match. The goal is a multi-prompt train simulator, a plan-mode sandwich builder where every question gets a non-default answer that the replay must show as "Book Recommended", and an auto-mode turn followed by plan mode and execution.

## Design

`scripts/capture-claude-showtail-e2e.ts` (run with `bun run capture:claude-e2e`) captures every scenario in sequence, or one with `--scenario`: for each it drives an interactive Claude session through a PTY with Showtail hooks, generates replay content from the report and source checkpoints, replays it, and verifies the result. Writing into a non-empty output directory needs `--replace`, and a subprocess exit other than 0 aborts the capture unless that step allows failure. The content checkout defaults to `../aifirstcontent` and Showtail to `../../Showtail`, both overridable by flag; the capture runs the content repo's `scripts/generate-claude-e2e-test-content.ts` and writes fixtures under that checkout's `test/fixtures/claude-showtail-e2e`. A Showtail verify failure is tolerated only for exit 3 with the known journal-entry type error, which is recorded in the capture.

The capture copies `.claude.json` and `.credentials.json` from `AIFIRST_CLAUDE_AUTH_HOME` (default: your home directory) into a scratch HOME at mode 0600 and pre-allows `Bash(*)`, `Edit(*)`, `Read(*)` and `Write(*)` there, so run it only on a machine where that is acceptable. Two Python PTY drivers in `test/fixtures` drive the authoring and replay sessions.

Exact comparison uses canonical conversation events plus every source checkpoint rather than raw terminal bytes, because PTY redraws, spinners, timestamps and cursor movement are volatile; raw logs are kept for review. `scripts/lib/claude-e2e-oracle.ts` normalizes both sides (rewriting paths when a turn changes directory, dropping output of `ls -la` preflight commands and stderr of commands that reset the replay root) and `scripts/lib/claude-e2e-scenarios.ts` defines the turns and expected files. `test/claude-showtail-scenarios-e2e.test.ts` checks committed oracles when the sibling fixtures exist, and runs live replay only with `AIFIRST_CLAUDE_E2E=1` and a `claude` binary, matching the rocket example's opt-in pattern.

## Responder fix

Previously, an exact workflow prompt whose captured pre-plan events were text-only went straight into planning and dropped that preamble. `respond` now sends every exact workflow prompt with planning through `selectedReplayReply`, which prefixes the planning reply with the trailing pre-plan text when no pre-plan tool segments exist. A unit test covers a text-only preamble before the first question.

## Validation

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`.
- `bun test`: failed (399 pass, 3 fail, Ran 420 tests across 40 files. [156.68s]), run on the submitted content.

Where to start: `captureScenario` in `scripts/capture-claude-showtail-e2e.ts`, which owns the capture/replay/verify flow and the overwrite guard.

Feedback wanted: is canonical-event equality strict enough as the "exact" oracle, or should some terminal output also be compared byte-for-byte?

- Each OS family now builds on its own runner. The `build-linux-windows` job is split into `build-linux` (Ubuntu) and `build-windows` (`windows-latest`), because Bun can only write PE version resources on a Windows host.
- `build-windows` checks ProductName, CompanyName, ProductVersion/FileVersion, description and copyright on every `.exe`. It then runs a smoke test on the x64 and x64-baseline binaries and uploads `binaries-windows-unsigned`.
- `workflow_dispatch` is now a build-and-verify dry run only. The `tag` input is gone, the tag/version check runs only on tag pushes, and the `release` job only runs for `refs/tags/v*` pushes.

**Build scripts**
- Target selection and argument building move into `scripts/build-config.ts`, which `test/build-config.test.ts` tests.

- `--all` is removed, and building a Windows target from a non-Windows host is rejected.
- ⚠️ `--bytecode` is no longer passed to `bun build`. The comment in `src/index.ts` is updated to match. This may make CLI startup a little slower; please confirm the trade-off is intended.

**SignPath**
- Adds `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml`, which enforces PE metadata for the three Windows executables, plus `.signpath/README.md`. `test/signpath.test.ts` checks that this config matches `build-config.ts`.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR prepares the CLI repository and its Windows release pipeline for a SignPath Foundation code-signing application, following the plan "Prepare AI First CLI for SignPath Foundation Approval" and the later request to "do a change to Apache 2.0 instead of MIT". It started from a Windows user whose installed `aifirst.exe` crashed on `--version`, and the request to fix it and publish replacement Windows executables for the latest release. The commit summarizes the goal as publishing Apache-2.0 licensing and a code-signing policy, building Windows artifacts natively with enforced PE metadata, and adding the pending SignPath artifact configuration. SignPath signing of Windows binaries is not wired up; per the user's decision, unsigned Windows binaries keep publishing while approval is pending.

**Build selection.** Previously `scripts/build.ts` picked targets inline, defaulting to all non-darwin targets with `--all` for the full set, and compiled with `--bytecode`. Target choice now lives in `selectBuildTargets` in `scripts/build-config.ts`: with no flag it builds the host OS family's targets, `--local` and explicit `--target` still work, `--all` is rejected, and a Windows target requested on a non-Windows host throws. `buildArgs` adds Windows metadata arguments (with a four-field version from `windowsVersion`) when the target is Windows and the host is `win32`, and throws for a Windows target on another host; non-Windows targets are built without Windows-only arguments. **Release workflow.** The combined `build-linux-windows` job is split into `build-linux` on ubuntu-latest and `build-windows` on windows-latest, because, per the workflow comment, Bun can only write Windows version resources on a Windows host. title: feat: improve learner TUI responsiveness
body:
## Summary

This makes the learner TUI and `aifirst run` stay responsive while programs run and plans stream in. It also bumps the version to **0.13.4**.

- **Child processes no longer block the screen.** The new `src/process.ts` adds `runAsyncProcess`. It streams stdout and stderr as they arrive and still keeps the full output. It also supports interactive stdin, timeouts, and cancellation through `AbortSignal`, and it stops the whole process group (`taskkill /T` on Windows).
- **Exercise runs share one code path.** `executePreparedExercise` in `src/commands/run.ts` holds the compile-then-run logic, the JUnit and runtime checks, the timeout and abort handling, and the rule that a deliberate exception counts as success. The CLI and the native TUI learner both use it, so `src/learn/native.ts` drops its own copy. In a real TTY, interactive exercises now stream their output live and read input from the learner.
- **TUI session (`src/tui/session.ts`):**
  - The transcript follows new output (`followLatest`) when a program runs or a choice is made.
  - A streamed "Proposed plan" can be revealed in full with any key or a click.
  - Running tasks get an `AbortSignal`, so the learner can stop a running program.
  - The choice panel is now sized by `tuiChoiceLayout`. When there are details, they sit in a scroll box that PgUp/PgDn scrolls.
- **Terminal renderer.** Any key skips the plan-document animation and the typed exercise-prompt animation. Before, only space and enter worked.
- **Replay executor.**
  - Commands that aren't shell commands now run through the async runner, with streaming and abort support.
  - On Linux with no display, graphical launches are skipped with a short note.
  - `read` operations show a one-line summary (for PNGs: width × height and size) instead of dumping binary data.

New tests cover each piece, using PTY and driver fixtures under `test/fixtures/`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check` — in sync (pack 2.0.1)
- [x] `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json` — no errors
- [x] `bun test` — 572 pass, 37 skip, 2 fail. Both failures also happen on `main` and come from this sandbox:
  - `system command dependencies > builds native Maven installation plans` expects an APT plan, and the sandbox has no APT package manager.
  - `OpenTUI learning interface > opens progress and command reference as dismissible Home screens` fails because the sandbox has a `code` stub on PATH, so the Home menu takes the "Open VS Code" path.
- [ ] Build and smoke test, book walk, and the macOS and Windows matrix (not run here; left to CI)
- [ ] Live learn tests (`bun run test:learn:live`), which need a real Claude client (not run)

title: Keep learner programs and long prompts responsive inside the TUI
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR implements the "TUI Quality-of-Life Improvements" plan: keep terminal programs inside the TUI with live output and, for interactive steps, an embedded input field, let any ordinary keypress or click reveal long prompts and plans, describe binary image output instead of printing it, return to the latest output after menu selections, and remove synchronous process execution from the asynchronous replay path so long-running commands cannot freeze rendering.

## Design

The core is a new asynchronous process runner in `src/process.ts`, `runAsyncProcess`, with a `ProcessInput` handle that callers use to write to or end a running program's stdin. It reports exit code 124 on timeout and has a separate stop path for Windows. `executePreparedExercise` in `src/commands/run.ts` feeds an `onInputReady` callback through to it when a reader input is attached, and stops a multi-step run after a step exits non-zero, times out, or is aborted. The last command of an interactive step reading reader input gets no execution timeout, and its stdin is an interactive handle when a callback is attached or the inherited terminal otherwise. `runTimeoutMs` now delegates to a new `executionTimeoutMs` helper. `src/learn/native.ts` now uses the executor's stdout/stderr and `aborted` result directly; previously it derived program output from the parsed tool result and checked the abort signal itself.

In the TUI, `LearnTuiSession` jumps back to the latest output after a picker selection with a value or a `run` result, scrolls detail panels with PageUp/PageDown when a detail panel is scrollable, and, for interactive programs, sends end-of-input on Ctrl+D. In the TUI session a skip flag now ends the prompt-typing loop the same way cancellation does; in the markdown renderer an `anyKey` mode lets any key reveal a plan. Detailed pickers are capped at roughly 14 rows or 45% of the terminal height instead of filling it. The replay executor reads PNG and other binary files as a short metadata description rather than raw bytes, reports a graphical step on Linux with no DISPLAY or WAYLAND_DISPLAY as skipped with exit 0, and returns exit 127 for a `<python>` command when Python 3 is unavailable.

## Consequences and limits

- The Windows branch of process stopping did not run in the recorded sessions, which were on linux/x64.
- The interactive TTY path in `run.ts` has not been shown with a user at a real terminal, and the renderer tests replace collaborators with fakes.
- The package version is bumped to 0.13.4 for the release.

New driver fixtures and tests under `test/` cover live streaming with reader input, non-blocking async commands and timeouts, PNG descriptions, compact pickers, and keypress/mouse reveal.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun scripts/sync-content.ts --check`, `bunx tsc -p tsconfig.json`.
- `bun test`: failed (566 pass, 8 fail, Ran 611 tests across 63 files. [467.37s]), run on the submitted content. The repo pins bun 1.4.0 (.bun-version; this environment runs 1.3.14); the failure may reflect this environment rather than the change.

Where to start: `runAsyncProcess` in `src/process.ts`, which owns the stdin handle, timeout exit code, and the Windows stop branch.

Feedback wanted: is stopping a whole multi-step exercise after the first non-zero exit, timeout, or abort the right behavior for books whose later steps were expected to run anyway?

title: Verify every book step in isolation and in sequence
body:
## Summary

Until now, CI ran every exercise step in its own temporary directory. That misses a whole class of learner-facing bugs: a reader works through a book in one persistent workspace, so files left over from earlier steps can break later ones. This PR checks each published step **both in isolation and in book order inside one shared workspace per book**, then gates PRs, `main`, and releases on that walk.

### Verification harness
- `scripts/run-exercises.ts` now has two passes: `--isolated` and `--sequential` (both run by default).
  - The sequential pass keeps one workspace per book. For multi-file project scaffolds, it removes files that an earlier step managed but the current step does not declare, and it respects the scaffold's `clean` list.
  - Each book stops at its first sequential failure, and the workspace is kept for inspection.
  - New flags: `--report <path>` writes a JSON report, `--json` prints that report, and `--keep-workspace` keeps the workspace after a successful run.
  - Steps with an external launch surface are recorded as `delegated` (left to the compiled CLI book walk) and are not counted as passed.
- `scripts/lib/verify.ts`: `verify()` accepts an optional caller-owned `directory`. It only deletes directories that it created itself.

### Content fixes found by the sequential walk (pack 2.0.0 → 2.0.1)
- **Python `py-2-12`**: `math.py` now goes in its own `py-2-12/` project root. Otherwise, in a shared workspace it shadows the standard library `math` module for every later exercise.
- **Java Chapter 6 Maven poms**: these now set `maven.compiler.source/target` to 17, so the build does not depend on Maven's default compiler level.
- **Java Thermostat step**: now cleans the stale `ThermostatApp.java` left by the previous step.

### CI
- New reusable workflow `.github/workflows/exercise-walk.yml`. It sets up Bun, Python 3.12, Temurin 21 (via `actions/setup-java@v5`), Maven, and the JUnit console launcher. It then runs `--isolated --sequential` and always uploads the JSON report as an artifact.
- `ci.yml` replaces the old `run-exercises` job with this workflow. `release.yml` now runs it as a required job (`needs: exercise-walk`) before releasing.
- Tests lock down the workflow wiring, the `py-2-12` path, and the pom compiler level.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check` (repo audit, asset sync, schema validation, `bun test`, and both `tsc` configs): 482 tests pass, typecheck clean.
- [x] `bun scripts/run-exercises.ts --isolated --sequential --report …`: **149 isolated + 149 sequential passed, 14 external launches delegated per pass, 0 failures** (163 steps per pass).
  - Caveat: this machine only has JDK 27. The Byte Buddy version pinned through the Chapter 6 Mockito dependency supports only up to Java 22, so `java-6-15` fails here with `Java 27 (71) is not supported by the current version of Byte Buddy`. That failure also stopped the Java book's sequential pass at that step. The numbers above come from a rerun with `JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS=-Dnet.bytebuddy.experimental=true` set only in this environment. CI pins JDK 21, so it should not hit this.
  - The JUnit console jar was not present locally. In this run, every delegated step was an external launch, so no standalone JUnit step was delegated.
- [ ] The `Full exercise walk` job passes on GitHub Actions (JDK 21 + apt Maven), and the `content-book-walk-report` artifact is uploaded.

title: Verify every book step in order, in shared workspaces, on every PR and release
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The Java exercise java-6-05 broke for a reader in the CLI, a bug that an automated in-order walk of the books should catch. The goal was a harness that runs every sample in both books in order, the way a reader does, and fixes what it finds. Shared project workspaces should drop files left by earlier exercises through an automatic exact checkpoint.

Previously `run-exercises.ts` verified each step on its own in a fresh temporary directory and nothing else. The script now offers two modes, `--isolated` and `--sequential`; when neither flag is given, both modes are selected. The isolated pass keeps the old per-step check. The sequential pass walks each book's steps in document order inside one persistent workspace per book. To make that possible, `verify` accepts a caller-owned `directory` and deletes the workspace when it created it, leaving a caller-supplied one in place. For project steps, `runSequentialBook` removes files from the previous step in that project that are not in the current step's scaffold, plus any `clean` paths, before running the step; non-project steps run in their exercise directory under the book workspace with no such cleanup. A book's walk stops at its first failure. External-launch steps are reported as "delegated" instead of run. A `--report` path writes a JSON summary and per-step results, and `--json` prints that report instead of the console summary. The campaign workspace is deleted when there are no failures and `--keep-workspace` is not set.

Content fixes: the chapter 6 Maven POM now also sets `maven.compiler.source`/`target`, a chapter 6 Java step gains a `clean` entry that removes `src/main/java/ThermostatApp.java` before it runs, and the Python `math.py` exercise gets its own scaffold and project root (`py-2-12`) so it cannot shadow the standard library later. `PACK_VERSION` and `package.json` go from 2.0.0 to 2.0.1.

This change does not include the compiled-CLI harness or the Xvfb window smoke tests from the original plan; external-launch steps are left to that CLI walk.

In CI, a new reusable `exercise-walk.yml` workflow sets up Python 3.12, Java 21, Maven and the JUnit console launcher, calls the script with both modes, and uploads the JSON report as `content-book-walk-report` (kept 14 days) whether that step succeeds or fails; `test-results/book-walk/` is git-ignored. title: fix: make Python replays portable across platforms
body:
## Summary

Python replays recorded from Claude Code sessions ran each captured shell command as `bash -lc "python3 ..."`. That only works on POSIX machines where `python3` is on the PATH. This PR adds a portable way to run those commands and keeps the original tool label (for example `PowerShell` on Windows) for display.

- **Schema and types** (`schema/content.schema.json`, `src/types.ts`)
  - Command operations get an optional `portableCommand` argv. `<shell>` and `<python>` are placeholders that the player fills in for the current platform.
  - Operations and `status` events get an optional `display` block (`toolName`, `description`, `command`) that holds the tool metadata from the authoring session.
  - Command operations get optional `timeoutMs` and `expectedTimeout` fields.
- **Importer** (`scripts/lib/import-showtail.ts`): for Python replays, captured Bash commands now also produce a `portableCommand`, with `python3` rewritten to `<python>` when it's called as `--version`, `-c`, `-m` or `<file>.py`. They also produce a `display` block.
- **Validator** (`scripts/validate.ts`)
  - In Python steps, `bash` commands that use `python`, `rm`, `timeout`, `ls` or inline `VAR=` assignments must have a `<shell>` portable command.
  - An empty `portableCommand` is rejected.
  - `expectedTimeout` without `timeoutMs` is rejected.
- **Content**: `books/ai-first-python-programming.json` and the Showtail e2e and rocket fixtures are regenerated with the new fields.
- **Version**: bumped to 1.7.2.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run check` passed: repository privacy audit (960 files), asset sync, `validate.ts`, `bun test` (459 pass, 0 fail) and both `tsc` passes.
- [x] New audit test: every captured shell command in Python chapters 9 and 10 has a `<shell>` portable command.
- [x] New audit test: `py-9-01` keeps the original `PowerShell` label while running `<python> --version` through the portable command.
- [x] The replay privacy-equivalence test now ignores `display` and `portableCommand`, the same way it already ignores `source`.

## Notes for reviewers

- The players (CLI and VS Code extension) are not in this repo. Until they read `portableCommand`, `display` and `timeoutMs`, they will keep running `command` as before.
- `timeoutMs` and `expectedTimeout` are in the schema and the validator, but the importer doesn't produce them and no content uses them yet.
- A portable command is still a shell script. Some still contain POSIX-style parts such as `/tmp/...` paths, `rm -f` and `$(pwd)`, so whatever shell the player uses for `<shell>` has to handle those.
- In the test fixtures, `display.command` keeps the raw capture paths from the recording (for example `/tmp/aifirst-habit-auto-plan-capture-…/workspace`). The published book has none of these, and the privacy audit passes.

title: Make Python replays portable across platforms
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Previously the importer captured each shell command as `["bash", "-lc", command]` with no portable form. This PR, which continues the in-progress portability work, adds a portable argv and a record of the original tool label to command operations in Python replays, so a consumer can choose a cross-platform form while still showing what the author's agent ran.

**Design.** Replay operations gain two optional fields:

- `portableCommand`: when the importer builds a command operation for a replay whose source paths include a `.py` file, it emits `["<shell>", command]`, with `python3` swapped for `<python>` when followed by `--version`, `-c`, `-m` or an unquoted path token ending in `.py`; other `python3` uses are left as-is.
- `display`: the captured `toolName` (falling back to `"Tool"`), plus `description` and `command` when the captured input had them. These strings are copied from the captured input without further redaction. The importer sets `display` only on those same `.py` command operations, though the schema also allows it on write, edit, read and status events.

Command operations also accept `timeoutMs` (integer, minimum 1) and `expectedTimeout` (boolean). In the regenerated Python book, a chapter 9 command keeps its `PowerShell` label while its portable form runs `<python> --version; <python> -c "import pygame; print(pygame.ver)"`. The audit test checks that every chapter 9 and 10 shell command gets a portable form starting with `<shell>`, and that this label stays separate from the portable command.

**Validation rules.** `validateOperation` now rejects an empty `portableCommand`, and an `expectedTimeout` without `timeoutMs`. For steps whose language is `python`, it also fails a `bash` command whose script mentions `python`, `python3`, `rm`, `timeout`, `ls` or an `UPPER_CASE=` assignment unless its portable form starts with `<shell>`; that flag is threaded through replay events, pre-plan events, workflow interludes and variants. Note the importer gates on `.py` source paths while the validator gates on step language, so a Python step with no `.py` source would get no portable form and could fail validation.

**Consequences.** This diff defines, imports and validates the new fields; it does not include a player that reads `portableCommand` or `display`, so platform behaviour depends on the consumer. The rocket fixture book and the habit-auto-plan, sandwich-custom-plan and train-multiprompt e2e fixture books were regenerated, and the package version moves to 1.7.2.

title: Record the starting exercise a Showtail replay depends on
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The goal is that exercises can be replayed independently of each other: the py-10-01 "Design a Level Editor" replay depends on a chapter 9 file (`level.py`) that comes from the previous exercise. This PR makes an imported replay record which exercise's scaffold it starts from when it depends on that scaffold, so a runner can set up that state before replaying.

Previously `processBundle` handed the previous exercise's scaffold to `deriveReplay` as `initialFiles` without recording which exercise supplied them. It now also hands over `initialExerciseId`, the previous step's (or its parent's) id, when there is a previous exercise and `scaffoldFiles` returned a file map for it.

`deriveReplay` adds a `replayNeedsInitialState` check over the pre-plan events, workflow interlude events and completion events. It returns false when there are no initial files; otherwise it walks the operation events in order, skipping non-operation events, and reports true when a `read` or `edit` touches a path from the initial files before the replay itself has written or edited that path. When that check is true and an initial exercise id was supplied, the `Replay` gets an `initialState: { fromExercise }` field. A replay that never reads or edits a scaffold path before writing it gets no `initialState`.

The `Replay` type and the content JSON schema gain an optional `initialState` object; when present, the schema requires a non-empty `fromExercise` string and allows no other keys. `validate.ts` fails when a replay references an exercise id that does not exist, or one that has no scaffold files. The Python book's chapter 9 and 10 replays now carry `fromExercise` values `py-9-01`, `py-9-02`, `py-9-03`, `py-10-01`, `py-10-02` and `py-10-03`. The chapter 9 and chapter 10 retrofit tests gain cases asserting these links, including that py-9-01 records no starting exercise.

Recording the start state is this PR's scope; the separate picker loop reported for py-9-01 is not addressed by this diff.

title: Run first-time setup from the hosted installers and document the guided learner
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes installing AI First flow straight into setup, as part of carrying out the "Seamless Install and Native Learning" plan, and updates the site copy to describe the guided, account-free learning path.

Previously the hosted installers ended by printing a "Next:" list telling the reader to run `aifirst init` and `aifirst next`, and on a missing PATH entry `install.sh` printed the line to add to the shell's rc file.

**Installer design.** In `static/install.sh`, when the install directory is not already on `PATH`, the script now picks the rc file for zsh, bash (`~/.bash_profile` on macOS, `~/.bashrc` elsewhere) or fish, and creates the rc file's directory if needed and appends a `# Added by aifirst` line plus `export PATH=…` (or `fish_add_path` for fish) when `grep -F` does not already find it there. For an unrecognized shell it prints a note to add the directory later instead. Either way it exports the updated `PATH` for the rest of this run; the profile line takes effect in new terminals. Then, unless `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1`, it runs `aifirst init` against `/dev/tty` when a terminal can be opened, and otherwise prints that interactive setup was skipped. If `init` returns non-zero, it prints "Setup was not completed" and continues. `static/install.ps1` mirrors this: unless `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP` is `1`, it runs `init` when `$IsInteractiveHost` is set, and reports "Setup was not completed" when `init` exits non-zero.

**Site copy.** `content/_index.md` now says the CLI includes a guided offline learner that needs no AI account or tool. `content/cli/_index.md` says AI tools are optional and that running `aifirst` later reopens the readiness checklist and guided menu, replacing the manual `aifirst init` step.

**Consequences.** Piped installs (`curl … | sh`) now become interactive when a TTY is available, and, for zsh, bash and fish, edit the user's shell profile when the directory isn't already on `PATH`. `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` skips the `init` call but not that profile edit. The PowerShell path is Windows-specific and the recorded runs were on linux/x64, so none shows it running. Neither changed script was run by a recorded session command; only the diff shows their behavior.

title: fix: publish macOS installer setup workaround

## Summary

title: Defer macOS installer setup to a new terminal to avoid Bun input bug
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

A macOS user reported that the hosted installer reaches the "Set up 2 tools? [Y/n]" prompt and then accepts no keyboard input, while exiting and running the installed command directly works fine. This PR applies the safe workaround on macOS until a durable fix lands in a Bun release.

## What changes

Previously, `static/install.sh` ran `aifirst init </dev/tty` right after installing whenever `/dev/tty` was readable, regardless of OS. Now, when `$OS` is `darwin`, the script skips the inline setup and instead prints a message telling the user to open a new terminal and run `aifirst init`. Because the `darwin` check comes first, macOS prints this message even when `/dev/tty` is not readable, so the existing no-terminal fallback now applies only to other platforms. Other platforms keep the existing branches unchanged: inline setup when `/dev/tty` is available, the existing fallback otherwise, and `AIFIRST_SKIP_SETUP=1` still skips setup entirely.

The commit message describes this as publishing a macOS installer setup workaround; an in-code comment links the hang to oven-sh/bun#41495, saying Bun cannot poll stdin reopened through the macOS `/dev/tty` alias while a direct invocation inherits the real terminal device.

The CLI page in `content/cli/_index.md` now says that on Linux and Windows the installer continues directly into guided setup, while on macOS users open a new terminal and run `aifirst init` as a temporary extra step, replacing the earlier promise that no second initialization command is needed.

## Consequences

macOS users get one extra manual step after installing, but setup is interactive when they take it. Once the Bun fix ships in a release, the `darwin` branch and the doc sentence should be removed together.

title: Fix stale xdg-desktop-portal after Gaming Mode exit
body:
## Summary

When Gaming Mode exits, Gamescope and Plasma can share the same user systemd manager. That leaves `xdg-desktop-portal` running with no KDE backend, so the KDE portal interfaces (InputCapture, FileChooser, Settings) are missing in the next Plasma session. Deskflow and other Flatpaks then fail.

This adds a teardown hook to the Gamescope template drop-in that stops the generic portal broker. The next Plasma session then starts a fresh one with the correct KDE environment.

```ini
ExecStopPost=-/usr/bin/systemctl --user stop xdg-desktop-portal.service
ExecStopPost=/usr/bin/sudo -n /usr/local/bin/bazzite-clear-autologin.sh
```

- The portal stop runs **before** the autologin backstop. Its `-` prefix makes it best-effort, so a shutdown or an already-closing user bus can't mark the Gamescope unit failed.
- The autologin backstop still reports failures, as before.

## Changes

- `scripts/gamescope-clear-autologin.conf`: new `ExecStopPost` portal-cleanup hook, and updated comments.

title: Stop stale xdg-desktop-portal when Gaming Mode exits
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR fixes a stale desktop portal after leaving Gaming Mode on Bazzite, following a request to inspect the problem and put together a plan to address it, with the user choosing targeted hardening over a broader change. Gamescope and Plasma can share the same user systemd manager, so `xdg-desktop-portal` can survive the switch back to the desktop without its KDE backend, which breaks Flatpaks such as Deskflow.

## Design

The drop-in adds a first `ExecStopPost=-/usr/bin/systemctl --user stop xdg-desktop-portal.service` ahead of the autologin backstop. Stopping only the generic broker during teardown lets the next Plasma session activate it again with the KDE environment. The leading `-` makes the stop best-effort, so that, per the drop-in comment, a closing user bus should not mark the Gamescope unit as broken; the autologin backstop keeps no such prefix. Because the drop-in hooks the `gamescope-session-plus@.service` template, it applies to every client instance.

## Consequences

- The README adds a feature bullet for stopping the Gamescope portal broker on exit, documents the new hook, renames the section to "One-Shot Autologin and Portal Cleanup", and tells users to rerun the installer after updating a checkout.
- A new troubleshooting entry for broken Flatpaks after Gaming Mode shows a `gdbus introspect` check for the InputCapture, FileChooser and Settings interfaces, and restarts `plasma-xdg-desktop-portal-kde.service` and `xdg-desktop-portal.service` to recover the current session.
- The README Tests block lists `./tests/test-units.sh`, and its coverage line now mentions the ordering of the Gamescope cleanup hooks.
- The drop-in comment no longer spells out the `Relogin=true` login-loop reason for clearing autologin twice; the two clears themselves are unchanged.
- A new `tests/test-units.sh` statically checks the hook order and the best-effort prefix, and runs `systemd-analyze --user verify` on the drop-in when the Gamescope base unit is installed (it skips that otherwise).
- `tests/test-ensure.sh` becomes executable and gets shellcheck fixes, including exporting `WAYLAND_SESSION_DIR` in the empty-dir negative test.

title: fix(digest): don't count commands quoted inside scripts or heredocs
body:
## Summary

Command lines were split on `;`, `|`, `&&`, `||` and newlines even inside quotes and heredoc bodies. A line in an inline script that mentioned a test runner (`python -c "..."`, `cat <<'EOF' ... EOF`) therefore counted as a test run, and its grouping key came out wrong, e.g. `bun test',`.

- **New `src/util/shell.ts`** – `splitCommands()` splits on chain and pipe operators but leaves single-, double- and backtick-quoted strings alone (it handles backslash escapes) and skips heredoc bodies (`<<`, `<<-`, quoted or unquoted delimiters). Commands after the heredoc's closing delimiter are still split normally.
- **Digest (`src/digest/build.ts`)** – `testSegment` and `commandKey` now use the splitter. Grouping keys also drop heredoc and redirection tokens (`<<'PY'`, `>`, `2>&1`), so `cd repo && python - <<'PY' …` groups as `python`.
- **Correlation (`src/correlate/correlate.ts`)** – `makesCommit` uses the same splitter, so a `git commit` that appears only in quoted text or a heredoc no longer counts as the session making a commit.
- Fixes the known gap noted in PR #8.
- Version bumped to `1.0.0-rc.12` in all four places, and the bundle is rebuilt.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck`: passes
- `bun test`: 96 pass, 0 fail. The new `tests/shell.test.ts` covers chains and pipes, quoted scripts, escaped quotes, heredoc skipping (including a pipe after the heredoc opener), and test detection and grouping keys.
- `bun run bundle`: the rebuilt `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` matches the committed one.

title: fix(digest): don't count commands quoted inside scripts or heredocs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR exists to dogfood Tracetoon on its own repository, prompted by the request "Can you dogfood this and use it for a PR." The commit message says it fixes a known gap noted in PR #8. According to the commit message, command lines previously were split on `;`, `|` and newlines even inside quotes and heredoc bodies, so a line of an inline script that mentioned `bun test` (a `python -c` string or a quoted heredoc) was classified as a test command, and its grouping key came out as `bun test',`.

**Design.** A new quote- and heredoc-aware splitter, `splitCommands` in `src/util/shell.ts`, now feeds test detection (`testSegment`), command grouping (`commandKey`) and commit detection (`makesCommit`). It walks the line character by character: inside single, double or backtick quotes, separators are kept as text; a backslash escapes the next character outside single quotes. When it sees `<<WORD` or `<<-'WORD'`, it skips from the end of that line to the matching terminator line, then resumes splitting what follows. The terminator may carry leading or trailing spaces or tabs for every heredoc form, and if no terminator line is found, everything after the marker's line to the end of the command is skipped. A `<<<` here-string is also read as a heredoc marker at its second `<`, so later lines are skipped unless a matching terminator line follows.

`commandKey` also drops tokens starting with `<`, `>` or a digit followed by `>`, so heredoc markers and redirections are left out of grouping keys when they follow the program name.

**Consequences.** When a test runner appears inside a quoted script or a terminated heredoc body, the splitter keeps it out of the command list, so test detection and grouping see the real first command instead. The splitter is a heuristic, not a shell parser: it does not handle `$(...)` nesting or ANSI-C `$'...'` quoting specially, so those cases follow the plain quote rules above. Version goes from 1.0.0-rc.11 to 1.0.0-rc.12 and the bundled `dist/tracetoon.mjs` is regenerated.

New tests in `tests/shell.test.ts` cover chains and pipes, quoted scripts, heredoc bodies and what follows them, test detection and grouping keys.

title: Fix preview links and keep unrelated work out of PR digests
body:
Three fixes found while dogfooding tracetoon on its own PRs. Also bumps the version to `1.0.0-rc.8`.

## Preview links you can click (`b95f159`)
`render` and `preview` used to print a bare path. Agents passed it on as a relative path, and users couldn't open it. Both commands now print an absolute `file:///` URL, which you can Ctrl+click in a terminal. They also return it as `previewUrl` in `--json`. The comic image is printed the same way. SKILL.md now tells agents to pass the link on exactly as printed.

## Earlier work and viewed commits no longer leak into a PR's story (`f167fc6`)
- **Turn boundaries:** only edits inside the repo now decide where a turn ends. Before, editing a file outside the repo (notes, a report) after the last base commit pulled a whole earlier turn, prompts included, into the PR.
- **Commit authorship:** a commit SHA only counts as made by the session when it shows up in the output of a command that creates commits (`commit`, `merge`, `cherry-pick`, `revert`, `am`, `rebase`, `pull`), whether run alone or chained. Before, a SHA in any output counted, so running `git log` in another repo claimed authorship of those commits.
- The eval harness now pins two cases whose branches have since been merged or committed, so their results stop changing over time.

## `cd`-prefixed commands are judged by their target directory (`c973ef3`)
Agents log a command with the shell's directory from before it ran. So `cd ../other-repo && bun test` was filed under this repo, and the other repo's test failures showed up in this PR. Commands are now filed under the directory they `cd` into (`src/trace/pathMatch.ts`, `src/correlate/correlate.ts`).

## Testing
