title: fix(digest): keep other repos' work out of a PR's digest
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR keeps work from other repositories and earlier turns out of a PR's digest, and makes the preview link openable: the request was for "a proper link that can be followed in a browser", ideally a URL the user control-clicks to open. Both digest fixes were found while dogfooding this PR. Previously render and preview printed a bare path; per the commit message, agents relayed it as a relative path the user couldn't open.

## Why

Agents log a command with the shell's directory from before it ran, so `cd ../other-repo && bun test` was filed under this repo and its test failures showed up in this PR. Previously a command record belonged to the PR when its cwd was under a repo root or its text mentioned one. Commit detection and turn boundaries had similar leaks: a commit's SHA in any command's output counted as the session having made it, so `git log` in another repo claimed authorship, and a turn's end was judged by every edit, so editing a note outside the repo kept a whole earlier turn in the PR.

## Design

- `leadingCd` reads a leading `cd`, `pushd`, `Set-Location` or `sl`, expands `~` (and, on Windows, Git Bash `/c/` drive paths), and resolves the target against the logged cwd; when a command starts with such a directory change and the target resolves, `belongs` judges it by that directory or by the repo paths it mentions instead of the logged cwd and branch; other commands keep the previous checks.
- `makesCommit` matches commit-making git subcommands (commit, merge, cherry-pick, revert, am, rebase, pull), chained or not, and `commitMoments` credits a commit by SHA to a command when `makesCommit` matches it, while the existing subject match is unchanged.
- `dropEarlierWork` ends a turn at its last edit inside the repo when it has one, and otherwise falls back to the turn's latest record.
- `render` and `preview` print an absolute `file:///` URL via `fileUrl` and return it as `previewUrl` in `--json`; the comic image line uses the same form, and SKILL.md's preview step tells agents to show the title and body and pass the link on exactly as printed.

## Consequences

A PR's digest should stop showing test failures, commits and earlier prompts from other repositories or from earlier turns whose in-repo edits all came before the base commit, even when notes outside the repo were edited later. A `cd` that is not the first command in a chain is not followed, so such commands still fall back to the logged cwd. Unit tests cover `git log` output not counting as a commit, `git commit` in a chain counting, and `leadingCd` resolving a cd-prefixed command's target directory; tests/flow.test.ts asserts `previewUrl` and the Ctrl+click preview line. The eval harness pins two cases whose branches have since merged or been committed, so they stop drifting; and the version moves from 1.0.0-rc.7 to 1.0.0-rc.8 with a regenerated bundle.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (71 pass, 0 fail, Ran 71 tests across 7 files. [22.64s]), `bun run bundle`.

Where to start: `leadingCd` in src/trace/pathMatch.ts, which decides the directory a cd-prefixed command really runs in.

Feedback wanted: should `leadingCd` also follow a `cd` placed after another command in a chain, or does matching just the first command avoid enough false matches?

title: Add --aggregate-only for sealed runs and accept the lean reviewed path in the gate
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The final benchmark needs a set of held-out test cases nobody has looked at, so that tuning cannot contaminate them. The request to switch Codex back to the neo4j subscription is not part of this diff. This PR adds an aggregate-only reporting mode for such sealed runs, and makes two gate changes that came up while preparing them.

**Aggregate-only reports.** `prbench score`, `scripts/paired-delta.ts` and `scripts/qualify-cases.ts` take `--aggregate-only`. With it they print overall tables without per-case rows or deltas, leave-one-case-out ranges or case names; `score` and `paired-delta` show the composite with its interval, W/T/L, errors and cost, while `qualify-cases` shows case counts, consensus and flip shares, composite intervals and error counts. With `--json` as well they emit aggregates; for `score` that is, per root, an arms list and paired deltas without per-case or leave-one-out data. Previously `paired-delta.ts` printed the full result including per-case rows; with the flag, its JSON branch goes through the extracted `aggregatePairedDelta` and its markdown branch hands the flag to `pairedDeltaMarkdown`. Tests assert that no case id appears in aggregate-only output.

**Lean reviewed path in the adoption gate.** The adoption gate and admission now accept a candidate whose current v2 review matches its review plan: distinct reviewer agent ids numbering at least the larger of the planned pass count and lens count, a pass for each planned lens, and the planned reviewer model and effort. When the plan's runner is `tracetoon`, each pass must also come from a Tracetoon run with a verified model. The three-role rule stays an accepted alternative. `meta.workflow` now records the review plan and the reviewer entries read from Tracetoon's `review-plan.json` and `review.json`, and workflow gaps name each unmet requirement. A malformed stored plan is dropped, so the gate reports no review plan recorded.

**Validation unavailable to both arms.** When neither writer completed any validation in any pair, the performance report records `validationUnavailable` and an explicit limitation, listed in the comparison summary too, instead of leaving the gate inconclusive for that alone. Matched, unmatched, one-sided and mixed validation results keep their effect.

Existing test files gain cases for the lean path and its gaps, the stored review plan in the workflow record, and validation unavailable to both writers.

The CHANGELOG and `docs/reproduce-graph-vs-base.md` document the new flag.

<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Tuning the graph candidate across models means many comparison runs, and the goal is for the candidate to match or beat the main skill's composite score at much lower cost, on a cheap model or the same one. This PR lets a comparison skip the native writer and makes the score report show the composite gap directly.

`compare --systems native,baseline,candidate` picks the writer systems for a run; it defaults to all three, requires baseline and candidate, and accepts the short names, the full Tracetoon names and the provider's native name. Baseline and candidate are required because the baseline pairing is the primary comparison, and any other name fails with an "Unknown system" error listing the valid ones. When native is left out, no native writers run and the candidate is judged only against the baseline, in both orders. Previously, rebuild judged the candidate against both the baseline and the provider's native system. Planned counts, rebuild coverage, the quality gate and `--plan` output follow the selected systems: the plan JSON gains `systems` and `judgedAgainst` fields, and `qualityGate` accepts a null native and then checks consensus against the baseline alone.

A subset is stored in the manifest settings, so it becomes part of the experiment identity; a run with all three systems omits the field and keeps its earlier identity. Manifests without the field are read as all three systems. A resume without `--systems` keeps the systems the experiment was frozen with; a resume that names a different set changes the experiment's inputs and is refused like any other input change.

In `accuracyMarkdown`, the candidate-vs-baseline table gains a Composite Δ column: candidate minus baseline over per-case means, with a 95% bootstrap interval over cases.

title: Add crossjudge: judge candidate drafts of one run against baseline drafts of another
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR comes out of planning the next best benchmark run to execute. The approved plan for the next benchmark round notes that the current model comparison rests on composite scores from separate runs, which carry about ±3 points of noise, and that prbench never judges one model's draft against another's. `prbench crossjudge` closes that gap: it pairs the `tracetoon-candidate` drafts of one finished compare run with the `tracetoon-baseline` drafts of another (for example, runs with different writer models), reusing their saved artifacts instead of running any writer.

## Design

Both runs must be `prbench.comparison/v2` experiments with exactly one writer model each, and their judge contract, judges, rubric version, replicates, split and case hashes must match; otherwise the command refuses with the list of differences. The harness running the command must also have the same rubric version and the same judge contract digest as the runs. Every draft is loaded and checked against its receipt before any judge is called, so a missing or mismatched draft fails up front.

When the inputs match, each pair is judged in both orders by every configured judge, through the existing `judgePair` and the stage cache (`--cache`, default `.prbench-cache/v2` beside `--out`), with `--parallel` concurrent pairs (default 4). Results are summarised with the consensus rule `compare` uses for its quality gate (a win only when every judge's two orders agree), plus per-judge and per-case tallies, per-draft composite scores, a factual-error rate and judge cost from stored judgments that carry a cost. `--out` receives the input provenance (`crossjudge.json`), the stored judgments, `pairs.json`, `summary.json` and `summary.md`; if a judge job fails, `pairs.json` is still written with the finished pairs but no summary is, and the CLI exits with status 2. Separately, with `--plan` it only verifies inputs and prints the planned call count, and it does not require a Claude login. Reusing an `--out` that holds a different cross-judge is refused. To share the run layout, `modelRoot` in `src/comparison.ts` is now exported.

## Consequences

A run can be judged against another from saved artifacts, without running a writer again. The tests in `tests/crossjudge.test.ts` use fake judges, so they check the pairing, refusal and summary code around the judges, not real judge output.

title: Retry timed-out judges, fix effort-arm isolation resume, count Codex subagent usage
body:
## Summary

Two commits. They make judging hold up better against timeouts, fix resume for arms that set an effort, and make Codex cost accounting more complete.

### Judges retry instead of invalidating runs
- If a judge call times out or hits a transient error, it is retried up to 3 times with backoff. This also happens on resume when a timeout was saved earlier. Before, the run was invalidated.
- Codex judges now report timeouts as timeouts.
- Each failed judge attempt records which judge it was. The score report gets a judge-reliability table (`collectJudgeFailures`) next to the writer-reliability table.

### Isolation proofs for effort arms
- Probes saved the bare model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`), but resume compared against the arm spec (`claude-sonnet-5-5@medium`). So every resume of an arm with an effort was refused with "Saved isolation proof does not match this experiment."
- Probes now save the arm. Older proofs are matched on the bare model, and the experiment id still pins the exact arms.

### Score: Codex subagent usage, de-duplicated judgments, robustness tables
- Codex writer tokens and estimated cost now add up every thread a run spawns: the main rollout plus forked subagent rollouts. Each model response is counted once, by response id, so parent history replayed into a subagent isn't counted twice. Live runs record `meta.usageScope` (`all-threads` / `main-thread`) and `meta.subagentThreads`.
- For older runs, `score` recomputes all-thread usage from the saved traces of the accepted attempt. The score table says what each cost covers and how many subagents each draft used.
- The judgment walk skips `<order>.json.attempts` folders. Their `NNN.accepted.json` files are byte copies of the final judgments, so they were being counted twice.
- Paired composite deltas now include a leave-one-case-out range. There is also a new per-case composite delta table (candidate minus same-model baseline) for each model.

### Shell-independent writer environment hash
- The writer environment identity (Codex and Claude) now ignores shell, terminal and session bookkeeping such as `PWD`, `SHLVL`, `_`, `TERM_SESSION_ID` and `CLAUDE_*`. Experiments frozen with the old hash keep it as long as it still matches.

## Testing
- `bun run typecheck`: passes.
- `bun run prbench validate`: passes.
- `bun run test`: 251 pass, 1 skip, 3 fail on the first run. All 3 failures came from this environment: the host shell had `TRACETOON=0` exported, and it leaked into the fake writer fixtures (`tracetoonOff` was `"0"` instead of undefined) in `tests/agents.test.ts`, `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` and `tests/codex.test.ts`. With `env -u TRACETOON`, those three files pass (37/37). I did not re-run the whole suite with the variable unset.
- New and updated tests: `tests/codex-usage.test.ts`, `tests/environment-hash.test.ts`, `tests/score.test.ts`, `tests/recovery.test.ts`, `tests/comparison.test.ts`, `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts`.

title: Retry timed-out judges, count Codex subagent usage, and accept effort-arm isolation proofs
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR keeps comparison runs going when a judge call times out, lets runs with effort arms resume, and makes Codex writer cost cover subagent threads.

**Judges.** `judgeOnce` retries timed-out and transient judge calls up to 3 attempts with backoff, also when resuming from a saved timeout, and stops early on cancellation. The Codex judge provider throws a timeout error when its call times out. Failed attempts record which judge made them, and the score report gains a judge-reliability table beside writer reliability.

**Isolation proofs.** Previously, probes saved the bare model while resume compared against the arm spec (`model@effort`), so every resume of an arm with an effort was refused. Probes now record the full arm; proofs saved before that match on the bare model, with the experiment id still binding the exact arms.

**Codex usage.** Previously, `parseCodexResult` summed token usage from the `codex exec --json` events alone. Live runs now read the new rollouts from the sandbox `CODEX_HOME`, sum the main rollout plus any forked subagent rollouts found there while counting each model response once by response id, and record `usageScope` (`all-threads` when the rollouts hold at least the main thread's input tokens, otherwise `main-thread`) and the subagent thread count. For older Codex runs without a recorded cost, `score` recomputes all-thread usage from the accepted attempt's saved traces when they are kept and hold at least the recorded input tokens, and the score table says what each cost covers and how many subagents ran per draft.

**Score robustness.** The judgment walk skips `.attempts` folders so judgments are counted once, and paired composite deltas gain a leave-one-case-out range plus a per-case delta table per model.

**Environment hash.** The writer environment identity for both Codex and Claude ignores shell, terminal and session bookkeeping such as `PWD`, `SHLVL` and `CLAUDECODE`; variables that can change a writer, such as `PATH`, `TMPDIR` and `LANG`, still count. An experiment frozen with the legacy hash keeps it while that hash still matches the current environment.

The artifact schema accepts the new optional `meta.usageScope` and `meta.subagentThreads` fields. `tests/codex-usage.test.ts` covers subagent usage, `tests/environment-hash.test.ts` the shell-independent hash, `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` resuming with a saved effort-arm proof, `tests/comparison.test.ts` a timed-out judge call, `tests/recovery.test.ts` judge retries on resume, and `tests/score.test.ts` the reliability and per-case tables. The comparison tests drive a fake comparison setup, so they exercise the code around it rather than real judge and writer processes.

title: Run comparisons in parallel, end to end on Codex or Claude
body:
## Summary

Runs comparisons in parallel, end to end on Codex or Claude.

- **`--provider codex|claude|both`** picks who writes and who judges. A comparison never mixes the two model families. `both` runs two independent comparisons into `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`, and each provider judges its own run. The two runs are reported separately and never pooled.
  - Claude writers are `claude-native` plus baseline and candidate Tracetoon on Opus and Sonnet (effort medium), with Opus and Sonnet as judges.
  - `compare` can choose the writer models while keeping the provider's judges.
- **`--parallel <n>`** (default 4) runs up to n writers, judges and isolation probes at once per provider. It uses a new job pool (`src/run/pool.ts`) and cancellation (`src/run/cancellation.ts`).
  - Judges start as soon as both drafts they compare exist.
  - `--parallel 1` keeps the serial order.
  - Frozen inputs, cache keys and reports don't depend on the setting.
  - After a failure no new job starts. Running jobs finish and are saved, and `--resume` continues.
- **Credentials:** concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login file through a link, so refreshed tokens are never overwritten. Windows keeps the exclusive copy mode. Claude uses a long-lived setup token (`prbench auth claude`).
- **Judging:** a per-prompt schema constrains judge references (`src/judge/rubric.ts`).
- **Fixes:**
  - Windows-recorded cases now replay correctly on POSIX hosts.
  - The launch directory is no longer part of the Claude environment identity.
  - An escaped dot in a shell glob is no longer read as an absolute host path.
  - The sandbox's fake `gh` treats `--help` as help.
- README documents providers and parallel runs.

## Testing

- `bun run typecheck` passes.
- `bun run test`: 226 pass, 1 skip, 3 fail. The 3 failures are environmental: the host shell exports `TRACETOON=0`, which leaks into the fake Claude/Codex fixtures. These are the tests that assert Tracetoon's env var is unset. Rerun with `env -u TRACETOON`, all 3 pass.

title: Run comparisons in parallel, end to end on Codex or Claude
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Users have Claude or ChatGPT but rarely both, so this PR lets `prbench compare` run end to end on one provider (writers and judges) or on both separately, never mixing them, and runs writers and judges in parallel.

`compare --provider codex|claude|both` picks who writes and who judges. Codex keeps Sol and Terra and its frozen identity; claude runs Claude Code on Opus and Sonnet at medium effort with the same models judging; both runs two independent comparisons in `<out>/codex` and `<out>/claude`. Each comparison uses one provider for both writers and judges, and a frozen experiment refuses to resume under another provider. Previously the comparison loop hard-coded `codex-native` as the native system and threw "Codex CLI unavailable." A new `claudeComparisonSystem` runs the Claude arms, installing the pinned skill only for the Tracetoon arm. Claude writers get the frozen skill and runtime, a stripped Anthropic and Claude Code environment, no MCP servers, no USD budget cap, and an early stop on the result event. A Claude isolation probe reads the startup catalogue; Claude judges run with no tools and no hooks. `prbench auth claude` stores a setup token (mode 0600).

`--parallel <n>` (default 4) bounds concurrency: writers and judges share one job graph where a judge runs once the two drafts it compares exist, isolation probes run beforehand under the same limit, and results are persisted in a fixed order. With `--provider both`, the two runs start together and their output lines are prefixed `[codex]` or `[claude]`. After a writer or judge failure nothing new starts and running jobs finish and are saved. Concurrent Codex runs share the dedicated login through a symlink instead of queuing on exclusive copies; Windows keeps the copy mode.

To test whether a cheaper writer can match a stronger one, `compare --models <ids>` replaces the writer models while the provider's judges stay the same; ids must be distinct, and `--provider both` refuses the option.

Fixes found while running comparisons:
- Claude judges invented fact IDs and cited the other draft's evidence, so each judge call now gets a schema whose reference fields are enums of the IDs that side may cite (when that side has IDs of that kind).
- The Claude profile hashed PWD, OLDPWD, INIT_CWD and npm_* variables, which blocked `--reuse-from` from another directory; writers run in their own sandbox cwd, so these are dropped, and the Codex hash is unchanged.
- On Linux, a Windows-recorded checkout was named with the whole Windows path and session paths kept backslash tails, so both Tracetoon arms lost edit attribution; the checkout is now named by the recorded path's last segment, and unrelated host paths keep their spelling; the commit message reports 92 linked replayed edits on pr8 and 45 on pr5, up from 0.
- The scope audit turned the escaped dot in `rg --files -g '!\.agents/**'` into `/.agents/**` and rejected the draft; such a backslash is now dropped when the token continues without backslashes.
- A writer's `gh pr create --help` counted as a second, empty PR; the fake `gh` now treats help invocations as help.

The Claude and parallel tests replace `claude`, `codex` and `gh` with fakes, so they cover the orchestration rather than the real CLIs. The interactive terminal handling in `src/cli.ts` has no keyboard-driven coverage.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

title: Performance gate: pass on paired priced cost per draft, not time and tokens
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes prbench's performance gate decide on what a draft costs rather than on writer wall time and input tokens, so a candidate that is slower or reads more cached input but is cheaper per draft is not held back.

Previously the gate's verdict rested on per-model writer wall time and median input tokens; it now pools all models into one cost ratio.

**Design.** The criterion is a candidate/baseline geometric mean of paired per-draft priced cost at most 1.000, with pairs sharing model, case and replicate and log ratios averaged within each case and then across cases. The case-clustered 95% interval is reported but not required. Cost comes from a new shared `draftCost` in `src/report/score.ts`, which `collectDraftScores` now also calls, so the gate and `prbench score` price a draft the same way: the reported total where the agent gives one, otherwise an estimate pricing each model at its own rate and cached input at its own rate, with Codex counted across all threads when that usage is found.

**Consequences.** When any paired draft has no priced cost (a model without a price, missing token counts, a zero or non-finite cost, or Codex usage covering only the main thread), the gate is inconclusive and lists those drafts in `unpricedDrafts` and `summary.md`, which also prints the rule and labels the cost ratio as the criterion. Writer wall time and token counts stay in the report as information, not criteria. Validation-comparability handling is unchanged. The report schema moves from `prbench.performance/v2` to `v3`, and changing `src/performance.ts` changes the gate policy hash, per the changelog. Prices are list prices from `src/report/prices.json`, not billed amounts. The existing performance and comparison tests were updated to the new rule.

title: Score drafts on an absolute scale, add writer effort, and retry failed writers
body:
Adds absolute per-draft scoring (`prbench score`), cost estimates for runs that report no price, and writer effort as part of a compare arm. Also makes compare runs survive single writer failures by retrying them instead of stopping the run.

## Scoring
- `prbench score <roots…>`, plus a Scores section in every compare summary. For each draft it reports coverage (claims, context, uncertainties), the rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, averaged over all judgments of that draft. It also gives a documented 0–100 composite, case-clustered bootstrap intervals and paired candidate deltas. Works on old runs too.
- Accuracy section: the error rate per arm (share of judgments with ≥1 factual error, case-clustered CI) and error classes (validation, code structure, attribution, motivation, pipeline). Every candidate arm is compared with every baseline arm, with a 0.05 claim-coverage guard and the cost ratio.
- `src/report/prices.json` estimates USD from token counts when a run reports no cost (Codex).

## Writer effort
- `compare --models model@effort` makes effort part of the arm. Writers get the bare model and that effort (default `medium`, same as before), and saved artifacts must match both.
- Isolation probes run at the configured effort, not the arm's. Haiku@low misreported the skill path in the probe and stopped whole runs.

## Writer retries
A writer is retried up to 3 attempts, in a fresh sandbox each time, when it:
- **leaves no draft**: for example, Luna@low refused to publish, and Sonnet@low ran `gh pr create --fill`. `failure.json` now names the arm.
- **is rejected by the scope audit**: for example, one mistyped absolute path outside the sandbox. The rejected draft is never scored. Output is now cached only after the audit passes, so a retry no longer hits an immutable cache entry.
- **times out**.

Compare and score summaries add a writer reliability table with columns for no-draft, scope-rejected and timed-out attempts.

The fake `gh` now supports `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose`, taking the title and body from the branch's commits. Explicit `--title`/`--body` take precedence.

## Testing
- `bun run typecheck`: passes.
- `bun run test`: 237 pass, 1 skip, 3 fail. The 3 failures are in `tests/agents.test.ts`, `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` and `tests/codex.test.ts`. They happen because this environment exports `TRACETOON=0`, which the fake writers record and the tests expect to be unset. With `env -u TRACETOON`, those three files pass (36/36).
- New tests: `tests/score.test.ts`, plus retry, scope-audit and timeout cases in `tests/arm.test.ts`, `tests/comparison.test.ts` and `tests/sandbox.test.ts`.

title: Score drafts on an absolute scale, run writers at a chosen effort, and retry failed writers
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR moves the benchmark from A/B preference toward an absolute score, because a preference between two drafts cannot show how much better a writer is getting, and lets writers run at a lower effort so that axis can be tested.

## Design

`prbench score <roots…>` and a Scores section in compare summaries report per-draft coverage (claims, context, uncertainties), rubric, factual errors, unsupported claims and traps, averaged over all judgments of a draft, with a 0-100 composite. Per the commit message, this works on old runs retroactively; only judgments at rubric version 6 with a loaded fact sheet are scored. Components are fractions of the fact sheet and rubric over applicable items; when an item count is zero the fraction is 1. Coverage weighs claims 35, context 15, uncertainties 15 and rubric 35; each factual error subtracts 15, each unsupported claim 7 and each trap 10, and the composite does not go below zero. `src/report/prices.json` estimates USD from token counts when a run reports none (Codex), so cost and score can be compared per draft. An Accuracy section adds an error rate per arm, error classes, and each candidate arm against each baseline arm.

`compare --models model@effort` makes effort part of the arm: writers get the bare model and that effort (default medium, as before), and a saved artifact must match the model, plus the effort when the spec names one. Previously the writer received the full model string and a fixed effort of "medium". Arms are checked against the provider's efforts and must be distinct. Isolation probes use the bare model at the configured effort, not the arm's, because low-effort models misreport the skill path; the commit message cites Haiku@low stopping whole runs this way.

## Consequences

According to the commit message, a low-effort writer can finish without a PR: Luna@low refused to publish, and Sonnet@low ran `gh pr create --fill`, which the fake gh recorded without a title; per the commit message, both invalidated whole runs. `failureKind` now classifies "produced no PR" as `no-draft`, retried like a transient failure (3 attempts). A draft the scope audit rejects stays rejected and is never scored; a new sample runs in a fresh sandbox, so one mistyped absolute path no longer invalidates a run. A scope-rejected sample is not cached, so its retry does not hit the immutable cache entry. A writer that hits the timeout is retried the same way; a failure on the third attempt is still raised. The writer reliability table counts scope-rejected and timed-out attempts per arm. The fake gh now takes `--fill`, `--fill-first` and `--fill-verbose` from the branch's commits, with explicit `--title`/`--body` winning. A test has the fake Codex writer type one mangled out-of-sandbox path and expects one recorded scope failure. Those comparison tests replace the writer and gh with fakes, so they check the logic around those steps, not the real steps.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run prbench validate`, `bun run test` (240 pass, 0 fail, Ran 241 tests across 34 files. [274.89s]).

title: Keep shell bookkeeping out of writers and out of the environment identity
body:
## Summary

You couldn't resume a Claude comparison from a new shell. The Claude environment hash covered every inherited variable, including per-process ones like `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`, so a new shell produced a new hash. Those same variables also reached writers, so a host session's `CLAUDE_EFFORT` could change a writer's effort.

- `src/run/provider.ts`: `claudeComparableEnv()` skips exactly that list. The hash still changes when anything a writer can see changes.

title: Keep shell bookkeeping out of writers and out of the Claude environment identity
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR lets a Claude comparison resume from a new shell that differs only in per-shell bookkeeping, and keeps that bookkeeping and the host session's `CLAUDE_*` variables away from writers. It came out of work on optimizing how the evidence graph is built and retrieved for PR drafting, measured by comparison runs that had to be cancelled and restarted. As the commit message puts it, the environment hash covered every inherited variable, including per-process ones like `CLAUDE_PID` and `INVOCATION_ID`, so a comparison could not resume from a new shell. The commit message also reports that the same variables reached writers, so `CLAUDE_EFFORT` from the host session could change a writer's effort.

`sandbox.ts` now exports `VOLATILE_ENV`, a set of per-login and per-process names (systemd, D-Bus, XDG session, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`, `SHLVL`, `OLDPWD`, `_` and similar), and `VOLATILE_PREFIXES` (`KONSOLE_`, `CLAUDE_`). Previously the sandbox's dropped prefixes were `CODEX_`, `ANTHROPIC_` and `CLAUDE_CODE_`; they are now `CODEX_`, `ANTHROPIC_`, `KONSOLE_` and `CLAUDE_`, which subsumes `CLAUDE_CODE_`. `sandboxEnv` now removes any variable whose upper-cased name matches a dropped prefix or appears in `DROPPED_ENV` or `VOLATILE_ENV`, which covers `CLAUDE_PID` and `CLAUDE_EFFORT` from the host session. `claudeComparableEnv` in `provider.ts` imports the same two lists and skips a variable when it is in `VOLATILE_ENV` or starts with a volatile prefix, alongside its existing exclusions.

The consequence is that the environment hash ignores the volatile names and prefixes the sandbox strips, so it still changes when a variable a writer can see changes. Because the hash now skips these variables, a Claude environment hash recorded before this change will differ from the new one whenever that environment contained any of them. One asymmetry to note: the sandbox compares upper-cased names, while the hash filter compares names as given, so a lower-case spelling of a volatile name would be dropped from writers but still counted in the hash.

A new test in `tests/claude-comparison.test.ts` sets `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, `INVOCATION_ID` and `SHLVL`, checks that the Claude environment hash is unchanged and that none of them appears in a created sandbox's env, then sets an unrelated variable and checks that the hash does change.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run prbench validate`, `bun run test` (230 pass, 0 fail, Ran 231 tests across 32 files. [263.23s]).

Where to start: `sandboxEnv` in `src/run/sandbox.ts`, which owns dropping the volatile names and prefixes before a writer starts.

Feedback wanted: is `VOLATILE_ENV` missing any per-shell variable you see on your machines (for example from tmux, screen or other terminals), and should the hash filter upper-case names the way the sandbox does?

title: fix: recover shell exit codes from Claude results
body:
## Summary
Claude Code transcripts sometimes report a failed Bash call only in the `tool_result` text (for example `Exit code 1\nModuleNotFoundError: …`) and leave out any structured `exitCode` / `exit_code` / `code` field. Because of that, structured `tool_result` events in exported reports had no `exitCode` for those failures.

- `src/core/claudeCode.ts`: adds `resultTextExitCode`, which reads a leading `Exit code N` line from the result content. It is used only when neither the structured result nor the content block has a numeric exit code. The regex is anchored to the start of the text, and the match must be followed by a newline or the end of the text.
- `tests/claudeToolCall.test.ts`: the failed-Bash fixture now uses Claude's `Exit code 1` prefix, and the test checks that the `tool_result` event has `exitCode: 1, isError: true`.

title: fix(claudeCode): recover shell exit codes from Claude result text
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR makes Showtail's Claude Code importer keep a command's exit status in its structured conversation events; the surrounding work uses the chapter 9 material as acceptance criteria, which is context for this fix rather than something the diff implements. Per the new helper's comment, Claude sometimes puts the status in the result text, as a leading `Exit code N` line, rather than in a numeric field. Previously `rawToolResult` read the exit code from the structured result's numeric fields and then from the tool_result block's fields, with no fallback to the text, so such a result carried no exit code.

## Design

`rawToolResult` keeps the same lookup order and adds a final fallback: when neither the structured result nor the tool_result block carries an integer exit code, it calls the new helper `resultTextExitCode` on the block's `content`. The helper returns nothing when the content is not a non-empty string, and nothing when the text does not start with `Exit code` followed by an optionally negative integer and then a line break or the end of the text; the match is case-sensitive and needs exactly one space, so `exit code 1` or `Exit code: 1` sets no code. When the pattern matches, it returns the parsed number if it is an integer, so `Exit code 0` yields 0 as well. A numeric field, when present, still wins over the text, so results that already carried a structured code are unchanged.

## Consequences

When a tool_result has no numeric exit code field and its content starts with an `Exit code N` line, the exported result now carries that `exitCode`. The match is anchored to the first line, so output that merely mentions "Exit code" later in the text does not set a code. The Bash fixture in `tests/claudeToolCall.test.ts` now starts its content with `Exit code 1`, and the matching event is expected to have `exitCode: 1` and `isError: true`; it exercises the text fallback itself, not the numeric-first precedence or the first-line anchoring. `isError` is still read from `is_error` or the structured result, independent of the recovered code.

## Validation

title: feat: add self-upgrade command

## Summary

Adds `showtail upgrade`, so a standalone installer build can update itself to the latest GitHub Release without running the installer again.

- **Resolves the release asset** for the current platform/arch (`src/core/selfUpgrade.ts`) and compares semver. Possible outcomes: `current`, `newer` (local build is ahead, so nothing changes), `upgraded`, or `pending` (Windows).
- **Checks the download before replacing anything.** If the binary is empty or `--version` doesn't print the expected version, the upgrade is aborted.
- **Updates the bundled editor extension** (`showtail.vsix`) and refreshes capture integrations by running `setup --first-run --json`.
- **Leaves Bun/source-managed copies alone** and tells the user to update them the way they were installed.
- **Windows:** the running `.exe` is locked, so the swap is done by a PowerShell script that runs right after the command exits.
- `upgrade` is added to `NO_BOOTSTRAP`, so running it doesn't trigger first-run setup. It sits under a new "Maintain Showtail" help group and supports `--json`.
- Docs: README, installation guide, CLI reference, classroom workflow, and an Unreleased CHANGELOG entry.

title: feat: add `showtail upgrade` to self-update installer builds
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
## Why

This PR adds a `showtail upgrade` command so an installed copy can update itself in place, as requested: "Make a showtail upgrade command to upgrade showtail from an install so users don't have to re-run the installer."

## Design

`runUpgrade` in `src/commands/upgrade.ts` calls `selfUpgrade` in `src/core/selfUpgrade.ts`, which looks up the latest GitHub Release, picks the asset matching the current platform and architecture, and compares versions numerically. When the installed version equals or is newer than the release, it returns `current` or `newer` without downloading anything. Otherwise it downloads the binary into the install directory, runs the downloaded copy's `--version` to confirm it reports the expected release, then downloads the bundled `showtail.vsix`.

On Linux and macOS the existing binary and extension are moved to backups, the new files are renamed into place, and the backups are restored if a replacement step throws; after a successful swap it invokes `setup --first-run` to refresh capture integrations. An unsuccessful refresh leaves the upgrade in place; the result reports `integrationsRefreshed: false` and the command prints that integrations will refresh the next time Showtail starts. On Windows, where a running executable can't be replaced, it writes a helper script that waits for the process to exit, swaps both files and refreshes hooks, and the command reports `pending` once that helper is launched. The helper gives up after 30 seconds if Showtail is still running, and because it is detached, an unsuccessful Windows swap is not reported back by `showtail upgrade`. Before any network request, the command refuses to proceed unless the running executable is named `showtail` (or `showtail.exe` on Windows), which turns away a Bun/source invocation. `upgrade` also skips the first-run bootstrap that other commands perform. `--json` emits the result object for scripts.

## Consequences

The release lookup honours `SHOWTAIL_REPO`, so forks can point upgrades at their own releases, and sends `GITHUB_TOKEN` as a bearer token when it is set. When an update is needed, a release without a `showtail.vsix` asset is rejected before anything is downloaded. The README, installation guide, classroom workflow, CLI reference and changelog now describe the command.

The recorded runs were on linux/x64, so none shows the macOS, arm64 or Windows replacement paths running outside of the unit tests' fakes.

title: Prepare SignPath Foundation code signing and harden release pipeline
body:
## Summary

Prepares Showtail for code signing through the SignPath Foundation, and hardens the release and CI supply chain to match what the Foundation expects.

**Release pipeline (`.github/workflows/release.yml`)**
- New `validate` job: the tag must match `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, agree with `package.json` and `src/core/version.ts`, and point to a commit that is on `main`.
- Default permissions drop to `contents: read`. A concurrency group keeps two releases from running at once.
- The Windows executable is built with PE metadata (`scripts/build-windows.ps1`), uploaded unsigned, and sent to SignPath. The job then checks that the signer is SignPath Foundation before it publishes anything. Signing won't start until `SIGNPATH_ENABLED`, `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID` and `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN` are configured.
- An SPDX SBOM, licenses and checksums are attached to the release.
- Actions are pinned to commit SHAs, and Bun is pinned to the version in `.bun-version`.

**CI and repository hygiene**
- Added CodeQL, Dependabot, CODEOWNERS and a dependency-review workflow. Dependency review only runs when `vars.DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED == 'true'`, because the action hard-fails while Dependency Graph is disabled.
- New `license:check` script (`scripts/verify-licenses.ts`) and `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.
- Build scripts are split into `build-non-windows.sh` and `build-windows.ps1`.

**Docs and policy**
- `docs/code-signing-policy.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `.signpath/` artifact configuration, and `.github/SIGNPATH_APPLICATION_CHECKLIST.md`.
- New uninstallation guide. The privacy and installation pages are expanded, and `install.sh`/`install.ps1` now print where to find uninstall instructions.

**Tests**
- `tests/signingReadiness.test.ts` checks that the signing and policy pieces stay consistent.

## Maintainer follow-up after merge
- Turn on Dependency Graph, then set `DEPENDENCY_REVIEW_ENABLED=true`.
- Once SignPath onboarding is done, set `SIGNPATH_ENABLED`, `SIGNPATH_ORGANIZATION_ID` and the `SIGNPATH_API_TOKEN` secret. **Until then, tagged releases fail at the Windows signing step.**
- Work through `.github/SIGNPATH_APPLICATION_CHECKLIST.md` before applying.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun run typecheck`: passes
- [x] `bun run format:check`: passes
- [x] `bun run license:check`: passes

The failures are in hook/stdin capture and session-lifecycle tests, which this PR doesn't touch, so they look environmental. Please confirm on CI.

body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR prepares the repository for a later SignPath Foundation application for Windows code signing: the project must be clearly open-source licensed and meet the foundation's published requirements, while the application itself waits until public reputation evidence exists. The checklist notes the foundation can still reject an application that meets every requirement. The signed scope is only `showtail-windows-x64.exe`, and Apache-2.0 stays the project license.

**Release pipeline.** Previously the release workflow copied whichever `showtail-*.vsix` was newest; it now copies the file named for the extension's version. The single release build job is replaced by `validate`, separate non-Windows and Windows build jobs, and a `publish` job that needs all three. `validate` fails unless the tag is `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`, matches the versions in `package.json` and `src/core/version.ts`, and points at a commit reachable from `main`. The Windows job fails until the `SIGNPATH_ENABLED` variable is `true` and the SignPath organization ID and API token are configured; it then uploads the unsigned executable and submits an origin-verified signing request. The workflow token drops to `contents: read`, only `publish` gets `contents: write`, and releases also attach an SPDX SBOM, `SHA256SUMS`, the license and third-party notices. `.signpath/artifact-configuration.xml` describes the signed artifact.

**Builds and license checks.** `build-all.sh` now delegates to `build-non-windows.sh`, so the Windows executable comes only from `build-windows.ps1` on Windows, which fails when the package version, embedded version or another metadata field doesn't match. **Docs and repository policy.** The PR adds a code-signing policy, uninstallation docs, `SECURITY.md`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`, workflow CODEOWNERS, Dependabot and CodeQL. The privacy page's promise of no external API calls is replaced by a list of user-initiated network operations and the third-party services involved. title: Migrate legacy trails from local AI-tool transcripts
body:
## Summary

Older trails can now get back the transcript detail that newer Showtail versions capture.

- **`showtail migrate [tool]`** matches existing sessions to local Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI/IDE, Copilot CLI and Copilot Chat transcripts. It then appends any replies, edits, plans, decisions, models, tool calls/results and recap stats the trail is missing. It supports `--dry-run`, `--json`, `--session`, `--file` and `--yes`. `showtail migrate undo [batch-id]` removes a migration batch.
- **One-time upgrade offer.** The first time an existing generation-1 install runs an interactive command, it offers a home-directory scan for projects, shows one bulk preview and asks for one confirmation. Fresh installs never see the offer. Non-interactive runs put it off until the next terminal command. Bulk progress is kept in `~/.showtail-cli/migrations/` and can be resumed with `--resume`.
- **The old trail is never rewritten.** Recovery only appends, through enrichment records. Each record says when the recovery ran and names its source by provider session id and transcript digest, never by an absolute path.
- **Supporting changes:**
  - Each plugin gets a `migration` hook (`discover` / `read` / `planFiles`).
  - Transcript readers can optionally keep edits (`includeEdits`).
  - A `knownProjects` registry in the global config, kept up to date by `init` and hooks.
  - `projectDiscovery.ts` for the bulk scan.
  - Docs and CHANGELOG are updated.

### Fix included in this PR

The second commit fixes a regression introduced by the first. `migrate.ts` and `upgrade.ts` used `import { stdin, stdout } from 'node:process'`. Under Bun, that opens stdin as soon as the module loads. `cli.ts` imports both modules eagerly, so every `showtail hook …` call lost its stdin payload before `readHookPayload()` read it, and prompts and edits were silently dropped. Both files now read `process.stdin` / `process.stdout` only when needed.

## Testing

- New tests: `migrate.test.ts`, `migrateAll.test.ts`, `projectDiscovery.test.ts`, plus additions to `globalConfig`, `plugins`, `antigravityCliTranscript` and `firstRunSetup`.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- `bun test`: 673 pass, 4 skip, **9 fail**. All 9 also fail on `main` in this sandbox (from `codex install --no-hooks`, `reattach`, `showtail move` and sole-writer mode), so none come from this branch. On `main` the same run gave 15 failures.
- Before the stdin fix this branch had 61 failures, mostly hook end-to-end tests.

The repo's `CLAUDE.md` describes a no-PR, land-straight-to-`main` workflow. This PR was opened because it was explicitly requested.

title: feat: migrate legacy trails from local AI-tool transcripts
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
Older Showtail trails can lack replies, edits, plans, decisions and tool calls that AI tools still retain in local transcripts. This PR implements the plan "V1-to-V2 Transcript Migration and Upgrade Workflow": an append-only migrator for Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI/IDE, Copilot CLI and Copilot Chat transcripts, plus a one-time offer, when an existing install upgrades, to migrate the eligible projects that discovery finds.

**Design.** The six local-transcript plugins (Claude Code, Codex, Antigravity CLI and IDE, Copilot CLI, Copilot Chat) gain a `migration` capability, and `migrationPlugins` in the registry collects the plugins whose transcripts can enrich trails. `showtail migrate [tool]` enriches the active project; `--dry-run` previews and `--json` emits machine output, and `migrate undo` reverses a batch. Migration appends enrichment records and overlays rather than rewriting journal entries; the tests cover enriching a legacy session without duplicating its events and a dry run that writes no batch. Previously `findProjectTranscripts` skipped any transcript whose cwd did not match the project root inside the loop, and that loop now skips entries with no cwd. With `--json` or `--yes`, `migrate` skips the interactive preview and match prompt and applies the batch; only `--dry-run` writes nothing. `migrate undo` rewrites the journal to drop the batch's lines and records a `migration-undo` marker, which `verify` treats like an `import-undo` one. `latestBatchId`, the default target of `import undo`, now skips migration batches (`mig_` ids or batches named by enrichment records).

**Upgrade path.** A machine-wide config records known projects and a history generation (`HISTORY_GENERATION = 2`); an existing generation-1 install gets one pending generation-2 offer, while a machine with no prior global config is treated as a fresh install. The installers call `setup --first-run --offer-migration`. Without a terminal, `maybeOfferHistoryMigration` returns before prompting, so the offer stays pending. Bulk discovery walks the home directory (skipping symlinks and pruned folder names) and also adds the current directory, known projects, ledger-indexed trails and each transcript's recorded cwd; it skips a home catch-all and migrates each eligible project independently.

**Limits.** The `win32` lower-casing branch in `migration.ts` and `projectDiscovery.ts` and the `install.ps1` change are Windows code, while the recorded runs were on linux/x64. The interactive prompts in `migrate` and `upgrade` need a terminal, which the recorded checks did not have.

Antigravity CODE_ACTION edit recovery applies in migration mode while live reconcile still drops those edits, as a test covers; other tests cover local coding tools exposing transcript migration. The CHANGELOG, CLI reference, installation and data-layout docs describe the command and the machine-wide config.

On Windows, VS Code-compatible CLIs (`code`, the Antigravity launcher) are `.cmd` batch files. `spawnSync` goes through `CreateProcess`, which can't run batch files directly. That includes a bare `code` that PATHEXT resolves to `code.cmd`. So the extension install failed on Windows.

- Adds `src/core/extensionCli.ts`:
  - `extensionCliInvocation()` sends every Windows launch through the command processor (`%ComSpec%`, falling back to `cmd.exe`) as `cmd /d /c <cli> ...args`.
  - On POSIX the CLI is run directly, as before.
  - Arguments are passed as separate tokens, so Node/Bun quote them. This covers paths with spaces (`Program Files`, temp dirs).
- `installVsCodeExtension()` and `installAntigravityIdeExtension()` now call the shared `runExtensionCli()` instead of calling `spawnSync` themselves.
- Adds unit tests for the invocation shape on win32 (bare `code` and a full `code.cmd` path under `Program Files`) and on POSIX.
- Includes the branch's `.showtail/` provenance trail, which this repo commits on purpose.

## Testing

- `bun test tests/vscodeExtension.test.ts`: 8 pass, 0 fail
- `bun x tsc --noEmit`: clean
- `prettier --check` on the changed files: clean
- Full `bun test`: 622 pass, 4 skip, 62 fail. A clean `main` checkout in the same environment fails 65 tests, and every test failing on this branch also fails there. The failures are in hook and session end-to-end suites, not in the code this PR touches.

title: fix: launch extension CLIs through cmd on Windows
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR fixes how the VS Code and Antigravity extension installers launch their CLI on Windows, because the Windows launch path for these installers blocks tagging a new release.

Previously, `installVsCodeExtension` and `installAntigravityIdeExtension` called `spawnSync` directly on the extension CLI with `--install-extension <payload> --force`. On Windows, `code`-style launchers ship as `.cmd` batch files, which a direct `spawnSync` cannot execute, as the commit's code comment explains.

## Design

A new module, `src/core/extensionCli.ts`, owns the process invocation. `extensionCliInvocation(cli, args, targetPlatform, commandProcessor)` returns a command and argument list: when the target platform is `win32`, it runs the command processor with `/d /c <cli> <args…>`; on any other platform it runs the CLI directly with the original arguments. The command processor defaults to `ComSpec`, then `COMSPEC`, then plain `cmd.exe`. Each token stays a separate spawn argument; the code comment says this leaves Windows quoting of paths with spaces to Node/Bun.

`runExtensionCli(cli, args)` wraps that and calls `spawnSync` with UTF-8 output, and both existing installers now go through it instead of spawning the CLI themselves.

## Consequences

- When the platform is `win32`, an extension CLI launch goes through the resolved command processor with `/d /c`, including a bare `code` that PATHEXT resolves to `code.cmd`.
- On other platforms the CLI is executed directly with the same arguments.
- The new cases in `tests/vscodeExtension.test.ts` target `extensionCliInvocation` with an explicit command processor, not the `ComSpec` fallback or the two installer call sites.
- CI results for the pushed head were not available when this was written.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`.
- `bun test`: failed (614 pass, 70 fail, Ran 688 tests across 94 files. [309.30s]), run on the submitted content.

**Where to start:** `extensionCliInvocation` in `src/core/extensionCli.ts`, which owns the `win32` branch and the command-processor fallback.

**Feedback wanted:** Since `cmd /c` re-parses the joined command line, could a VSIX path containing `&`, `^` or `%` be misinterpreted, and should the arguments be escaped for cmd?

title: feat(brief): owners rows say where each behavior lives; code cells spell out direction
body:
## Summary

The evidence brief now says **where** each behavior lives, and code cells say **which way** a change went.

**Owners rows** (TOON brief, neighborhood tail, lean review packet lens A)
- Maps each clause of the commit sentence to the one or two changed functions whose changed lines say it.
- Hunks now record the words on each function's changed lines (`fnWords`). A changed doc comment counts toward the definition below it, so the brief can still tell apart several functions defined in one hunk.
- Scoring: words that most functions share count for less, and linked hunks get a bonus. A clause is assigned only when one function clearly leads.
- The section appears only for a change unit where two or more functions own different sentences. It shows at most 5 rows per unit and 6 in total, and never shows call relations.

**Direction in code cells**
- Lines are labeled `added:` / `removed:` instead of bare `+`/`-`. Paired lines show as `was ... -> now ...`.
- When a boolean condition changes, including a condition split across several lines, the cell lists which operands were dropped, kept and added, instead of the bare removed fragments.
- Value fallbacks such as `a || ref` still show as value changes.
- The direction words don't count against the code-cell budget.

**Docs**
- `drafting.md`: take direction from the code cells, and say where a behavior lives using the owners rows.

New tests are in `tests/brief-owners-direction.test.ts`. Expectations in `brief-extras` and `graph-search` were adjusted.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck`: passed.
- `bun run test`: 45 of 46 files passed. In `tests/review-run.test.ts`, 5 tests hit the 5 s test timeout under the parallel runner (the subprocess-heavy `codex exec` tests). Run alone, `bun test tests/review-run.test.ts` passed 17/17. I did not check whether `main` shows the same timeouts under load.
- `test:bundled` / `test:compiled`: not run locally; left to CI, which runs the packaged contracts on every PR.

## Notes

- `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` was **not** rebuilt. The committed bundle dates from `8853328` and is already behind the evidence-graph commits on `main`. Rebuilding it here would bring in all of those changes, not just this one. It should be refreshed in its own commit (`bun run bundle`) before release.

title: Record every check in a chained command, and keep the full merge base
body:
## Summary

Two fixes to the digest that agents write PR descriptions from.

**Every check in a chained command is now recorded.** Agents often run several checks in one shell command, e.g. `bun run bundle; bun x tsc --noEmit && bun test > log; bun scripts/eval-summaries.ts`. Until now the digest recorded only the test run, and gave it every result line from the whole output. So the eval's "57/57 checks pass" showed up under the tests, and the bundle, typecheck and eval looked like they never ran. Agents then wrote PR descriptions saying those checks "were not run" when they had been.

- The new `commandRuns` (`src/digest/build.ts`) returns one run per verification segment, in order. `commandRun` now returns the first of these, so existing callers keep working, and `sessionDigest` records all of them.
- When one command runs several checks, they share one output. Each run keeps only the result lines that match its kind, using the new `KIND_LINE` patterns (test, typecheck, lint, build, eval).
- In a chain, a non-zero exit status doesn't say which check failed. A failure based only on the exit status is now recorded as `unknown` instead of being attributed to every check. A single check that fails is still recorded as `failed`.
- Several test runners in one command still collapse into one listed test run, as before.

**`digest.json` now keeps the full merge-base hash.** It used to store the merge base cut to 12 characters. `tracetoon source --revision base` needs a full hash, so it always failed with "Code evidence must use the prepared base or head revision".

The second commit rebuilds `plugin/skills/tracetoon/dist/tracetoon.mjs` and `build.json` from these sources, as CONTRIBUTING requires.

## Tests

- New test in `tests/evidence.test.ts` covers:
  - a bundle + test + eval chain producing three separate runs, each with only its own result lines
  - a `&&` chain of build, typecheck and test, with each segment's command recorded
  - a failing chain giving `unknown`, while a single failing typecheck still gives `failed`
- `tests/preparation.test.ts` now runs `source --revision base` and checks that it resolves to a 40-character hash.

## Verification

All of these were run locally on Bun 1.3.14:

- `bun run typecheck`: passed
- `bun run bundle` then `bun run build:check`: passed
- `bun run test`: 36 source test files passed, 0 failed

`bun run test:bundled` and `bun run test:compiled` were not run locally. They are left to CI, which runs the packaged contracts on every PR.

title: Record every check in a chained command, and keep the full merge base
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The purpose of this PR is to give non-test checks in a chained command their own digest entries and keep the full merge base. As the commit message puts it, one shell command often chains several checks (`bun run bundle; bun x tsc --noEmit && bun test > log; bun scripts/eval-summaries.ts`), and agents writing PR descriptions then claimed checks "were not run" when they were. The commit message also says the old digest attached the eval's "57/57 checks pass" to the tests.

Previously `commandRun` returned a single run per command (`{ cmd: verify.seg, kind: verify.kind, ...result }`), and `buildFullDigest` stored the merge base cut with `slice(0, 12)`.

**Design.** A new `commandRuns` returns the verification runs it finds in one command, in order; `commandRun` now calls it and returns the first. `commandRuns` emits one entry per non-test check segment, while several test segments in one command collapse into a single test entry whose `cmd` joins them with ` ; ` and whose outcome is set to `unknown`. If `commandRuns` finds more than one entry in a command, it filters the shared output per entry with that kind's `KIND_LINE` pattern, and a non-zero exit status no longer decides an entry's outcome (it becomes `unknown`). In `sessionDigest`, each run returned by `commandRuns` is pushed, instead of one optional run. `buildFullDigest` now writes the full `mergeBase` instead of a 12-character slice; the commit message says the digest now keeps the full hash, and that the truncated value made `tracetoon source --revision base` fail because it requires a full hash.

**Consequences.** A new test in tests/evidence.test.ts covers a captured release-check chain (bundle, tests into a log, then the eval), and tests/preparation.test.ts was updated for the full hash. The session pushed the branch; CI results for this head are not in the session logs.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (Source test files: 36 passed, 0 failed (up to 4 fresh processes)).

Where to start: `commandRuns` in src/digest/build.ts, which splits a chained command into per-check runs and filters each run's result lines.

Feedback wanted: is downgrading exit-status failures to `unknown` in multi-check chains the right trade-off, or should the last segment of a `&&` chain keep its failure?

title: test/ci: guard against Bun processes that never exit on Windows
body:
Windows CI jobs have been hanging. Each time it was a different test file, and some runs hung for up to 6 hours. The cause is Bun 1.3.14 on Windows: after a CLI process or a `bun test` run has printed its full result, the process sometimes doesn't exit. Any `spawnSync` waiting on it then blocks indefinitely. This PR stops these hangs from stalling CI and adds an explicit exit to the CLI.

## Changes

**CLI**
- `src/cli.ts` now flushes stdout/stderr and calls `process.exit` with the command's exit code. It no longer relies on the process exiting naturally.
- When `$TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` is set, the CLI writes its exit code to that file just before exiting. It also removes the variable from its own environment so child processes don't inherit it.

**Test harness**
- `tests/spawn-guard.ts` runs a command with inherited stdio. If the exit file appears and the process is still running 3s later, the guard kills it and returns the recorded exit code. Commands that exit normally, or that never finish, behave as before.
- `tests/helpers.ts` is preloaded for every test file. It mocks `node:child_process` so that `spawnSync(bun, [cli.ts | tracetoon.mjs, ...])` goes through the guard. This covers all eight test files that spawn the CLI, plus the helper in `graph.test.ts`.
- `review-run` and `review-lean` tests cap each CLI call at 180s and report the command and its partial output if it times out. Their output goes to files instead of pipes, because on Windows a piped `spawnSync` also waits for any child process that still holds the pipe. `TRACETOON_REVIEW_TIMEOUT_MS=60000` means a hung fake reviewer is killed after 1 minute rather than 15.
- The per-test timeout goes from 30s to 120s. One CLI call takes about 10s on the Windows runner, and a single test can make several.

**Test runner / CI**
- `scripts/test-files.ts` kills any test file that runs longer than 15 minutes (`TRACETOON_TEST_FILE_TIMEOUT_MS`), along with its process tree. It prints the output collected so far and marks the file as failed, so the log shows the last test that ran.
- Once a file's `Ran N tests` summary appears, the runner gives `bun` 20s to exit. After that it kills the process and takes the result from the summary's fail/error counts. The killed process's pipes are destroyed and unref'd so they can't keep the runner alive. `test-source` and `test-packaged` exit explicitly once their output is flushed.
- The CI test job now has a 45-minute limit instead of GitHub's 6-hour default.
- The bundle and `build.json` are regenerated from the merged source.

Note: this branch includes a merge of upstream `main` (#52, #53, #55). If the base already contains those, the diff against it will only show the watchdog and guard work above.

## Testing (Linux, Bun 1.3.14)
- `bun run typecheck`: passed
- `bun run test`: 49 of 49 source test files passed, including new `spawn-guard.test.ts` and `test-files.test.ts`
- `bun run test:bundled`: passed, with 14 packaged contracts verified against the shipped bundle
- `bun run build:check`: the build-identity check passed, then the command stopped because the bundle receipt (`dist/*.build.json`) is gitignored and only `bun run bundle` creates it. CI runs `bundle` before `build:check`, so I didn't run that full sequence locally.
- I couldn't test on Windows here, where the hangs actually happen. The Windows CI job is the real test.

title: Stop tests hanging on a Bun that will not exit; target one repo for gh calls
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
This PR asks whether issue 52 is fixed and finishes the fix: gh calls must target one repository, also from a fork. It also stops Windows CI jobs from hanging for hours on a Bun that does not exit.

**Hung test runs.** Commit f17a0924eef1 says Windows runs hung three times, each time in a different test file, and printed nothing until the job was cancelled. Per commit fd4c9f7b30d5, earlier hangs hit a different file each time and CLI processes that had printed their whole result. Per commit 9af69e8f453c, CLI processes that printed their result and never exited keep appearing in new test files. Previously the runner waited for each file's close event with no limit, and bun's per-test timeout cannot interrupt tests that block in spawnSync. The runner now kills a file after 15 minutes (its whole process tree on Windows, the child alone elsewhere), and the CI test job has a 45-minute limit. Once a file's summary line appears, the runner waits 20s for bun to exit, then kills it and takes the result from the summary's fail and error counts. A killed child's pipes are destroyed and unref'd, and test-source and test-packaged exit explicitly. Per commit 9da90dccfd02, `tracetoon review import` printed its result on Windows CI and then did not exit, because the entry point relied on a natural exit. The earlier whole-file hangs look like the same thing. The CLI now flushes its output and calls `process.exit`. When `TRACETOON_EXIT_FILE` is set, it writes its exit code to that file first, after clearing the variable from its own environment so child processes never inherit it. `tests/spawn-guard.ts` kills a process that is still alive 3s after the exit file appears and returns the recorded code. Per commit 9af69e8f453c, the guard leaves commands that exit by themselves, or never finish, as before. `tests/helpers.ts` sends spawnSync calls that run `cli.ts` or `tracetoon.mjs` through this guard.

Per commit 2fe71a320c8c, the watchdog caught review-run stalled for 15 minutes on Windows; product timeouts for a real reviewer are 15 minutes, and the tests' spawnSync had none. Review-run and review-lean CLI calls are now capped, and an error names the command. Per commit 2fe71a320c8c, a hung fake codex is killed after a minute. With piped output, spawnSync on Windows waits for every holder of the pipe, so these calls redirect to files. A call that timed out with its whole JSON result counts as finished. The per-test timeout is now a 120s `--timeout` flag in the runner, since bunfig's setting never took effect. Real hangs are bounded by the watchdog and the spawn caps. The runner guards are tested with fake processes.

**One target repo.** The target is gh's default repo when that repo is a remote of this clone, and origin otherwise; a default that matches no remote is ignored when a GitHub origin exists. `prTruth` resolves it. PR, title-rule and recent-comic lookups pass it with `--repo`, and the `gh repo view` calls name it directly. Doctor checks push access on origin. Comic hosting still pushes to origin; the private-repo check uses the target. Render records the target and its preview prints `PR target: …`; when the approval recorded a target, publish refuses if it changed. From a fork, `gh pr create` gets `--head owner:branch`, and the existing-PR lookup keeps only PRs whose head lives in that fork; this was found while publishing from a fork. Receipts are read whenever a run has any; receipt summaries prefer a wrapper's total over per-file lines; the environment identity ignores temp and terminal variables. tests/target.test.ts covers the target choice, offline mode and fork head, using a fork clone with stubbed gh.

The merged-list test no longer depends on reviewer finish order; the bundle was rebuilt. The CI results in the logs are for an earlier commit, not head 9af69e8f453c.

## Validation

<sub>From runs on the submitted content.</sub>

- Checks passed on the submitted content: `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (Source test files: 49 passed, 0 failed (up to 4 fresh processes)).
- `bun run build:check`: failed, run on the submitted content.

Where to start: `publishImpl` in src/commands/publish.ts (fork `--head` and target refusal), then `resolveTarget` in src/github/target.ts.

Feedback wanted: is the 20s post-summary grace long enough on slow Windows runners?

title: Add an evidence graph of how each PR was made, queryable by agents
body:
## Summary

Each digest now also builds an **evidence graph** (`evidence-graph.json`) showing how the PR was made. It links each prompt to the edits made in its turn, each edit to the diff hunks its lines survive in, each run to the PR files edited after it, and each commit to the session that made it. Agents ask the graph questions with the new `tracetoon query` command instead of reading every fact and the whole patch.

The graph runs in-process on [cypherlite](https://github.com/neo4j-labs/cypherlite) v0.16.1 compiled to WebAssembly. It adds no native modules and no database file. If the engine can't start, the digest is still written, with a note saying the graph is missing.

### What changes

- **`tracetoon query [name] --run <id>`**: the named queries are `outline`, `why <path|path:line|H#|diff:N>`, `verified [path]`, `unverified`, `unexplained`, `turn <S#>`, `stale <R#>`, `dead-ends`, `pushback` and `schema`. It also accepts read-only `--cypher` (with `--params`). Output is compact TOON, or JSON with `--json`. Sections are capped at 60 rows unless `--all` is given.
- **Digest** (`src/digest/build.ts`): adds per-file facts, the checks run after each file's last edit, and the edits made after each run. Budgeting now keeps what explains the PR instead of the most recent facts.
  - A shell command that chains several checks (`tsc && bun test`, …) is now recorded as one run per check, each keeping only its own result lines. A failing exit status in the chain is no longer blamed on every check.
  - `digest.json` keeps the full merge-base hash (it was cut to 12 characters), so `tracetoon source --revision base` works again.
- **Claims, notes and review**:
  - Stale test claims name the files edited after the run.
  - `evidence-notes.md` gains per-change provenance and embeds the graph outline.
  - The reviewer gets `graphLeads` in `review-input.json`: files no passing check followed, and hunks no captured edit explains.
- **Getting drafters to use the graph**: in prbench comparisons, drafters (Sonnet especially) rarely queried the graph. Fixes:
  - `prepare` now prints a `next` step.
  - `prepare --json` carries a `graphOutline`.
  - `render` adds `graphHint` when no query ran.
  - SKILL.md tells whoever drafts to use the graph as an index, while still reading every behavior hunk and expanding commits that have a message body.
- **`doctor`** reports whether the evidence-graph engine is available.
- **Vendoring**: `plugin/skills/tracetoon/assets/cypherlite.wasm` and `src/graph/vendor/` are pinned by tag, revision and SHA-256 in `build-dependencies.json`.
  - `bun scripts/cypherlite.ts check` verifies the vendored bytes against the pin, and `build-info.ts` runs that check too.
  - `bun scripts/cypherlite.ts rebuild` rebuilds them reproducibly.
- `assetsDir()` moves from `src/comic/raster.ts` to `src/util/assets.ts` so the graph engine can find its wasm too.
- An offline benchmark, `scripts/eval-graph.ts`, reports digest size and fact retention per budget, provenance lookup cost, and timings.
- Docs updated: README, CONTRIBUTING, SKILL.md, `contribution-workflow.md` and `digest-schema.md`.

The last commit regenerates the bundle and `build.json`. The earlier commits had changed source after the bundle was last stamped, so `build:check` reported a stale build identity.

### Review pointers

- `src/graph/build.ts` and `src/graph/queries.ts` hold most of the new logic.
- `src/digest/build.ts` contains the chained-check splitting and the relevance budgeting.
- The vendored files under `src/graph/vendor/` and `cypherlite.wasm` are generated, so don't review them line by line. Their hashes are checked against `build-dependencies.json`.

## Testing

Run locally on Linux with Bun 1.3.14:

- `bun run typecheck`: passed
- `bun run test`: 37 source test files passed, 0 failed. New: `tests/graph.test.ts` and `tests/evidence.test.ts`.
- `bun run build:check`: passed after the rebundle (it failed with a stale build identity before it)
- `bun scripts/cypherlite.ts check`: the 4 vendored files match the v0.16.1 pin
- `bun run test:bundled`: all 14 packaged contracts passed against the shipped bundle
- `bun run test:compiled`: not run locally; left to CI, which runs the packaged contracts on every platform for every PR

title: Add a queryable evidence graph of how each PR was made
body:
<!-- tracetoon:start -->
The purpose of this PR is "a proper feature integration, not just a partial integration, even if it means making architectural changes to tracetoon" of a lightweight graph database. Previously the relationships between sessions, prompts, edits, runs and commits were recomputed in memory from heuristics and then thrown away, and `fitBudget` trimmed with fixed rules.

**Design.** When the engine loads, the digest also builds `evidence-graph.json`: prompts linked to their turn's edits, edits to the hunks their lines survive in, runs to PR files edited after them, commits to their sessions. Per its commit message, the engine runs in-process on cypherlite v0.16.1 compiled to WebAssembly, pinned by hash and rebuilt with scripts/cypherlite.ts, so no native modules are added. `tracetoon query` answers named questions (outline, why, stale and others) or read-only Cypher, as TOON, printing up to 60 rows per section unless `--all` is given; bare `tracetoon query` lists the questions. When the engine cannot start, the digest is still written with a note. `assetsDir` moves to src/util/assets.ts, falling back to the working directory on error, and raster.ts re-exports it; .prettierignore skips src/graph/vendor/. Doctor, packaged contracts, docs and an offline benchmark (scripts/eval-graph.ts) also cover the graph.

**Consequences.** The digest gains per-file checks after the last edit and relevance-aware budgeting; stale test claims name later-edited files; the reviewer gets graph leads, which it treats as places to look, not findings. This PR adds a lean reviewer that reads one packet and reports findings, while Tracetoon writes the review contract itself. references/reviewer-lean.md holds the reviewer's instruction: it may make at most 3 location lookups beyond the packet, report at most 8 findings, and update review-findings.json in one turn during a confirmation round. title: feat(brief): neighborhood evidence layout; render reports each finding once
body:
## Summary

Adds a **neighborhood layout** for the evidence brief, and stops `render` from repeating brief-check findings the writer can't clear.

### Neighborhood brief layout (`5539230`)
The brief can now be laid out as the graph's neighborhoods instead of TOON tables. Set it with `TRACETOON_BRIEF_LAYOUT=neighborhood`, which is the default on this branch. `toon` reproduces the previous brief byte for byte.

- Each change block shows:
  - its requests (full text, once)
  - its commits, with each sentence's hunks (`→ H#`)
  - each changed file, with its hunks, the requests behind them and key changed lines (`- old ⇒ + new`)
- Hunks keep up to 24 key changed lines in the graph (`Hunk.code`). They can be cited as `H#` through a new `hunks` section in `briefParts`, so render checks them.
- Sentence → hunk links are made at hunk level and kept conservative. A sentence links to a hunk when:
  - it names the file
  - it's a list sentence (each part is matched separately)
  - only one code hunk shares words with it
  - otherwise, `describedHunks` scores it, with its tie margin
- The blocks are packed to an evidence budget of 2,112 tokens (`TRACETOON_BRIEF_BUDGET`):
  - headers, requests, sentences and file lines are always included
  - code lines are added greedily, by value per character
  - on big PRs, text is clipped and file lines are compacted to fit

Main code: `src/graph/neighborhood.ts` (new), `src/graph/queries.ts`, `src/graph/build.ts`, `src/graph/layout.ts`. Tests: `tests/neighborhood.test.ts`.

### Render: report each finding once (`48a90d7`)
Codex graph-arm drafts ran up to 44 renders because render kept repeating findings the writer couldn't clear. For example, a sentence that attributed a result to the commit message was flagged as a run claim 18 times. The goal request and change rows were also reported as uncovered dozens of times.

- If an earlier render already reported a finding, render now lists it under "repeated" and doesn't block on it.
- A sentence tagged with the commit message, or naming it, is no longer treated as a run claim.

Tests: `tests/render-loops.test.ts`.

The skill references (`quick-path.md`, `contribution-workflow.md`) and the bundled `dist/tracetoon.mjs` are updated to match.

## Validation
- `bun run typecheck`: passed
- `bun run test`: 39 source test files passed, 0 failed (Bun 1.3.14, Linux)
